title: After the Mad Tyrant's Rebirth, She Was Taken by Force
author: Qiong Yu
synopsis:
They say the reigning emperor is cold and ruthless, his moods as unpredictable as the wind, rarely gracing the inner palace with his presence — until the fourth daughter of the Xi family entered the court.

To say that among three thousand women in the harem, he favored only her alone would not be an exaggeration.

He bestowed upon her the character *Chen*, then granted her Chenqian Palace — the grandest and closest to his own quarters. Within a mere half year, she rose from the rank of Zhaoyi to the head of the Four Consorts.

He even had honeydew melons transported from two thousand li away, delivered to her door each and every day — all because she was fond of them.

All of it, just to coax a smile from his beauty.

Yet no one knew that this same Consort Chen, she who reigned supreme in the inner palace, would one day be found huddled in the corner of a resplendent golden hall, tears blurring her vision, watching with frightened eyes as a figure draped in shadow slowly approached.

The faint clinking of iron chains drifted through the air.

The tall man clad in imperial yellow knelt on one knee before Xi Rongyan

chapters.title: Spring Dream
chapters.content:
"Rongyan, does it feel good?"

Under the dim canopy, the warm light beyond the gauze curtains blurred Xi Rongyan’s gaze.

Inside the warm bed, the sweet, cloying scent made her body burn, and she instinctively leaned toward the scorching, towering figure before her.

She heard her own unfamiliar, breathy gasps, her fingers clutching tightly at the man’s white lapels, her body aching unbearably.

Through the hazy, misty bed curtains, she couldn’t see the man’s face clearly.

Tears blurred her vision as she felt the discomfort in her body, and the man’s deep, husky laughter reached her ears before he pulled her tightly into his embrace.

His large hand traced her tear-streaked cheek, then lingered on her damp back.

She saw his deep, desire-filled eyes fixed on her as he sighed softly, "Rongyan, we’ll have a child soon."

"You’ll soon forget him."

"You can only be mine."

His scorching palm lifted her limp body, giving her a painful pleasure.

---

Xi Rongyan woke from the bed, staring blankly at the familiar canopy for a long time.

The scene from her dream felt so real it almost deceived her.

As if she were still in that warm, intimate bed, enveloped in ambiguity.

It wasn’t until reality slowly settled in that she propped herself up.

Who was the man in her dream?

And those dangerous, icy eyes...

She touched her cheek, still slightly warm, her heartbeat unsteady.

Her slender white fingers pressed against her forehead, her black hair spilling over the white bedclothes as she slowly exhaled.

A thin layer of sweat had formed on her back.

These days, she kept having such dreams, yet she could never see the man’s face clearly.

Outside the bed curtains, the gauze lamps were lit, and a maid’s voice came from beyond the curtains. Xi Rongyan softly responded, and the curtain was lifted.

Soft, warm light filtered in. Baozhu saw Xi Rongyan’s hibiscus-like face, her eyes glistening as if filled with water, her fair cheeks flushed, even her forehead dotted with fine sweat.

A few long strands of hair clung to her damp cheeks, exuding a bewitching allure, but it startled Baozhu.

Outside, a light rain still fell. She quickly turned and ordered the maids to close the slightly ajar window, then looked at Xi Rongyan with concern: "Miss, have you caught a chill again?"

It was early spring, still carrying a lingering cold, and it had been raining for two days.

Moreover, Miss had been heartbroken over Young Master Gu’s passing, crying for days, and had been in low spirits ever since.

Perhaps she hadn’t noticed and caught a chill.

But Xi Rongyan shook her head, murmuring, "I just had a dream."

She sat up on the edge of the bed, staring at the carpet, lost in thought for a moment.

She had also dreamed of him being forced to kneel on the carpet by that man...

Xi Rongyan’s face paled slightly, her cool fingers pressing against her burning cheek, feeling at a loss.

She didn’t understand why she kept having such dreams.

After all, she had never even read those vulgar novels, let alone seen a man’s body.

How could this be?

Baozhu watched as Xi Rongyan lowered her head, covering her face, her hair cascading over her shoulders. Unable to help herself, she asked worriedly, "Miss, what’s wrong?"

"Should I call a physician?"

Xi Rongyan shook her head. Only when the last trace of heat faded from her cheeks did she softly say, "Help me dress. I need to visit Mother first."

Only then did Baozhu call Hua Shan to help Xi Rongyan dress.

Sitting in front of the dressing table, Xi Rongyan looked at her reflection in the bronze mirror, and for a moment, she saw the dazed eyes from her dream.

She took a deep breath and ordered the maid to open the window.

A cool breeze blew in, and as she listened to the patter of rain, watching the camellias sway in the downpour, her heart finally calmed.

She pushed the dream out of her mind.

Once dressed, she went to see her mother.

Her mother had always been in poor health, and these past few days, she had been ill again. Xi Rongyan stood by the bedside, heart aching as she looked at her mother’s haggard face and softly said, "Mother’s illness will get better soon."

Madame Xie leaned against the soft pillow behind her, a jade hairpiece adorning her forehead. Even in illness, the beautiful, elegant woman retained her grace.

Her eyes held worry as she tightly gripped Xi Rongyan’s hand and sighed softly, "Rongyan, my illness will pass with rest. But I’m worried about you."

"With what happened, I’m afraid people with ill intentions will spread rumors about you."

Xi Rongyan knew what her mother was worried about. Lately, there had been whispers outside.

Sometimes, even Xi Rongyan herself wondered if she was truly as cursed as people said.

When Xi Rongyan was three, her father had betrothed her to someone.

He was the eldest grandson of the esteemed and virtuous Grand Tutor Zhang—Zhang Jingsheng.

But when Zhang Jingsheng was six, he accidentally fell into a lake while playing by the pond. By the time the servants found and rescued him, he had already stopped breathing.

Though the incident was later traced to a dispute between the concubines in the household, it left a stain on Xi Rongyan’s reputation.

Later, when Xi Rongyan was ten, another marriage was arranged.

This time, it was to the eldest legitimate son of the prestigious Gu family—Gu Yunyu.

Xi Rongyan and Gu Yunyu could be considered childhood sweethearts.

Her father was a Yellow Gate Attendant in the Ministry of Personnel, and Gu Yunyu’s father was a scholar in the Hanlin Academy. The two men had been close friends since their days at the Imperial Academy, and their families were of equal status.

Her mother and Gu Yunyu’s mother had also been close friends in their youth, and the two families often visited each other.

Young Master Gu was handsome and refined, and two years ago, he had passed the imperial examinations, becoming a judge in Jingzhao Prefecture. His future had been promising.

Most importantly, Gu Yunyu treated Xi Rongyan with great care. Though he had never overstepped boundaries, she could always feel his thoughtfulness.

Xi Rongyan had looked forward to this marriage, her heart filled with joy.

The two families had already set a date, and she was to marry him in May.

But who could have predicted that half a month ago, while Gu Yunyu was out on a spring excursion with a few close friends from the same examination class, they would encounter bandits. In the ensuing struggle, Gu Yunyu was stabbed in the chest and fell, never to wake again.

When Xi Rongyan heard the news, she was devastated, refusing to believe it.

It wasn’t until her father confirmed it that she felt as if her heart had been torn apart.

She remembered the sachet Gu Yunyu had given her during the Qixi Festival, with the words "a lifetime together" embroidered inside. The thought of it now felt like her heart was being carved out.

For days, she couldn’t understand—why had she been so joyfully awaiting marriage, only to be met with such tragedy?

Gu Yunyu was such a good man. Why did this have to happen to him?

Even if the bandits were caught and executed, who could bring Gu Yunyu back to life?

Xi Rongyan still felt the pain acutely, her eyes reddening.

She looked at her mother, her voice hoarse. "What others say is their business. I don’t care."

"Even if I never marry, I only wish to stay by Mother’s side."

Madame Xie looked at Xi Rongyan’s face and sighed softly. "How can you say such things?"

"Now that those scoundrels outside are spreading rumors that you’re a husband-killer, it’s affecting your prospects. It won’t be easy to arrange another marriage."

"The Empress Dowager has summoned you to the palace. Go and see her. If she can take the initiative to arrange a marriage for you, I’ll be at ease."

---

chapters.title: Encountering the Emperor
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze, her fingers tightening around the embroidered handkerchief as she softly spoke, "Mother, Brother Yunyu just passed away. If the Empress Dowager arranges a marriage for me now, what will others think?"

"They’ll say I’m heartless and unfaithful."

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan closed her eyes briefly and said softly, "Besides, I’m not in a hurry to marry."

Xi Rongyan’s words made sense.

Madame Xie also understood why she said this.

But it wasn’t that Xi Rongyan was in a hurry—it was that her age couldn’t afford to wait.

Originally, Xi Rongyan had come of age last September. Madame Xie had wanted to arrange the marriage sooner, but the master’s chosen date was this May. Now, Xi Rongyan was past fifteen, and if the marriage were delayed until sixteen, she would be considered old.

Even if they arranged the betrothal now, the elaborate process would take time. The earliest she could marry would be by the end of the year.

If it took longer, she wouldn’t be able to marry until next year.

Madame Xie sighed and patted Xi Rongyan’s hand. "Let’s not talk about this now. The Empress Dowager has summoned you to the palace today. Go see her first."

Xi Rongyan nodded and stayed with her mother a while longer before leaving.

As she stepped onto the veranda outside, she saw the fine rain still falling, the dampness tinged with melancholy. She thought of Gu Yunyu again.

She remembered how kind he had been to her.

Then she recalled the scene from two days ago, when Gu Yunyu’s younger sister had run to her, crying and accusing her of causing her brother’s death.

After a long pause, Xi Rongyan lowered her head, opened her umbrella, and stepped into the rain.

Her silver-threaded misty gauze skirt merged into the rain, the hem flashing briefly on the reflection of the bluestone path.

---

Xi Rongyan had visited Empress Dowager’s Cining Palace many times before.

The Empress Dowager was her aunt. When she was young, her father often brought her, her sister, and her elder brother to the palace to pay their respects.

It used to be the Kunning Palace; now it was the Cining Palace.

By now, the light rain had stopped, leaving the stone tiles damp.

She walked carefully along the long palace path. The rules in the palace were stricter than outside, and she maintained her decorum, keeping her head slightly lowered the entire way, not daring to make the slightest mistake.

As she passed two palace maids, she caught them glancing at her and whispering out of the corner of her eye.

She couldn’t help but tighten her grip. Had the rumors outside already spread into the palace?

Suddenly, the eunuch leading the way to Cining Palace stopped and turned to Xi Rongyan, whispering, "Fourth Young Lady, His Majesty is coming."

Xi Rongyan had encountered the Emperor before during her palace visits. She steadied her heart, adhered to etiquette, and stopped in her tracks, bowing to the Emperor’s sedan chair as it passed.

As the procession passed before her, Xi Rongyan’s heart still tightened slightly.

She hoped it would pass quickly.

She recalled an incident from two years ago when she had entered the palace and happened to see eunuchs carrying a body wrapped in white cloth. The white cloth was stained with splashes of blood, and the pale fingertips exposed outside were still dripping.

The eunuch had recognized the senior palace maid beside Xi Rongyan as someone from the Empress Dowager’s palace and came over to greet them. The senior maid casually asked, only to learn that the person under the white cloth was a newly entered palace beauty who had offended the Emperor’s taboos and was beaten to death.

At that time, everyone around her had remained calm, as if it were nothing more than an ordinary death.

The senior maid beside her had merely nodded, as if it were the most commonplace thing.

Xi Rongyan had stared at the bloodstained white cloth in a daze and had a nightmare that night.

Since then, she had harbored a fear of the Emperor.

She didn’t know what kind of taboo could lead to someone being beaten to death.

But the procession in front of her suddenly stopped. Xi Rongyan only saw a pair of black boots embroidered with golden dragons in front of her. Her fingers nervously tightened around the embroidered handkerchief in her hand, and she quickly performed a half-kneeling bow. "This subject greets His Majesty."

Wei Qi looked down at Xi Rongyan’s slender fingers, tightly clenched in anxiety. His gaze swept over her delicate nose and then settled on the green jade earrings swaying beside her cheeks.

They trembled uneasily.

Wei Qi’s eyes darkened. She was still this afraid of him.

Watching her long lashes flutter, just like in his past life, when she would restlessly try to pull away from his embrace.

Seeing her again, the emotion of losing and regaining her made his feelings tense, making him want to lock this woman even tighter by his side.

His hand unconsciously rose, wanting to touch her, but then he remembered—at this time, Xi Rongyan was still an unmarried noble lady.

The Empress Dowager would arrange another suitable marriage for her.

She would have a husband who cherished her deeply.

At this moment, she feared him.

She kept her distance from him.

Sure enough, before his fingers could touch her cheek, he saw Xi Rongyan’s anxious, fearful eyes looking up at him.

Just like in his past life, she always looked at him with that kind of frightened expression.

And she even took a small step back.

Wei Qi suppressed the dark displeasure rising in his heart, forcing a smile as he withdrew his hand. "Sister Rong, are you going to the Empress Dowager’s?"

Xi Rongyan heard the Emperor address her so familiarly and felt a flicker of unease.

Though the Empress Dowager was her aunt, the Emperor was not the Empress Dowager’s son. She and the current Emperor had only met a few times.

Although she often visited the palace to accompany the Empress Dowager, the only royal she was familiar with was the former Crown Prince. She wasn’t close with the other princes, let alone the Emperor.

She didn’t consider herself on familiar terms with the Emperor, so his address unsettled her.

She lowered her head even more respectfully, not daring to look up.

Wei Qi nodded. "Then Sister Rong, you may go."

Xi Rongyan felt an inexplicable relief under Wei Qi’s towering presence and quickly took her leave, turning away.

But the gaze on her back felt like needles, and she clenched her hands, her palms sweating.

Wei Qi stood with his hands behind his back, silently watching Xi Rongyan’s proper and cautious retreating figure.

She had always been the epitome of a noble lady—her demeanor impeccable, never making a mistake.

She was reserved, conservative, and approachable.

And a little timid, always following the rules.

Even in his past life, after her husband died, she would rather cling to his cold spirit tablet than remarry to him.

He pressed his lips together, the last trace of warmth fading from his cold expression.

High Eunuch Gao bent over and whispered beside Wei Qi, "Your Majesty, how should we handle these two?"

Wei Qi’s icy gaze swept over the two palace maids kneeling on the ground, their mouths gagged. He casually delivered a cruel sentence: "Fifty strokes."

Then he turned and boarded his sedan chair again.

The two palace maids on the ground trembled violently, repeatedly kowtowing and pleading for mercy. Fifty strokes would take their lives.

High Eunuch Gao, fearing their cries would disturb Xi Rongyan ahead, quickly ordered them to be dragged away.

He looked at the bloodstains on the ground from their kowtows and couldn’t help but sigh.

They only had themselves to blame for their loose tongues, gossiping about the Fourth Young Lady of the Xi family. They had thrown their lives away for nothing.

His Majesty had never been a merciful master.

chapters.title: Do You Wish to Enter the Palace?
chapters.content:
As soon as Xi Rongyan entered the Cining Palace, the Empress Dowager beckoned her with a smile. "Rongyan, come sit beside me."

Only then did a smile appear on Xi Rongyan's face as she obediently sat down next to the Empress Dowager.

The Empress Dowager took Xi Rongyan's hand, examining her face carefully before sighing. "You look thinner. Are you grieving over the Gu family's affairs?"

"Or is it because of those rumors outside?"

Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze and softly admitted, "Those rumors outside are indeed painful to hear, and I am truly heartbroken over the Gu family's matters."

She paused, then added quietly, "A gentleman as kind as Brother Yunyu did not deserve such a fate."

"Perhaps it is truly my fault for bringing him misfortune."

The Empress Dowager frowned upon hearing this. "How could you believe such nonsense?"

"When you were born, the master calculated your fortune—it was excellent. How could you be cursed in marriage?"

As she spoke, the Empress Dowager patted Xi Rongyan's hand. "Do not worry about marriage. I will find a good match for you."

Then, with a smile, she asked, "Or do you have someone in mind?"

Xi Rongyan felt that it would be too heartless to start discussing another marriage so soon after her fiancé's misfortune. She herself was also in pain.

She looked up at the Empress Dowager. "Aunt, let us delay the engagement for now. I am not in a hurry."

The Empress Dowager, with her well-maintained hands, gently touched Xi Rongyan's delicate skin and sighed. "Rongyan, how can marriage be delayed?"

Xi Rongyan silently clenched the embroidered handkerchief in her hand, the floral butterfly pattern distorted under her slender fingertips.

Then, the Empress Dowager's soft voice reached her ears. "The eldest grandson of the Xuanyi Marquis, Ren Ziqi, is just the right age for you—three years older. He passed the imperial examination last year as the third-ranked scholar and now serves in the Hanlin Academy."

"I hear he is of upright character, gentle and courteous. The Xuanyi Marquis's family is known for its integrity. Though the elders are not particularly distinguished, the younger generation is promising, and Ren Ziqi is the most outstanding among them."

"You would certainly live a happy life with him."

The Empress Dowager smiled again. "And his appearance is exceptionally handsome. When he paraded through the streets as the third-ranked scholar, how many young ladies lost their hearts to him?"

"You would surely like him too."

Xi Rongyan felt that many things were beyond her control. She had never had a say in her own marriages.

Both engagements had been arranged by her father for the sake of the family, without ever considering her own wishes.

She could not argue with her aunt, so she softly spoke, "Aunt, could you let me think about it a little longer?"

"I do not wish to finalize the engagement so soon. At least wait three months, until the talk about the Gu family has died down."

The Empress Dowager understood Xi Rongyan's meaning. She patted her hand, her gaze filled with pity. "I watched you grow up. You have always been obedient and kind. I know you have a good heart. The people outside do not understand you, but I do."

"Even a small bird's death would sadden you, let alone a person."

"The Gu family's boy was indeed good to you. You two were a suitable match, but it was simply a matter of shallow fate. There was no other reason."

"Do not think too much about it."

As she spoke, she looked at Xi Rongyan's face—her dark hair like clouds, her plain jade hairpins inserted horizontally, the jade color shimmering. With her fair skin, red lips, and white teeth, she was naturally a beauty of extraordinary grace.

No matter whom she married in the future, with her appearance, figure, skin, and her considerate and gentle nature, she would surely be cherished by her husband and live a smooth and happy life.

It was a pity that both engagements had not gone well.

With a sigh, she softly added, "After the Gu family's incident, your father and I discussed whether to let you enter the palace. After all, with the rumors outside, arranging a marriage would indeed be difficult."

"But I did not agree at the time."

The Empress Dowager tightened her grip on Xi Rongyan's hand and asked, "Now, I ask you, do you wish to enter the palace?"

"If you do, I can protect you within the palace."

Xi Rongyan was taken aback. Suddenly, the scene of her encounter with the Emperor earlier flashed through her mind.

She had not dared to look up at the Emperor's face, but she could feel the imposing pressure he exuded.

Although the Emperor had spoken gently, unlike the rumors suggested, she inexplicably felt a little afraid of him. So she shook her head. "If I enter the palace, I will not be able to visit home often. I do not wish to enter the palace."

The Empress Dowager nodded, patting Xi Rongyan's hand with a sigh. "Very well."

"I know your nature. You would likely not fare well against the schemes of the women in the harem. You are my most beloved niece, and I will find you a satisfactory marriage."

"I will also summon the Xuanyi Marquis's family to the palace and give them a proper talking-to."

Xi Rongyan's eyes reddened with emotion, and she obediently nodded. "Rongyan will follow Aunt's arrangements."

The Empress Dowager finally nodded in relief and then asked about Xi Rongyan's mother's illness.

The two sat together talking, and before they knew it, it was already noon.

Xi Rongyan stayed until she had finished lunch with the Empress Dowager, then sat and chatted for a while longer before leaving.

As she exited the Cining Palace and walked along the palace path again, the sky was slightly overcast.

The weather in the third month was still chilly. The cold wind seeped in through her collar, and Xi Rongyan felt a slight chill. The fingers she had left outside were cold and stiff.

Her mind began to wander, thinking about how she would hold a hand warmer when she returned, sit by the stove to read a book, and then drink a cup of hot tea.

But today, for some reason, as she walked halfway, a palace maid carrying a bucket of water rushed out from one of the halls, and the icy water splashed directly onto Xi Rongyan's clothes.

Her dark green dress was soaked, the fabric clinging to her skin.

The elder maid leading Xi Rongyan immediately stepped in front of her, her expression stern. "Which palace are you from, and who is your supervising maid?"

The pale-faced palace maid knelt on the ground, trembling so much that she seemed unable to speak.

Xi Rongyan saw that the girl was so frightened and, although she was cold, thought that she would soon be out of the palace and in the carriage, so she did not want to make things difficult for the young maid.

The bucket of water was large, and the maid was so thin and small—she must have had a hard time.

She softly said to the elder maid beside her, "It is nothing. It is only my skirt that is wet. It is no big deal. Let us go on ahead."

Before she could finish, another figure in deep blue approached quickly and stood before Xi Rongyan. "Are you the Fourth Young Lady of the Xi family?"

Then he kicked the kneeling palace maid and politely said to Xi Rongyan, "This palace maid is from Baohua Hall. The Emperor ordered her to clean this palace for storing books. I came to check if the cleaning was done, but I did not expect to see this servant bump into Fourth Young Lady Xi."

"She has offended a noble lady, but it is up to the Fourth Young Lady to decide her punishment."

Xi Rongyan recognized the eunuch before her as Gao Yi, the Emperor's close attendant. Not wanting to make things difficult, she softly replied, "It is not really her fault. I did not see her coming either. Please, High Eunuch Gao, let her off."

Gao Yi could not help but smile at Xi Rongyan. "Fourth Young Lady Xi is kind and benevolent. The Emperor is also a kind and benevolent man who never punishes his subordinates. It seems you share the Emperor's sentiments."

Then he said to the kneeling maid, "Hurry up, get up, change your clothes, and go back to work."

Xi Rongyan sighed in relief. She had heard that the Emperor was unpredictable, stern, and cold, but she had not expected him to be so lenient with his subordinates.

Now that the matter was settled, she wanted to take her leave from Gao Yi. But Gao Yi said, "Fourth Young Lady, follow me to the front hall to change your clothes. It is not far."

Xi Rongyan hastily declined, "Thank you for your kindness, High Eunuch Gao, but I am only a little wet. It is no trouble."

She was about to leave when Gao Yi, looking distressed, blocked her way. "The Emperor is a man of great virtue and kindness. Fourth Young Lady, as the Empress Dowager's beloved niece, if the Emperor were to learn that you encountered such a thing in the palace and were allowed to leave like this, he would surely feel uneasy and be ashamed to face the Empress Dowager."

"We, the servants, would also find it hard to sleep or eat."

Xi Rongyan had thought it was a small matter, but Gao Yi made it sound so serious. She quickly said, "I will not mention this to the Empress Dowager. Do not worry, High Eunuch Gao."

Gao Yi looked distressed. "Even if Fourth Young Lady does not mention it, we servants still feel guilty. The Emperor will also find out."

As he spoke, Gao Yi was about to perform a grand bow to Xi Rongyan. "Please, Fourth Young Lady, do not make things difficult for us."

Gao Yi was the Emperor's personal eunuch. How could Xi Rongyan allow him to bow to her? She quickly stopped him. "Since it is your kind intention, I accept."

Then she said to the elder maid beside her, "Auntie, go and inform the Empress Dowager. I will change my clothes and leave."

The elder maid glanced at Gao Yi, then politely said to him, "After Fourth Young Lady has changed her clothes and left safely, please send someone to inform us."

Gao Yi quickly smiled. "Do not worry. We will not neglect Fourth Young Lady."

Only then did the elder maid leave with peace of mind.

Xi Rongyan followed Gao Yi forward. Indeed, it was only a few steps away.

But as Xi Rongyan looked up at the name of the hall, Baohua Hall, she suddenly remembered that Gao Yi had said the palace maid was from Baohua Hall, and he had come from Baohua Hall. Did that mean the Emperor was also in Baohua Hall?

---

chapters.title: Bumping Into the Emperor
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan's heart raced. She wanted to ask Gao Yi, but he had already disappeared in a flash. She turned her head, and the palace maid behind her urged, "Fourth Young Lady Xi, please go inside. High Eunuch Gao has gone to order someone to bring you clothes."

Xi Rongyan saw the maid's urgency and looked down at her own clothes, which were more than half soaked. In the cold spring chill, she was indeed very cold, so she went inside.

Inside the hall, a palace maid led Xi Rongyan into a room and asked her to wait for a while.

The room had a charcoal brazier, which made it much warmer.

But why was the charcoal fire lit here alone with no one around?

Though she was cold and puzzled, she could not help but go to the side of the brazier, sit down, and warm her hands. Then she looked around the room.

Both walls of the room were lined with full bookshelves, filled with books. The room seemed to have a scent of ambergris mixed with the smell of books, which inexplicably made one drowsy.

Outside, it seemed to have started raining again, the fine sand-like sound of rain. She thought that when she returned, her skirt would probably be wet again.

Suddenly, Xi Rongyan was startled again. Why were there no servants in the room, not even her own maid who had followed her? She softly called out, "Baozhu."

Her soft voice echoed in the empty room, with no response.

Only then did she feel a slight panic rising in her heart. She quickly stood up and wanted to go out and look.

She stood up from the chair and walked quickly toward the outside. Perhaps she walked a little too fast, for as soon as she passed the screen, she bumped head-on into someone.

Her body involuntarily stepped back, but her waist was quickly held by a warm and strong hand.

The scent of ambergris lingered around Xi Rongyan's nose. She stared blankly at the golden dragon on the dark robe before her. In a moment of distraction, she looked up and met a pair of deep and concerned eyes.

The warmth at her waist quickly disappeared as the figure stepped back respectfully. A deep voice spoke, "I heard that a palace servant had bumped into Sister Rong. I happened to be here reading, so I came to see."

After speaking, Wei Qi asked in a low voice, "Sister Rong, are you all right?"

Xi Rongyan came back to her senses at Wei Qi's deep voice and quickly paled, curtsying to Wei Qi. "This subject is fine. It was I who bumped into Your Majesty just now. Please forgive me, Your Majesty."

But a pitying sigh came from above her. Xi Rongyan suddenly felt a warmth on her body. When she came to her senses again, she saw a pair of long fingers in front of her chin. A bright yellow robe with embroidered golden dragons was draped over her.

The deep voice was right by her ear, the hot breath seeming to scatter on her face. "You need not be so polite. Be careful not to catch a cold."

The gentle voice inexplicably made her heart flutter. Xi Rongyan resisted the urge to step back and looked up at the Emperor. "Your Majesty is kind, but this subject is of low status and dare not use Your Majesty's belongings."

As she spoke, she began to nervously try to remove the cloak.

But her fingers were quickly pressed down by a large hand. She looked up to meet the Emperor's deep gaze. "It is just a cloak. Would you have me watch you remain wet?"

Xi Rongyan was stunned. Then she saw Wei Qi quickly withdraw his hand and look at her deeply. "Your maid has gone to the Imperial Household Department to get embroidered shoes that fit your feet. Clothes will also be sent soon. You need not worry."

"No one will come in."

With that, Wei Qi took a step back. His gaze did not fall on any other part of Xi Rongyan's body. He turned and walked out.

Xi Rongyan still stood there in a daze. The charcoal fire behind her suddenly crackled, reminding her. She recalled the Emperor's gentle gaze just now, which seemed different from the rumors of his coldness.

She felt at ease and turned to continue waiting.

Soon, a palace maid brought in a set of clothes and shoes.

Xi Rongyan did not see her own maid, so she softly asked, "Is my maid outside?"

The palace maid stood before Xi Rongyan very respectfully and said, "Miss Baozhu fell on the way. High Eunuch Gao had someone take Miss Baozhu to the Imperial Physician's Office to be examined."

Xi Rongyan was startled again and asked, "How did she fall?"

The palace maid shook her head. "Perhaps the road was slippery from the rain, and Miss Baozhu was walking a bit too fast."

Xi Rongyan could only nod and went into the inner room to change clothes, refusing the palace servants' help.

After quickly changing her clothes, she went out, but it was quiet outside.

Her maid had not returned yet. The only one waiting outside was a palace maid with her head lowered.

She stood by the window, watching the sky gradually darken and the rain falling more clearly. Her heart grew increasingly uneasy.

She had delayed too long.

She turned and ordered the palace maid beside her to go to the Imperial Physician's Office to ask about her maid's condition.

The palace maid acknowledged and quickly went out.

The sound of rain hitting the steps outside, the cold air seeping in from outside—she knew it was not good to stay in this hall for too long.

Perhaps she should go to the Imperial Physician's Office to find her maid first, then return together.

With this thought, she asked the palace servant behind her, "Is the Emperor here?"

The palace servant answered very respectfully, "His Majesty is reading inside."

Then she looked up at Xi Rongyan. "Shall Fourth Young Lady be guided?"

Xi Rongyan thought that since the Emperor was here, she should certainly take her leave from him.

So she nodded and followed the palace servant deeper inside.

Baohua Hall was very large, with bookshelves everywhere. When they reached the end, the palace servant stopped outside and softly said to Xi Rongyan, "His Majesty is inside."

Xi Rongyan heard the quietness inside and hesitated whether to go in.

Would it disturb him if she went in now?

While she hesitated, Gao Yi suddenly came out quietly from inside and softly asked Xi Rongyan with a smile, "Does Fourth Young Lady Xi wish to see His Majesty?"

Xi Rongyan saw Gao Yi come out and could only nod. She lowered her voice and asked, "Is it convenient now?"

"If it is convenient, please have High Eunuch Gao announce it."

Gao Yi smiled. "It is convenient. Fourth Young Lady can go in directly."

With that, he stepped aside.

chapters.title: As If Afraid of Me
chapters.content:
This was the first time Xi Rongyan had come to this place, yet it suddenly stirred a familiar yet fearful emotion within her, even making her want to leave for a moment.

She didn’t know why—perhaps it was the dim lighting here, with the only bright spot being the place where the emperor sat at the head of the room.

But even there, the light flickered on and off. Half of the emperor’s face was hidden in the shadows, his tall figure like a dark silhouette, resembling a hunter waiting in the darkness, silently awaiting his prey.

A sudden image flashed in her mind. She stared blankly at the shadow behind the zitan desk, as if she saw herself kneeling on the ground in disheveled clothes, engulfed in flames, begging the lofty figure above to save her.

Her heart pounded, and the fear grew stronger.

High Eunuch Gao whispered beside her, “What’s wrong with Miss Xi?”

Xi Rongyan snapped back to reality and quickly lowered her head, walking forward.

When she was five steps away from the desk, she stopped, bowing respectfully to the emperor in proper etiquette.

Wei Qi, who had been hidden in the shadows, slowly revealed his face under the lamp.

He set down the book in his hands, and the golden crown on his head glinted faintly.

Those sharp, all-seeing eyes now looked at Xi Rongyan as he said softly, “Sister Rong, sit.”

His long fingers pointed to the seat across from him. Though his voice was gentle, it carried an irresistible pressure.

She didn’t dare lift her head, obediently walking over to sit on the cushion before him.

Her hands rested properly on her knees, but her palms were slick with sweat.

Wei Qi poured tea for Xi Rongyan, as if knowing what was on her mind. He spoke slowly, “Your maid sprained her ankle. Imperial Physician Wang is setting it for her.”

“I’ve already sent someone to look after her. Once she’s bandaged, they’ll help her come back to see you.”

As he spoke, Wei Qi’s gaze settled on Xi Rongyan’s lowered brows.

He smiled slightly, pushing the jade porcelain teacup toward her. “Sister Rong seems afraid of me.”

The pale, long fingers in front of her occupied the entire cup. In the dim light, they inexplicably made her tense.

She quickly reached out with both hands to take it, replying formally, “This subject reveres Your Majesty and would not dare overstep.”

But Wei Qi’s fingers already covered the cup, and despite her caution, her fingers still brushed against his.

Her hand trembled uncontrollably, and the tea in the jade cup sloshed, wetting Wei Qi’s fingers.

Xi Rongyan’s face paled. Just as she was about to lift her head and apologize to Wei Qi, she met a pair of deep, dark eyes.

Wei Qi’s appearance was not the kind that exuded warmth. His sword-like brows were sharply angled, his thin lips and long eyes gave him a cold, detached aura. Even when his eyes held a hint of a smile, it still made people feel uneasy.

Her grandmother often said that appearance reflects the heart.

A cold and heartless person must have a cold and aloof appearance.

A kind and gentle person must be as warm as jade.

But Wei Qi clearly did not have a warm appearance.

In truth, Xi Rongyan and Wei Qi had little interaction before. They had only met a few times in the past.

Wei Qi had been enfeoffed as a prince at fifteen and was sent to guard the northern frontier. He only returned when the late emperor suffered a stroke and fell gravely ill.

It was said that during his nearly ten years in the north, his hands were stained with much blood, and his reputation was one of brutality.

It was also said that the late emperor had once summoned Wei Qi alone. On that very day, the late emperor passed away. When Wei Qi and the eunuch by the late emperor’s side emerged, the Grand Eunuch announced the late emperor’s decree: Wei Qi was to be established as the crown prince.

Her father had once described the scene to her. The soldiers Wei Qi had brought back from the north stood guard outside the palace gates, ostensibly to prevent chaos, but it also ensured that none of the court officials dared to object.

Some said Wei Qi had ambitious designs, that he had usurped the throne by patricide.

Though no one dared speak of it openly, such rumors still circulated in private.

Perhaps it was these rumors that had left a mark on Xi Rongyan’s heart, making her feel a hint of fear toward Wei Qi.

At this moment, she knelt before the emperor, holding the cup in her hands, and quickly apologized, “This subject has been discourteous. Please forgive me, Your Majesty.”

Wei Qi silently watched Xi Rongyan kneeling before him.

Her slender nape was fair under the lamp, her gentle brows and eyes lowered, her delicate eyebrows curved like a crescent moon.

The folds of her blue silk skirt shimmered faintly, and her wrists, holding the cup, were raised properly, the wide sleeves hanging halfway down, revealing the jade bracelet on her wrist.

Wei Qi leaned casually against a small table beside him, his long fingers tapping on his raised knee, his scrutinizing gaze never leaving Xi Rongyan.

Her propriety—was actually fear of him.

Wei Qi remained silent, slowly straightening his body. He bent down to support Xi Rongyan’s hand, his voice soft with a hint of regret, “Why must Sister Rong fear me so?”

“Treat me as your cousin. There’s no need for such formality.”

The warm breath was right in front of her, surrounded by the scent of ambergris. She kept her head lowered, still maintaining a respectful posture. “Your Majesty is the Son of Heaven. This subject would not dare overstep.”

If Xi Rongyan had lifted her head at this moment, she would have seen the coldness flickering across Wei Qi’s face.

His thumb brushed against her fingers before quickly letting go. Still in good humor, he chuckled softly, “If Sister Rong insists on being so distant, I won’t force it.”

“You may rise.”

Xi Rongyan’s heart tightened at these words. After expressing her gratitude, she stood up.

She hesitated internally, wondering how she should treat the emperor.

Did the emperor truly wish for someone to be as close to him as family?

Her father and elder brother had said that the emperor was the Son of Heaven, the ruler. Only by always recognizing him as such would one avoid making mistakes.

From a young age, she had strictly followed her father’s teachings. Every time she entered the palace, she had never made a single error.

Even before the empress dowager, she had never taken advantage of favor to act arrogantly, losing her manners or sense of hierarchy.

The hall, filled with bookshelves, was dimly lit. Apart from the bright area where they were, the rest was a blur of shadows.

It felt as if only she and the emperor existed in this space.

The sound of fine rain came from outside the window. Her palms were sweating, and she couldn’t suppress the urge to leave this place that was too dark and made her uneasy.

The emperor across from her spoke first, his deep voice flowing slowly in the silence. “Did the empress dowager discuss your marriage with you?”

Xi Rongyan maintained her composed demeanor and quickly replied respectfully, “She did.”

Wei Qi smiled casually, “Oh?”

As he spoke, his fingers turned a page of the book, as if he were casually reading while idly chatting with her. Then he asked nonchalantly, “Which family does the empress dowager favor?”

Xi Rongyan thought for a moment before answering, “The empress dowager has not yet decided.”

Wei Qi hummed, his gaze falling on Xi Rongyan. “Then which family do you favor?”

Xi Rongyan lowered her eyes. “This subject’s marriage is to be arranged by her father.”

Wei Qi’s lips curled with a cold edge, then he asked lightly, “The Gu family broke off the engagement. Are you heartbroken?”

---

chapters.title: The Emperor Is Different from the Rumors
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan hadn’t expected the emperor to ask her this. Did he also hear about it?

She pondered for a moment before nodding honestly. “Yes, I am.”

Because she truly was.

As soon as she finished speaking, she heard a tearing sound—Wei Qi’s fingertips had torn the page. She looked at him in shock.

Wei Qi glanced at her wide, surprised eyes, his lips pressed with coldness.

He smiled. “Did I startle you?”

Xi Rongyan quickly shook her head.

Wei Qi nodded silently, his long fingers tapping on the desk, saying no more.

A long silence followed.

Outside, the sky had grown very dark. If she didn’t return soon, her family would worry.

Wei Qi took in Xi Rongyan’s uneasy emotions, the shadow in his eyes deepening.

At this moment, a eunuch entered quietly, kneeling before Wei Qi and whispering, “In response to Your Majesty, Young Lady Baozhu has returned.”

Wei Qi swept his gaze over Xi Rongyan’s face, noticing her relieved expression. His eyes turned icy in the dim light.

He waved his hand but still stood up to look at her, his voice remaining gentle. “Sister Rong, let’s go.”

Seeing the emperor stand, Xi Rongyan quickly got up as well. “This subject can return on her own.”

Wei Qi stood before Xi Rongyan, his tall figure casting a shadow over her. He looked down at her fair face and smiled. “It’s fine. I need to leave as well.”

With that, he walked ahead of her, and Xi Rongyan followed closely behind.

In the outer hall, Baozhu, who had been waiting outside, saw Xi Rongyan come out and quickly approached happily. “Young Lady!”

Xi Rongyan asked her, “Is your foot better?”

Baozhu nodded. “It was just a sprain. The imperial physicians pressed it, and it’s fine now.”

Xi Rongyan let out a relieved breath.

Wei Qi stood with his hands behind his back, watching the scene. Then he quietly ordered the person beside him, “Prepare a palanquin.”

Hearing the emperor’s order, Xi Rongyan quickly turned to decline.

Wei Qi looked down at her, his voice gently admonishing, “It’s raining outside, and the palace paths are slippery. Go slowly.”

Wei Qi stood before her, his shadow looming over her, carrying an inexplicable ambiguity.

Xi Rongyan didn’t dare refuse again and quickly agreed.

Guided by High Eunuch Gao to the outside, she saw that a palanquin was already waiting at the hall’s entrance.

It was Xi Rongyan’s first time riding a palanquin inside the palace. She felt a bit uncomfortable, but High Eunuch Gao said it was a rare bestowal from the emperor.

She got in, and four or five palace attendants carrying lanterns walked beside her, slowly moving toward the depths of the palace.

High Yi only completely exhaled after seeing Xi Rongyan safely seated in the palanquin and departing. He turned and returned to Bao Hua Hall.

Wei Qi stood with his hands behind his back by the window, watching the slowly receding light.

Through the fine curtain of rain, the figure illuminated by the lanterns appeared hazy, swaying as if near, then far.

Wei Qi rubbed his thumb ring, his expression growing colder.

High Yi stood behind Wei Qi, softly reporting what Xi Rongyan had said to the empress dowager in Ci Ning Palace.

Wei Qi’s face remained expressionless. When he heard that Xi Rongyan did not wish to enter the palace, the corners of his lips pressed downward.

High Yi cautiously lowered his head again. “The empress dowager also said she favors the second young master of the Xuan Yi Marquis’s residence. The fourth daughter of the Xi family has agreed.”

A cold, oppressive aura spread out. Even High Yi was terrified.

Wei Qi’s cold eyes showed no emotion as he turned and strode out of Bao Hua Hall.

Meanwhile, Xi Rongyan exited the palace gates and saw a tall figure standing by her carriage.

Upon seeing her, the figure quickly came over with an umbrella.

Xi Wenli walked to Xi Rongyan’s side, holding the paper umbrella over her head, and asked with concern, “Why did it take you so long to come out?”

Xi Rongyan walked beside her elder brother toward the carriage, speaking softly, “Today, I stayed a little late talking with Aunt. On the way back in the afternoon, a palace maid accidentally spilled water on me.”

She then gave her elder brother a rough account of what happened afterward.

Inside the carriage, her elder brother had prepared a hand warmer for her. She held it in her hands, warming her fingertips.

Closing her eyes, she thought again of the emperor’s gentle expression today, which was somewhat different from what she had imagined.

She couldn’t help but ask her elder brother beside her, “Does His Majesty have a good temper?”

Xi Wenli looked at his younger sister and sighed helplessly. “Why would you ask that?”

Xi Rongyan lowered her head. In the swaying carriage, her jade hairpin loosened slightly.

She spoke softly, “Today, when I saw His Majesty, he seemed very gentle, not as stern as I thought.”

“He’s different from the rumors.”

Xi Wenli was a secretary in the Secretariat, in charge of the four libraries and their branches. Though he worked in the central government, he didn’t have much involvement in court politics and rarely met the emperor.

However, he was surrounded by sons of noble families with extensive connections. He knew a thing or two about the new emperor, who had been on the throne for three years.

He seriously lowered his voice to Xi Rongyan, “His Majesty is reserved. His true temperament is rarely shown, but he is by no means a gentle man.”

“In the three years since his ascension, he has supported a group of new aristocratic families to maintain the court’s balance. He was once the feudal prince of the north, brutally suppressing the northern barbarian tribes. His hands are stained with countless lives. How could he possibly be gentle?”

“Back then, when the late emperor was gravely ill, the three princes were eyeing the throne, yet in the end, it was His Majesty who ascended.”

“A gentle man could never sit in the position he does now.”

“The emperor’s mind is as deep as the ocean. Do not easily overstep.”

Xi Rongyan listened in surprise, then simply nodded lightly. Her earrings brushed against her face, and she fell silent.

When the carriage stopped, Xi Wenli draped a cloak over Xi Rongyan and said softly, “You go rest first. I’ll go give Mother our regards.”

Xi Rongyan hummed in agreement, adjusting the cloak before turning toward her own courtyard.

After returning to her courtyard, she bathed and sat on the luohan bed with her cat, lost in thought. Suddenly, she asked Baozhu beside her how she had fallen today.

Baozhu was drying Xi Rongyan’s hair with a towel and a warmer. Hearing her mistress’s question, she replied, “This servant doesn’t know either. I was walking when it felt like something hit the back of my heel, and I tumbled down.”

“But the palace maid beside me caught me in time. It hurt so much that I forgot to see what it was.”

Xi Rongyan nodded, then asked, “Are you better now?”

Baozhu smiled. “Much better. The palace’s medicinal plaster is truly effective. After applying one, the pain was gone.”

Xi Rongyan absentmindedly pinched the cat’s ear.

After her hair was dry, she lay on the soft pillow, watching Baozhu tidy the books by the bed. Then she softly said, “I don’t want to get married anymore.”

Baozhu was taken aback by Xi Rongyan’s sudden words. She paused, then looked up to see Xi Rongyan’s dark hair framing her small face, her beautiful eyes dim, her lips parting as she murmured, “Should I not say such things?”

Her voice was very soft. “Actually, I’ve been thinking… Did the Gu young master’s accident really happen because I bring misfortune to my husbands?”

Baozhu, worried that Xi Rongyan was dwelling on painful memories, quickly said, “Young Lady, don’t think like that. It’s not your fault.”

Xi Rongyan pulled the brocade quilt over her face, her fingers clutching the peach blossom hairpin that Gu Wenyu had given her as a betrothal gift. A muffled voice came from under the quilt, “Maybe.”

After a long while, a soft voice came again, “But I still feel terrible.”

“They all say it’s over, but can Brother Wenyu’s sudden accident really be so easily forgotten?”

Baozhu didn’t know how to comfort her, so she silently stayed by her side. When there was no more movement, she carefully lifted the quilt.

The person inside had fallen asleep, her eyes red-rimmed.

Baozhu sighed silently, then put down the curtain and quietly left.

chapters.title: Betrothal
chapters.content:
A few more days passed, and the lingering drizzle finally gave way to a hint of sunshine.

Xi Rongyan sat by the waterside pavilion in the back courtyard, resting her chin on her hand as she watched the fish, lost in thought. Soon, a matron from her mother’s side came to summon her to the main courtyard.

Upon arriving at the main courtyard, Madame Xie smiled and had Xi Rongyan pick fabric. "Spring has arrived, and the weather is warmer. Choose a pattern you like, and I’ll have a couple of spring outfits made for you."

As she spoke, she turned to Xi Rongyan with a smile. "In a couple of days, it will be the Flower Festival. You can wear them then, and I’ll take you to meet the Marchioness of Xuanyi."

Xi Rongyan hesitated. "Actually, it wouldn’t matter if we met a little later."

Madame Xie chuckled. "Do you think no matchmakers have approached the Xuanyi Marquis’s household?"

"I’ve heard that many families want to form a marriage alliance with the Xuanyi Marquis’s household. The young marquis is noble, refined, and conducts himself with integrity—an excellent choice."

"Yesterday, the Empress Dowager met with your father. She suggested settling the matter soon. If the Xuanyi Marquis’s household finalizes a marriage first, wouldn’t that be a missed opportunity?"

"Ren Ziqi is twenty now—just the right age for betrothal."

"If you’re satisfied, the Empress Dowager will arrange the marriage for you."

Xi Rongyan had wanted to say it wouldn’t matter if the opportunity passed, but seeing the lingering traces of illness on her mother’s face and the worry in her eyes, she swallowed her words and obediently nodded.

She casually pointed to a bolt of lotus-white orchid-patterned rainflower brocade.

Madame Xie smiled. "You suit subtle colors. That’s fine."

She then ordered someone to make the dress.

On the day of the Flower Festival, Xi Rongyan and her mother boarded a carriage together.

On the Flower Festival, the imperial garden, Xiuyuan, would be open to the public. Noblewomen from official families would gather there, and the Empress would preside over the event.

There were many activities: drinking hundred-flower wine, wearing flower crowns, chasing butterflies, and feasting on floral banquets.

In the past, Xi Rongyan had attended every year, but last year she had missed it due to a cold.

The garden was vast, filled with women. Peach blossoms were in full bloom, and petals covered the ground. Elegantly dressed young ladies in groups of three or five chased butterflies, their laughter filling the air.

As soon as Xi Rongyan arrived, all eyes turned to her, and whispers followed.

Some were schadenfreude, some were mocking, and others were pitying.

Xi Rongyan tightened her grip on her mountain hibiscus fan, carefully following her mother’s steps.

Madame Xie had a prior acquaintance with the Xuanyi Marquis’s household, so she took Xi Rongyan to the gazebo where the Marchioness of Xuanyi, Madame Lin, was seated.

The Empress Dowager had not yet issued an imperial decree, nor had she summoned the Xuanyi Marquis’s household. Madame Xie simply wanted to gauge their intentions first.

From a distance, Wei Qi stood on a balcony, watching Madame Xie lead Xi Rongyan to the gazebo where she sat and chatted with Madame Lin. His eyes narrowed dangerously.

A cold, detached smile curled at the corner of his lips before he turned away.

Xi Rongyan turned her head to look outside but saw no sign of the Gu family. A pang of sadness filled her heart.

Her mother, noticing her distraction, pulled her along to exchange pleasantries with Madame Lin of the Xuanyi Marquis’s household. Only then did she snap back to attention.

Madame Lin looked at Xi Rongyan. Her graceful and quiet demeanor made it clear she was a well-educated and refined young lady from a noble family.

She had heard of Xi Rongyan—rumored to be the epitome of a noblewoman. Seeing her in person, she found the reputation well-deserved.

Listening to Xi Rongyan’s voice, soft as falling pearls, and seeing the plain jade hairpin in her hair, paired with her lotus-white half-high crossed-collar skirt, complemented by the lustrous pearls hanging from her ears, she was truly a sight to behold.

Delicate and fair, with a face like flowers veiled in mist.

Madame Lin nodded with a smile. "Everyone outside says the Fourth Young Lady of the Xi family is graceful and refined. Indeed, that is the case."

Madame Xie sighed regretfully. "It’s a pity her marriage prospects have been unlucky."

"And then there are the idle rumors."

Madame Lin looked at Madame Xie. "None of that matters. I don’t believe those things."

"Those rumors about bringing misfortune to her husband—those are hardly credible."

Madame Xie’s eyes lit up, though she still seemed troubled. "Sister, you are truly reasonable."

Madame Lin smiled. "It’s not about being reasonable or not. While others pray to Buddha for fate, I have never done so."

"Fate is in one’s own hands. I’ve saved many people myself."

"Even those at death’s door. Fate is not predetermined."

Madame Xie was taken aback.

She then remembered that Madame Lin was not from a noble background. In fact, she had once been a female physician.

By a twist of fate, she had saved Lord Ren, the Marquis of Xuanyi, earning his favor. Years ago, she had married into the marquis’s household in a grand ceremony.

Perhaps she truly did not believe in fate.

That was a good thing.

Suddenly, a commotion arose from another direction. A line of palace maids approached, each holding a bamboo slip, distributing them to the women. They announced it was time for the flower game.

The Empress would then select the top three participants, rewarding each one by one. The winner would even receive a flower crown placed on her head by the Empress herself.

This had been a tradition in past years. The woman who received the flower crown could request a reward from the Empress.

Even concubines from the imperial harem could participate, adding to the lively atmosphere.

A palace maid’s tray reached Xi Rongyan. She took a slip, though she had no intention of participating seriously. She hastily wrote something, considering it mere participation.

Given the rumors surrounding her, she didn’t want to draw attention. Naturally, what she wrote would never be selected.

After a while, the winners of the flower game were announced. Those who had participated gathered to watch.

Madame Xie was deep in conversation with Madame Lin, so she told Xi Rongyan to take her maid and go see the excitement for herself.

Xi Rongyan assumed she wouldn’t be selected and had no desire to go. But seeing her maid craning her neck to look, clearly eager to see the spectacle and find out who had won, she finally stood up and led the maid to the back of the crowd.

Over there, the Empress stood on a high platform. A palace maid beside her held a tray containing the winning slips.

One by one, she read out the names of the three winners. Women stepped forward, receiving their rewards amid envious gazes. The first-place winner even had the Empress personally place a flower crown on her head and bestow her blessing.

Normally, the event would end there. But this time, they announced there was an additional reward: a special floral wine bestowed by the Empress herself.

This floral wine was exclusive to the palace, extremely precious. Its production was complex—hundreds of pounds of flowers were needed to make a single pot.

Rumor had it that drinking a cup could dispel impurities, nourish the skin, and leave the body fragrant for days.

This was the first time such a reward had been offered, and all the women present were eagerly anticipating it.

Then, the head matron read out five names in total—and to her surprise, Xi Rongyan’s name was among them.

Xi Rongyan blinked in shock. She never expected to be chosen.

Seeing the others step forward, she had no choice but to harden her resolve and follow.

The matron brought the wine and stood before Xi Rongyan with a smile. "Congratulations, Fourth Young Lady Xi. Your flower slip caught Her Majesty the Empress’s eye. This Hundred-Flower Brew is most nourishing. Even Her Majesty rarely partakes of it."

Xi Rongyan stared at the wine cup in front of her, stunned. She could not drink even a drop of alcohol.

Only those close to her knew this, but she couldn’t refuse the Empress’s gift.

Baozhu and Chunyun, standing behind Xi Rongyan, were worried but didn’t dare intervene.

The other rewarded women had already drunk theirs. Under the watchful eyes of the crowd, Xi Rongyan maintained her composure, gracefully lifting the cup and draining it.

Her movements were poised, without a hint of impropriety.

She then thanked the Empress for the gift.

But as soon as she finished drinking, she began to feel dizzy. She tightly gripped Baozhu’s hand, her body swaying slightly.

The palace maid in front of her noticed Xi Rongyan’s discomfort and said with concern, "The Hundred-Flower Brew is a bit strong. If Miss Xi is feeling unwell, there is a resting place called Qing Shan Ju not far ahead, specially for female guests. Since only women are present today, Miss Xi can rest there without worry."

Xi Rongyan knew she would lose her composure after drinking, so she accepted the palace maid’s suggestion with gratitude.

Under the gaze of the crowd, she knew that if she stayed any longer, she would soon lose her dignity. She quickly had Chunyun go inform her mother, while Baozhu helped her toward Qing Shan Ju.

The effects of the alcohol were already spreading through her body. She exhaled, feeling a slight feverish warmth.

Baozhu knew all too well what Xi Rongyan was like when drunk and didn’t dare delay.

Fortunately, Qing Shan Ju was indeed nearby. As they arrived, Xi Rongyan, clinging to her last shred of clarity, looked up and saw the sign for Qing Shan Ju. Only then did she relax, allowing Baozhu to help her inside.

But Qing Shan Ju was empty. Baozhu had just helped Xi Rongyan onto a couch in one of the rooms when Xi Rongyan, her consciousness already blurred, clung to her and whispered tearfully, "Don’t leave..."

---

chapters.title: I Dreamed of You
chapters.content:
Baozhu had served Xi Rongyan for many years, and what she feared most was when Xi Rongyan drank alcohol.

Even if it was just a little fruit wine on a winter day indoors, she would soon seem like a different person.

She would cling to Baozhu, refusing to let go, and if she didn’t sleep properly, she would wander around, insisting on dragging Baozhu outside to pick flowers—even in the dead of winter.

It would take at least half an hour of chaos before she settled down, and by the time she woke up, she would have forgotten everything.

Later, Xi Rongyan herself became aware of how she behaved when drunk, so even if she craved a taste, she would only have a few sips of rice wine. She never touched fruit wine again.

Just now, when the palace maid mentioned that the Hundred-Flower Brew was strong, Baozhu had no idea how long her mistress would be in this state.

Xi Rongyan, now buried in her arms, was demanding a zither. Baozhu was helpless—where was she supposed to find one at a moment like this?

The woman in her arms was as limp as a boneless ragdoll, almost entirely reliant on Baozhu to support her. Yet she refused to stay still, making it impossible for Baozhu to simply lay her down on the couch. Baozhu was exhausted.

Just then, a noise came from behind. Baozhu turned her head and nearly fainted in terror.

There stood the Emperor, draped in a dark crane robe embroidered with golden dragons. His chest was half-exposed, still dripping with water, as if he had just bathed.

His sharp, cold features exuded an imperial majesty that made her heart tremble. A cold glance from him sent shivers down her spine.

Moreover, the Emperor’s senior eunuch, Gao Gonggong, barked sternly, "His Majesty is resting here! Who dares trespass in the imperial presence?"

Baozhu immediately dropped to her knees, trembling violently.

She stammered an explanation, cold sweat pouring down her forehead.

She couldn’t fathom why the Emperor would be here.

To make matters worse, the young lady in her arms was completely unaware of the situation. Kneeling on the ground, she still tugged at Baozhu, insisting she get up and fetch a zither for her.

Baozhu was so terrified she nearly kowtowed to Xi Rongyan, fearing that if her mistress did something improper in front of the Emperor, it would be a disaster.

Wei Qi’s gaze fell on Xi Rongyan, who was kneeling on the ground, half-buried in Baozhu’s arms.

Her fair face, flushed from the alcohol, peeked through her disheveled hair. Her jade earrings trembled, and her clothes were slightly disheveled.

She mumbled incoherently.

His noble and aloof expression revealed nothing, but Wei Qi took a step forward, approaching the two kneeling figures.

With his hands clasped behind his back, his narrow, elongated eyes lowered as he glanced at Baozhu. His voice remained unreadable. "Drunk?"

Baozhu quickly tightened her hold on Xi Rongyan and nodded repeatedly.

Then, trembling, she kowtowed and pleaded for forgiveness. "It was this slave’s fault for leading the young lady to the wrong place. Please, Your Majesty, spare us."

Wei Qi let out a nasal hum, then said, "Go fetch Madame Xi to take the Fourth Young Lady back."

Baozhu hesitated. "But the young lady is alone here..."

Before she could finish, she felt an icy gaze fall upon her.

She couldn’t describe the feeling, but though no sound was made, it sent a chill through her bones.

She belatedly realized that the Emperor’s dignity brooked no questioning.

Knowing she had misspoken, she quickly kowtowed again in submission.

She reasoned that with the Emperor present, nothing bad should happen.

Baozhu, her voice shaking, tried to soothe Xi Rongyan, fearing she would cause trouble. "Young lady, this slave will go fetch a zither for you. Wait a moment, I’ll be right back."

Xi Rongyan’s vision was already blurred. She only knew her body was burning, and she had no idea where she was. All she could hear was Baozhu’s voice.

She loosened her grip on Baozhu’s sleeve slightly, one fair finger pressing against the floor. A few strands of her black hair, slightly disheveled, hung in front of her forehead. Her voice was hoarse and slurred as she instructed, "Hurry..."

Baozhu didn’t dare delay. Seeing that her mistress was momentarily calmed, she quickly stood up to go find Madame Xi to take her mistress away.

After taking a few steps, she turned back, still worried, and glanced at Xi Rongyan, who was still on the ground. She decided she had to bring Madame Xi here as soon as possible and steeled her heart to turn away.

She rushed out and, almost instinctively, looked up at the sign above the door. When she saw it, she nearly jumped out of her skin—it wasn’t Qing Shan Ju at all. It was Qing Yue Ju.

Where was Qing Shan Ju?

She looked to the side and her heart leapt again. Qing Shan Ju was the pavilion next door.

But she had clearly seen the sign for Qing Shan Ju earlier.

But there was no time to think about it now. Her heart sank as she realized the gravity of her mistake. She hurried to find Madame Xi and deliver the message.

Meanwhile, Gao Gonggong, seeing Baozhu leave, discreetly retreated.

He stood by the window, watching Baozhu’s flustered back as she hurried away. With a subtle gesture, a guard silently followed after her.

Inside the room, Xi Rongyan, her mind hazy as if floating in the clouds, suddenly called out that she wanted to go admire the flowers. She looked up at the dark figure before her, her slender fingers reaching out to grab the hem of Wei Qi’s robe.

Wei Qi had only loosely draped the crane robe over himself. With Xi Rongyan’s tug, half of it slipped off, revealing his robust, muscular chest. The robe covered her hand as the troublemaker stared blankly, lost in confusion.

Wei Qi lowered his gaze, staring deeply into Xi Rongyan’s unfocused, misty eyes beneath her dark brows. His expression remained silent as he bent down and lifted her into his arms.

He held her on his lap, his long, bony fingers tracing inch by inch from her soft waist to her back, allowing the person in his arms to fidget against him.

He lowered his head and pressed his lips to her hair, inhaling her familiar warm fragrance. His dark eyes were unfathomable.

Xi Rongyan’s fair fingers clutched at his wide sleeve, her voice soft and purring like a cat’s. "The peach blossoms are in bloom... I want to pick some to make peach blossom tea..."

Her kitten-like voice made Wei Qi lower his gaze again. He extended a long finger to lift her chin. Her eyes, though, held no recognition of him.

The thumb adorned with a ring brushed over her watery, misty eyes. The blush spread across her face, her delicate brows vibrant. Yet he pressed his lips tightly together, his eyes shadowed.

Only in this state would she willingly approach him.

His fingers tightened involuntarily until the person at his fingertips shifted uncomfortably. Only then did he loosen his grip, pulling her tightly into his arms and gently patting her back. "If you like peach blossoms, I’ll have peach blossom trees planted all around your palace."

"You can have peach blossom tea every year."

Xi Rongyan seemed not to have heard Wei Qi’s words at all. Her fingers scratched at his neck before she suddenly lifted her misty eyes, giggling as if teasing the cat she kept.

The fragrant scent wafted into his nose. Wei Qi looked into Xi Rongyan’s eyes, which were filled with mist, her brows and eyes curved in a smile, exuding the aroma of the Hundred-Flower Brew.

He rarely saw Xi Rongyan smile, and she had never smiled in front of him before.

She was always so afraid of him.

She had even tried every means to escape him.

He slowly leaned down toward her, his dark eyes holding a captivating light as he watched her smile. "Yan’er."

Xi Rongyan heard him. She responded with a confused hum, her fingers suddenly brushing against the face of the man before her.

She slightly tilted her head to look into his eyes, as if they were somehow familiar.

She wrapped her arms around his neck, her beautiful brows half-closed. A jade hairpin fell from her hair, shattering crisply. In a soft, murmuring voice, she said, "I dreamed of you."

Wei Qi’s dark eyes flickered as he looked into Xi Rongyan’s. His hand tightened around her waist as he asked in a low voice, "What did you dream about me?"

Xi Rongyan pouted, as if tilting her head had tired her. She buried her face in Wei Qi’s neck, her voice aggrieved. "You bullied me."

"You always bully me..."

Wei Qi pressed his lips tightly together. The long fingers resting on Xi Rongyan’s waist tightened another degree.

If she had been more obedient, he wouldn’t have felt the need to confine her.

In the past, she had escaped so many times. He had punished her for it, so why did she still try to leave?

The person in his arms continued to fidget, her fingers wandering into his chest and moving downward. Wei Qi took a deep breath and caught her hand.

Xi Rongyan felt uncomfortable and tried to get up from Wei Qi’s lap to pick peach blossoms.

Wei Qi held her in his arms, soothing her. "Wait a moment. I’ll have someone pick a whole basket for you."

Xi Rongyan closed her eyes but insisted on pulling Wei Qi along. However, she couldn’t even stand steadily, her entire body as weak as a pool of spring water.

Wei Qi, fearing she might hurt herself, reached out to hold her. But she ended up pouncing on him instead.

Her fragrance enveloped him completely. He watched as her misty eyes opened slightly, her red lips parting as she said, "So hot..."

Unable to resist his body’s desire for her any longer, he leaned in and kissed her lips.

Breathing heavily, he asked, unable to control himself, "Yan’er, who am I?"

Xi Rongyan only let out a couple of confused whimpers. Her unfocused eyes clearly told Wei Qi that the person in his arms did not recognize him.

Wei Qi’s eyes darkened further. He carried her to the couch and pinned her beneath him, kissing her punishingly.

Xi Rongyan only felt her lips being crushed painfully. Tears welled in the corners of her eyes as she instinctively placed her hands on Wei Qi’s broad back.

chapters.title: Issuing the Decree
chapters.content:
Madam Xie had just been having a pleasant conversation with the Marquis of Xuanyi’s household when she learned that they were also interested in this marriage alliance. She was overjoyed, thinking that her daughter’s marriage was now settled.

Just as she was about to discuss the marriage arrangements with the Marquis’s family, Chunyun rushed in, panicked, and whispered something in Madam Xie’s ear.

Madam Xie’s expression changed abruptly. She quickly stood up, pulling Chunyun aside. “What did you say? The young lady isn’t at Qing Shan Ju?”

Chunyun nodded urgently. “This servant took the sobering tea over, but after searching Qing Shan Ju for a long time, there was no sign of the young lady. I just rushed back.”

Madam Xie knew that Xi Rongyan, after getting drunk, had no memory of what she had done. Her heart was filled with alarm and suspicion. She hurriedly asked, “Did you see Baozhu?”

Chunyun shook her head. “No, I didn’t.”

Fearful that something had happened, Madam Xie excused herself to the Marquis’s family and quickly led the maids to Qing Shan Ju.

When they arrived at Qing Shan Ju, there was indeed no one there.

Madam Xie knew Baozhu was steady and reliable—nothing bad should have happened unless something truly had.

For some reason, she suddenly glanced over and saw Qing Yue Ju not far away.

Could it be that she had gone to the wrong place and ended up at Qing Yue Ju?

With that thought, she hurriedly rushed to the nearby Qing Yue Ju.

As soon as she entered, Madam Xie heard a noise.

The voice was very familiar—it was her daughter’s.

She quickened her steps, following the sound. The first thing she saw was a bed with its curtains drawn, and a set of outer garments discarded on the floor. Whose could they be, if not Xi Rongyan’s?

Then, from behind the curtains, came a soft, hoarse voice: “Don’t leave…”

Madam Xie’s heart trembled. Her gaze fell on a pair of black boots with dragon embroidery on the floor. Her vision darkened, and she nearly fainted.

She hastily ordered the maids behind her to leave.

Just as she was about to speak, the curtain was suddenly lifted by a long, slender hand. The Emperor sat up, his expression cold, wearing a golden dragon crane robe. A trace of Xi Rongyan’s lip rouge was smeared on his cheek.

Xi Rongyan, wearing only her inner garments, was clinging tightly to the Emperor’s waist, her bare shoulders exposed, the undershirt beneath her moon-white inner robe barely concealing the stomach cover. She was murmuring, asking the Emperor to play the zither for her, completely unaware of what she was doing.

Madam Xie’s vision darkened again. Her legs gave out, and she knelt down in a panic.

She never could have imagined witnessing such a scene.

Madam Xie forced herself to speak through her dizziness, her voice strained: “This humble subject’s daughter acted improperly after drinking today and offended Your Majesty. Please, Your Majesty, forgive her.”

“I will take my daughter back and discipline her properly.”

Emperor Wei Qi sat leisurely on the edge of the bed, his hand still resting on Xi Rongyan’s waist.

He looked at the kneeling woman before him, his voice cold and unreadable. “I originally came here for some peace and quiet, but I was indeed disturbed.”

“However, considering that the Fourth Young Lady Xi acted improperly due to drunkenness, I will not hold it against her.”

“But her body has been seen entirely by me. Since we have already reached this point, and for the sake of Young Lady Xi’s reputation, I will bring her into the palace in a few days.”

As he spoke, Emperor Wei Qi adjusted Xi Rongyan’s clothes for her, then added in a tone that brooked no refusal: “At that time, I will issue a decree. It is only a matter of waiting.”

Madam Xie felt dizzy again.

The imperial palace was a place of complex intrigues, even more ruthless than the inner quarters of noble families. How could her daughter compete with those women?

But at this point, with the Emperor speaking so bluntly, and given what she had just witnessed…

She felt sick to her stomach. The marriage alliance with the Marquis of Xuanyi had been almost settled, yet this had happened.

Before she could figure out how to respond, Emperor Wei Qi’s voice suddenly turned stern and cold: “Or does Madam Xie not wish for her to enter my harem?”

Madam Xie, pressed by the Emperor’s authority, knew she could not defy the imperial will. The words had already been spoken, and her daughter was currently in this state, sitting in the Emperor’s arms. Even if she were unwilling, she had no reason to refuse.

Moreover, she did not know to what extent things had gone between Rongyan and the Emperor.

What if…

The distressed woman, at a loss, could only harden her resolve and reply: “It would be Rongyan’s great fortune to serve Your Majesty in the palace. This humble subject is also grateful that Your Majesty does not hold her mistake against her.”

Emperor Wei Qi’s expression softened slightly, then ordered Madam Xie to withdraw.

Madam Xie stumbled out in a daze, then suddenly collapsed against a servant beside her, unable to recover her senses for a long time.

Xi Rongyan, who had been sitting in Emperor Wei Qi’s arms, had already calmed down. Leaning against his shoulder, she was clearly about to fall asleep.

Her hair had long since come loose, falling over her moon-white shoulders. She lay quietly in Emperor Wei Qi’s embrace.

Emperor Wei Qi felt the soft warmth of her body. After holding her for a long time, he finally let go, placing her on the bed before standing up.

When Emperor Wei Qi stepped out, he was already properly dressed. His bright yellow dragon robe stood tall before Madam Xie. His towering figure looked down at the woman bowing before him, his face unreadable with imperial coldness.

He clasped his hands behind his back, his voice indifferent: “Madam Xie, prepare well. I will issue the decree today, and in two days, I will have the Fourth Young Lady Xi brought into the palace.”

With that, he directly stepped past Madam Xie and walked out.

Madam Xie only came back to her senses when the Emperor’s figure had disappeared. She had even forgotten to express her gratitude.

She hurried into the room, lifted the bed curtains, and saw Xi Rongyan sleeping peacefully, fully dressed, completely unaware of what had happened.

Madam Xie then looked at the sheets on the bed. Though she found some comfort, she suddenly slumped onto the edge of the bed, feeling as if everything had fallen into chaos.

---

Xi Rongyan woke up in her own boudoir in the afternoon.

As she awoke, she heard Baozhu crying outside. Still disoriented, she couldn’t tell where she was. With a pounding headache, she lifted the curtain and saw Baozhu kneeling on the ground, her forehead swollen and bleeding.

Inside the room sat her mother, father, and eldest brother, all looking at her with grave expressions.

Xi Rongyan’s mind went blank. “What happened?”

Madam Xie lowered her head, wiping away tears, then sat beside Xi Rongyan, her eyes red as she looked at her. “At noon, His Majesty already issued the decree. In two days, you will be taken into the palace.”

Xi Rongyan was slow to react. She turned her head to look at her mother. “What?”

Madam Xie closed her eyes briefly and recounted what had happened.

At that moment, Master Xi suddenly stood up, sighing as he glanced at Xi Rongyan. “Things have come to this point. There’s no use in being upset. The matter with the Marquis of Xuanyi’s family is over.”

As he spoke, he sighed again. “In His Majesty’s eyes, Rongyan’s purity has already been given to him. It’s impossible for her to marry someone else now.”

With that, he walked out.

Eldest brother Xi Wenli hesitated for a moment before following his father out.

He wanted to persuade his father to go to the palace and speak to the Empress Dowager about this matter. After all, with so many women in the harem, without the Emperor’s favor, one could be trapped there for a lifetime.

He didn’t want his younger sister to suffer.

Outside in the corridor, Master Xi frowned at Xi Wenli. “Can’t you see? Given His Majesty’s temperament, if he didn’t want Rongyan in the palace, he wouldn’t have brought it up at all.”

“Since he has, do you think His Majesty will pay any mind to the Empress Dowager’s opinion?”

“His Majesty and the Empress Dowager only maintain a superficial harmony. If we ungratefully refuse His Majesty, what do you think he will think of us?”

“That the Xi family looks down on him, and only wants to form alliances through marriage with other noble families?”

He looked sternly at Xi Wenli. “Don’t bring this up again. Defying His Majesty is a debt that will be remembered. The Empress Dowager may not be able to protect us forever. The Emperor’s mind is unfathomable.”

“Moreover, His Majesty issued the decree so quickly. There’s no room for maneuvering now.”

Xi Wenli was stunned.

He understood that everything his father said was correct. He was just worried about his younger sister’s future.
