With a face of mercy and tolerance, dignified in manner, yet she had turned everyone present against her.

Making others believe that the Emperor’s punishment of Xian Fei yesterday was because she had reported and instigated it.

Indeed, as soon as the Empress finished speaking, the hostile gazes grew even colder.

Lu Rongyue let out another cold snort. “Now that she has the Emperor’s favor, you all should be careful. Be wary that one day you might offend Zhen Pin, and she’ll report you to the Emperor, sending you to the cold palace.”

“She’s only been here for a day, tsk tsk, who knows what will happen in the future.”

The sarcastic tone made Xi Rongyan’s heart sink. She stood up and looked at everyone. “As for yesterday’s matter, first, I did nothing wrong. Second, it was not instigated by me. Third, how the Emperor punishes is not for me to decide.”

“Just now, the Empress also said I was not at fault. If you think that I, having just entered the palace, could manipulate the Emperor, then you underestimate my character. Or do you also underestimate the Emperor?”

“Do you think the Emperor cannot distinguish right from wrong and blindly favors me?”

Xi Rongyan’s voice was not loud, but each word was clear, soft and pleasant. Her entire demeanor was elegant, the dignified bearing of a noble lady, leaving the others momentarily speechless.

Naturally, no one dared to speak further. Who would dare to criticize the Emperor?

Lu Rongyue glanced at Xi Rongyan, her fingers tightening, teeth clenched, but she said nothing, only turning her face away with a cold snort.

She hadn’t expected Xi Rongyan to dare speak like that.

Song Helan watched the scene, pursing her lips, and had everyone else leave, keeping only Xi Rongyan behind.

Song Helan was very polite to Xi Rongyan, leading her to the inner hall to sit, even having Xi Rongyan sit beside her on the luohan bed.

A palace maid came to pour tea. Song Helan elegantly held a white cat in her arms, gazing lightly at Xi Rongyan, who sat properly by her side.

There was indeed a difference between the daughters of scholarly families and those of military families.

Restrained, refined.

Every movement exuded proper decorum. Her brows and eyes were gentle, and even a glance carried a poetic charm.

Most of the current concubines in the harem were taken when the Emperor was still a prince, and most were from military families. Now, the four consorts and those with ranks were all former concubines from the Prince’s mansion.

In the first year after the Emperor ascended the throne, according to ritual, a selection of beauties was held, but only three or four were chosen. In the second year, only two were casually selected, and this year, none were taken in.

It wasn’t that there were no women like Xi Rongyan in the harem, but today, she had seen for herself that there was something different about her demeanor.

No wonder the Emperor treated her differently. In this harem, there were few who could compare in appearance.

Recalling how the Emperor had confined his own cousin for Xi Rongyan’s sake, stopping her stipend and all the honors of her concubine rank, Song Helan’s eyes narrowed.

Xi Rongyan turned her head and saw the Empress’s expression. Her gentle face had a moment of ferocity. She swayed the teacup in her hand, then lowered her eyes and quietly sipped her tea.

Song Helan watched Xi Rongyan’s lowered profile, her expression softened, and she sighed. “Yesterday’s matter was indeed Xian Fei’s fault. Do not blame her.”

Xi Rongyan properly shook her head. “This concubine has never blamed Xian Fei.”

“Consider it a thing of the past.”

Song Helan looked at Xi Rongyan, her gaze filled with sighs. “I have known Xian Fei since we were young. She is a bit spoiled, straightforward, and speaks her mind without restraint.”

“After entering the palace, I had advised her to be careful with her words and actions, but she never listened to me.”

Song Helan reached out and held Xi Rongyan’s hand. “She has always been outspoken, without a filter. Did she wrong you yesterday?”

Xi Rongyan understood that, no matter what, she should agree with the Empress now.

She also knew that in a palace full of women, she needed to be even more low-key.

She also genuinely did not want to draw attention to herself, regardless of whether others believed her.

But she also refused to be bullied.

Xi Rongyan maintained a respectful expression and softly said, “This concubine entered the palace hoping to serve the Emperor harmoniously with all my sisters. Yesterday’s matter was a misunderstanding, but this concubine does not blame Xian Fei.”

“As for how the Emperor decides, this concubine cannot influence.”

Xi Rongyan stood up again and bowed to the Empress. “Also, yesterday, the Empress Dowager summoned this concubine for an important matter, causing me to neglect the Empress. This concubine has been feeling guilty and asks for the Empress’s forgiveness.”

Song Helan raised her eyebrows, watching Xi Rongyan’s obedient posture before her. She carefully examined the woman before her—delicate eyebrows, starry eyes, cherry lips, snowy skin, every piece of jewelry perfectly suited, neither excessive nor too plain, yet mutually enhancing.

Her words were both humble and dignified, neither servile nor arrogant.

One could see the refinement of a noble family.

The Empress Dowager’s niece—if she were a bit more arrogant, she would be easier to deal with.

But with this temperament, Song Helan couldn’t see through her.

Had she entered the palace willingly, or for some other reason?

That day, the Emperor had gone to the Flower Festival without informing anyone, and on that same day, he issued a decree to bring Xi Rongyan into the palace.

These past few days, she had carefully recalled many past details. Xi Rongyan and the Emperor had indeed not met many times before.

The Empress Dowager’s Cining Palace was far from the harem of the concubines. Xi Rongyan usually came in the mornings, and at that time, the Emperor was almost always in the Qianzheng Hall. They had few opportunities to meet.

The only time they had met was when she had heard that the Emperor, on his way to visit the Empress Dowager, had encountered Xi Rongyan. That day, the Emperor had also punished two palace maids for her sake.

Could it be that Xi Rongyan had already cast a spell on the Emperor back then?

Song Helan stared deeply at Xi Rongyan, fearing that everything was arranged by the Empress Dowager.

Even though the Emperor had only one prince, and the Emperor had still not established a crown prince, the Empress Dowager had started to scheme.

A beauty involved in two scandals, surrounded by rumors—it was a perfect arrangement to enter the palace.

As a woman, Song Helan had to admit that Xi Rongyan was indeed attractive. The Empress Dowager had truly placed a good piece on the board.

Song Helan’s gaze darkened, but she reached out and gently took Xi Rongyan’s hand, speaking warmly. “You need not apologize. The Empress Dowager and the Emperor have both sent people to explain this matter. I do not blame you.”

Song Helan had Xi Rongyan sit down again and said to her, “As for the matter between you and Xian Fei, since you say it was a misunderstanding, and Xian Fei also knows she was impulsive.”

“This matter still requires you to speak a few good words for Xian Fei before the Emperor. After all, we are all serving the Emperor in the harem. Harmony is what matters.”

“Those petty jealousies are really unnecessary, aren’t they?”

Xi Rongyan understood that no matter what, she should agree with the Empress now.

In truth, she also did not want to attract attention. Regardless of whether others believed her, she genuinely wanted peace and tranquility.

But she also refused to be bullied.

Xi Rongyan maintained her respectful demeanor and softly said, “This concubine entered the palace hoping to live in harmony with my sisters. I also did not wish for such things to happen.”

“If I can see the Emperor again, this concubine will plead for mercy.”

Xi Rongyan then looked at the Empress. “But the Emperor’s decision is not for this concubine to influence. I can only do my best.”

Song Helan smiled. “This matter started with you. Having you end it is not difficult.”

“Do not be modest.”

Although the Empress’s face maintained a faint smile, Xi Rongyan inexplicably felt a chill.

As she finally left Yongchun Palace, the bright spring sunlight shone on her, and everywhere she looked were high walls, with no end in sight.

---

chapters.title: Delicate Beauty
chapters.content:
She walked along the path, not knowing what she felt.

She had thought a lot. The way the concubines had looked at her in the Empress’s presence, their sarcastic and mocking words—she wasn’t hurt by those words. But they had mentioned Brother Chuanyu.

They used Brother Chuanyu to mock her, poking at her pain.

Even the dead were not spared; now they were being used to mock her.

Yuzhu noticed Xi Rongyan’s unease. Seeing her walking forward with her head down, not saying a word, she quickly stepped ahead and saw that Xi Rongyan’s eyes were slightly red.

Indeed, the Empress’s seemingly gentle words had hidden barbs.

Although her mistress had responded beautifully today, being mocked by so many people was still painful.

She softly comforted, “Mistress, don’t take those words to heart. When you have the upper hand, why bother with their words?”

Xi Rongyan slightly turned her head toward Yuzhu and softly said, “I don’t care about those words. I know they said them deliberately to mock me.”

Xi Rongyan lifted her head, looking at the palace walls, her voice hoarse. “Fighting and struggling was never my intention, but I cannot avoid it.”

Yuzhu fell silent, looking at Xi Rongyan’s bright, clear eyes that held a hint of sadness.

She gently dabbed the moisture from the corners of Xi Rongyan’s eyes with a handkerchief and softly said, “Mistress, you’ve already entered the palace. There’s no turning back.”

“Didn’t the Empress Dowager go through the same thing back then?”

“A concubine without children is like a boat adrift at sea. Even the Empress Dowager cannot protect you forever.”

Xi Rongyan lowered her head and said nothing, silently walking forward.

As she neared the Hanyuan Hall, she suddenly heard a soft call from ahead. Looking up, she saw her cousin, Xie Yumian, standing at her palace gate waiting for her.

Upon seeing Xie Yumian, Xi Rongyan suppressed the sadness in her heart and quickly walked over, her face showing some surprise. “Sister, how long have you been waiting?”

Xie Yumian was Xi Rongyan’s cousin, and the two had been close friends since childhood. Her cousin was two years older and had entered the palace two years ago.

Previously, when Xi Rongyan had entered the palace to accompany the Empress Dowager, she had wanted to visit her cousin, but she had heard that the harem was strict. Usually, even letters could not be exchanged, and visits required a special decree, with complicated procedures, so she had given up.

Xie Yumian tightly held Xi Rongyan’s hand, looking at her unchanged temperament and appearance, and sighed.

She had never expected Xi Rongyan to enter the palace one day.

She looked Xi Rongyan up and down, then softly said, “Let’s go inside to talk.”

The two entered together.

As soon as they did, Xie Yumian saw the inner courtyard filled with peach blossoms. Following Xi Rongyan’s steps into the hall, she saw every corner carefully arranged, and a vague, indistinct feeling arose in her heart.

She was currently squeezed into two rooms next to Qi Fei’s Yique Palace. Xi Rongyan had just entered the palace and could already live in the main hall.

Following Xi Rongyan, they sat together on the spacious luohan bed. The bright morning light streamed in, illuminating the room brilliantly, the lighting far better than her own quarters.

She looked at Xi Rongyan sitting beside her, who, as before, warmly poured tea for her. She smelled the aroma—it was the Yu Chun tea she had loved most in her boudoir.

Back then, she and Xi Rongyan had shared everything, sitting under the large carved window on the spring couch, watching the rain outside, holding cups of Yu Chun tea, and confiding in each other.

The steaming teacup was brought to her, and through the mist, she smelled the familiar scent. It was as if she had been transported back in time. After years apart, some things remained, but people had changed.

She had not fared well in the palace.

Not even comparable to Xi Rongyan, who had just entered.

She pinched the teacup with her fingertips and softly asked, “How does my sister have Yu Chun tea here?”

Even tea in the palace was ranked.

Those with the rank of consort and above could request their preferred tea from the Imperial Household Department. Those below consort rank were not allowed to choose; the tea provided was not up to them.

She was merely an unfavored Cainren, and the Imperial Household Department wouldn’t even bother with her tea.

Xi Rongyan held her teacup, sitting close to Xie Yumian as before. “There are many tea canisters on that table. Coincidentally, they are all teas I used to like.”

“I knew Sister liked Yu Chun tea, so I specifically prepared it first. My original intention was to invite Sister to talk today.”

Xie Yumian turned her head in surprise, looking at Xi Rongyan’s misty, watery eyes, which had always held a gentle, rain-like tenderness that made people feel affection and closeness.

She had always been soft-spoken and kind. She had always loved Xi Rongyan the most.

Even as she watched her grow more and more beautiful, she had been happy for her appearance, her temperament, and rejoiced that she would have a husband like the refined and scholarly Gu family heir.

She had been genuinely happy for her.

She truly believed that a woman as pure as porcelain like Xi Rongyan deserved to be cherished.

In the past, she had often taken care of her, and she had hoped she would live peacefully.

Xie Yumian’s eyes reddened as past memories made her heart ache. She set down her teacup and pulled Xi Rongyan into a tight embrace, smelling the peach blossom fragrance on her. Hoarsely, she said, “Why did you enter the palace?”

“Just now at the Empress’s, Sister did not speak up for me. Do you blame me?”

Xi Rongyan understood the situation and vaguely saw the power dynamics. She lowered her head onto Xie Yumian’s shoulder, her eyes filling with tears, and softly said, “I don’t blame you.”

“I never thought to blame you.”

Xie Yumian closed her eyes, then hoarsely said, “Almost all the women in the harem are on the Empress’s side. The Emperor rarely favors the harem, and those of us who entered later through the selection have no one to rely on in the palace. We can only depend on the past.”

“I was arranged to live in the Lanyue Pavilion of the Yi Qing Palace where Qi Fei resides. Just now, I did not dare to speak for you because I was afraid Qi Fei would target me.”

“Please, do not blame me, little sister.”

Xi Rongyan shook her head. “I actually understand a little. How could I blame you?”

Xie Yumian finally let go of Xi Rongyan and carefully examined her face.

Seeing her slightly reddened eyes, like peach blossoms falling into water, a complex emotion arose in her heart.

She said, “I have also heard about the Gu family’s matters in the palace. I felt sorry for you but could not help.”

“I also prayed that you would find another good husband like Young Master Gu.”

“But I never expected you to enter the palace. Was it arranged by the Empress Dowager?”

Xi Rongyan still felt that her entry into the palace was like a dream; she couldn’t explain it clearly.

She shook her head. “It was not arranged by my aunt.”

Xi Rongyan regretfully lowered her head. “My aunt had originally arranged another marriage for me, but due to a twist of fate...”

“After Brother Chuanyu’s incident, Mother wanted to quickly find a marriage for me. From the beginning, there was no plan to enter the palace.”

chapters.title: You Insist on Entering the Palace
chapters.content:
Xie Yumian looked at Xi Rongyan’s expression and saw that she did not really want to enter the palace.

She placed her hand on Xi Rongyan’s fingers, and after a long silence, she didn’t know what to say.

Gu Yuan’s accident was truly too unexpected.

A noble young master was out traveling, yet bandits dared to rob him. If blame must be placed, it could only be on bad luck—just happening to encounter such vicious and ruthless people.

She followed with regret, then softly said, “The people in the palace are complicated, especially since you are currently favored.”

“The only prince is the son of the Empress. General Song is the Emperor’s trusted and important minister. The Crown Prince will inevitably be the Grand Prince.”

“We can only rely on Her Majesty the Empress.”

“Yet you insist on entering the palace.”

Xi Rongyan looked at Xie Yumian, helplessly smiling. Upon seeing a familiar face, she finally felt a slight sense of comfort.

As for entering the palace, there was nothing more to say about it. The events of that day were not worth bringing up again—doing so would only add to the melancholy.

She lowered her head, gazing blankly at the golden thread lotus on her round fan, and only softly said, “Since I have entered the palace, I will take it one step at a time.”

Xie Yumian nodded, then looked at Xi Rongyan’s expression and suddenly asked, “Is it only you living in Guan Ju Palace?”

Xi Rongyan nodded.

Xie Yumian tightened her grip on her hand, hesitated for a moment, then spoke to Xi Rongyan, “Now that you have caught His Majesty’s eye, sister, can I ask you for a favor?”

Xi Rongyan looked at Xie Yumian, “What is it?”

Xie Yumian then took Xi Rongyan’s hand and gently said, “I want to ask you to request His Majesty to let me come and stay with you in Guan Ju Palace.”

“I see that the side hall is empty. You and I have been close since childhood. In the future, we can often be together and talk.”

Xi Rongyan hesitated for a moment, then softly asked, “I still don’t understand the rules of the palace. If I go over the Empress’s head and ask His Majesty to arrange for you to stay here with me, would that be inappropriate?”

Xie Yumian quickly replied, “Don’t worry, sister. As long as His Majesty gives the word, even the Empress cannot say anything.”

As she spoke, she tightly held Xi Rongyan’s hand, “Sister, I really want to come over.”

“In the future, we can support each other and keep each other company in the palace so it won’t be lonely.”

Xie Yumian truly wanted to escape from Qi Fei.

She usually couldn’t see the Emperor even once a month.

Since she entered the palace, the Emperor had only visited her place once or twice, and had never even touched her.

Qi Fei often mocked her coldly and hotly, which was also the reason why others looked down on her.

Moreover, now that Xi Rongyan was favored, although she didn’t know how long the favor would last, if she moved in with her, perhaps she could use Xi Rongyan’s connection to make the Emperor look at her more.

She was really tired of the cold and lonely days of being out of favor.

Xi Rongyan knew that Xie Yumian currently lived under Qi Fei, who was the mistress of her own palace and also a follower of the Empress.

If she asked the Emperor to let her sister come over, it would inevitably offend Qi Fei and the Empress.

But when she saw Xie Yumian’s reddened eyes in front of her, she thought that she must not be doing well under Qi Fei, which was why she was begging her like this.

At present, her relationship with the Empress was already somewhat strained, so it didn’t matter whether she offended them or not.

After a moment of hesitation, she nodded, “Sister, rest assured, I will speak to His Majesty.”

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan paused again, looking at Xie Yumian, “But I have just entered the palace and do not understand His Majesty’s temperament. If His Majesty does not agree, sister, please don’t blame me.”

Xie Yumian quickly nodded, “Don’t worry, sister. I understand that His Majesty has a cold and indifferent nature, with an unpredictable temper. Ordinary people don’t dare to approach him.”

“Even if it doesn’t work out, I won’t blame you.”

Xi Rongyan slightly reassured, nodded again, and softly said, “This morning, His Majesty said he would come to accompany me for dinner. I will bring it up then.”

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan looked at Xie Yumian and smiled, “If His Majesty agrees, you and I can indeed be together often.”

“I can only do my best, but I cannot guarantee it. As long as you don’t blame me, sister, it’s fine.”

Xie Yumian listened to Xi Rongyan’s words and was stunned for a moment.

She had been in the palace for two years and had never heard of His Majesty dining with any concubine.

He rarely even stayed overnight in the harem, let alone dine there.

If His Majesty could stay in the harem for a few more days, the imperial lineage would not be so weak.

With so many people in the harem, there was only one prince and one princess.

She looked into Xi Rongyan’s eyes, feeling a lump in her throat, but couldn’t say the words.

She nodded again in silence and softly said, “I won’t blame you.”

“If His Majesty doesn’t agree, then forget it. Sister, don’t anger His Majesty on my account.”

“Now that His Majesty comes to you is a good thing. Sister, you must seize this opportunity.”

Regarding her cousin’s words, Xi Rongyan had countless thoughts in her heart, but in the end, she only lightly nodded, “Thank you, sister, for telling me these things. I will remember them.”

The two talked until it was almost noon. Xi Rongyan casually invited Xie Yumian to stay for a meal.

But Xie Yumian had to return. There were rules in the palace: even if the concubines were close, they couldn’t stay too long, let alone dine together.

When the time came, she had to go back.

Qi Fei was watching her every move for mistakes. She was not on the Empress’s side, and since the Emperor didn’t pay much attention to the harem, the Empress was still the most powerful there. Dealing with her would be all too easy.

She softly said, “It’s been a long time since I’ve had a chance to talk with you, sister. Don’t see me off. I’ll go back by myself.”

With that, she got up without letting Xi Rongyan see her off and walked out on her own.

Once outside, she turned her head to look back at the peach blossoms in the palace. Her thoughts surged, and she felt a pang of jealousy.

She and Xi Rongyan had similar family backgrounds and had been close since childhood. In the past, she had never felt this way, but now she felt that Xi Rongyan was lucky in every aspect.

When the Gu family had their accident, she had even felt sorrow for her.

Now it seemed that perhaps she was the one who needed sympathy.

She tightened her sleeves and walked forward. Halfway there, she looked up and saw a palanquin carried by a dozen eunuchs ahead.

The man in the palanquin was noble and cold. She stood to the side in a daze and bowed. The man didn’t even glance at her, as if she were no different from an ordinary brick in the palace wall.

Until the palanquin passed by her side, she turned and watched as it stopped at the gate of Han Yuan Hall.

The Emperor stepped down from the palanquin and walked straight in with large strides.

She looked up at the sky. The bright spring sunlight stung her eyes. She blinked, and a sour feeling arose spontaneously.

She once again understood the jealous looks from the other concubines at the Empress’s place today.

Because she was jealous too.

---

chapters.title: Yan’er, Don’t Be Afraid
chapters.content:
After Xie Yumian left, Xi Rongyan got up and sat on the spring couch behind the screen, lost in thought.

Seeing her cousin from before, she recalled various past events from their time together in the boudoir, and felt a wave of emptiness.

Bao Zhu came in from outside with two peach blossom branches to offer as comfort, “Mistress, don’t overthink. Let them talk. They are just jealous of you.”

Xi Rongyan looked at the peach blossoms in front of her, took one in her hand, and after staring at it for a while, she propped her head up and softly said, “After spring, the peach blossoms will wither.”

“The begonia flowers will wither too.”

“Then lotus and roses will bloom in full splendor. They won’t be able to keep up with their jealousy.”

Bao Zhu softly agreed, then said, “But peach blossoms and begonia will bloom again next year. Mistress, why worry so much?”

Xi Rongyan was silent for a moment, plucked a peach blossom petal, and let it fall onto the carpet. She softly spoke, “It’s just that today, after seeing my cousin, I thought of the past and can’t calm down for a while.”

“She used to be a bright and cheerful girl, but today I saw her face filled with sorrow, and even her smile seemed forced.”

“I only hope that I can truly help her and give her some comfort.”

Halfway through her sentence, Xi Rongyan paused again.

She had only just entered the palace and didn’t understand how long the Emperor’s favor would last. Perhaps she was also insignificant in this harem.

At this moment, a palace servant outside announced that the Emperor had arrived.

Xi Rongyan was startled and hadn’t had time to get up from the spring couch when she saw the Emperor had already walked in behind the screen.

She hurriedly stood up to perform the palace greeting.

But as soon as she bent down, she felt a tightness around her waist. Before she could react, she found herself sitting on the Emperor’s lap.

She felt a slight unease. She was still not used to such closeness.

The Emperor’s breath fell on her neck, warm and a little suffocating.

Wei Qi lowered his head, looking at Xi Rongyan’s fair profile. She had never sat quietly in his arms like this before.

Although she was weak and timid, when she lost her temper, she could be very troublesome, biting and scratching. He was afraid of hurting her with his strength, so he never used much force. Even when angry, he was always the one to compromise in the end.

This rare moment of closeness softened his heart. Seeing the hint of redness in her eyes, he darkened his gaze, pulled her tightly into his embrace, and traced her eyelids with his fingers, asking with concern, “Did the Empress make things difficult for you?”

Xi Rongyan was taken aback and looked up, meeting the Emperor’s concerned and caring eyes.

The last time she had seen the Emperor when she entered the palace, although he had seemed somewhat gentle, there was still a depth in his eyes that was somewhat frightening.

Now, seeing the Emperor’s eyes filled with concern, though not as gentle as Brother Yuan’s, it still made her heart skip a beat.

She also recalled how the Emperor had kissed her last night, softly calling her name, which was very tender.

She was puzzled. Why did everyone say the Emperor was cold and cruel, even her cousin?

If the Emperor was only like this with her, but she had only interacted with the Emperor a few times...

She stammered and just shook her head.

Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan’s distracted eyes, then silently darkened his gaze and held her tighter.

He gently patted her back. Although he didn’t speak, it seemed like he was offering comfort.

Like a warm light, it puzzled Xi Rongyan and warmed her heart.

She still held the peach branch in her hand, her fair and delicate fingers crushing the petals. This gentle Emperor made her feel as if she were in a dream.

Wei Qi lowered his head. Her full lips were right in front of him.

He wanted to kiss her again.

But he was still afraid of scaring her.

In the past, Xi Rongyan had been afraid of him. Whenever she saw him approaching, she would hide.

Every time he kissed her, he had to forcefully pinch her chin to open her mouth.

He knew he had used force, and he knew it hurt her, but she never learned her lesson and always forced him to use strength.

Actually, thinking back now, those memories were also painful for Wei Qi.

He had envied the dead man more than once.

He could only vent his dissatisfaction with her by tormenting her. He had questioned her countless times about what he lacked compared to that dead man. Every time, her silent resistance was more lingering than her words.

She didn’t speak, which tortured him more than if she had.

Wei Qi was lost in thought. His fingers, holding Xi Rongyan’s hand, unconsciously tightened. When he came to his senses, Xi Rongyan was looking at him with a terrified expression.

Again, that look.

His dark gaze shifted, falling on the gilded lotus lamp column beside them, which vaguely reflected his fierce and distorted features.

He was startled for a moment, quickly covering Xi Rongyan’s eyes with his hand. Bending down, he rested his chin on her shoulder, where the pale embroidery of begonia flowers was, and closed his eyes, hoarsely saying, “Yan’er, don’t be afraid.”

He then wrapped his arms tightly around her, “The war in the north is intense, and I am also troubled.”

Xi Rongyan had indeed been scared by the Emperor’s expression just now.

It was already somewhat fierce and intimidating, and when his eyes darkened, it was especially terrifying.

It was said that when the Emperor was in the north, even the leaders of the northern tribes would be intimidated by his appearance. When his eyes narrowed, they seemed to flash with a bloody light, as if he were about to kill.

This was the first time she had seen such an expression.

It was as if he were two different people compared to when he first entered.

Now, with her eyes covered by Wei Qi, and hearing the Emperor’s gentle words, her thoughts were in chaos.

She didn’t know about the war in the north. Maybe it was true.

She was still fearful, her heart beating fast, but she nodded obediently.

Wei Qi released his fingers and slightly leaned back, looking at the person in his arms. He lifted her chin and looked at her still somewhat shocked and uncertain eyes, then bent down and kissed her eyelids.

He held her for a long time, knowing that he had not controlled his emotions well and had scared her again.

In the past, she had always said he looked terrifying.

She said she was used to people as gentle as Gu Yuanyu.

Wei Qi’s gaze shifted back to the person in the lamp column, his features twisted and distorted, as if he could never become the kind of person she liked.

His long fingers slowly combed through her hair. He closed his eyes and asked her, “This morning at the Empress’s place, did anyone disrespect you?”

Xi Rongyan, held tightly by the Emperor, found it a bit hard to breathe. Hearing the Emperor suddenly ask this, she stammered for a moment.

She still shook her head, “No.”

Wei Qi pursed his lips but knew that asking Xi Rongyan directly would mostly yield no results.

Her nature hadn’t changed much.

In the previous life, when she was bullied by the Virtuous Consort, she had never mentioned it to him.

Now, he had already sent the Virtuous Consort to the cold palace, also worried that with her nature, she would suffer again.

Wei Qi didn’t ask further. He just gently patted her back again, “After some more days, I will promote your rank and have you move to Cheng Qian Palace.”

“That place has been vacant for a long time and is currently under renovation. You’ll have to wait a little longer.”

“It is close to my Ming De Hall. In the future, I will live there with you. You can also come to Ming De Hall to find me anytime. No one will dare to treat you poorly, not even the Empress.”

Xi Rongyan was stunned, staring blankly at the dragon pattern on the Emperor’s dark robe, almost thinking she had misheard.

Were those words really said to her by the Emperor?

To have her live in Cheng Qian Palace, the closest to Ming De Hall, and even live with the Emperor?

It all sounded somewhat unbelievable.

At this moment, the sound of the meal being served came from outside. Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan, who was still in a daze, and didn’t expect her to respond.

At least he had taken the initiative now. Slowly, he would make her heart include him.

He took her hand and stood up to go out. The maids came to serve the dishes, but Wei Qi had them all withdraw. He personally served food to Xi Rongyan.

Xi Rongyan was still in a state of shock from the unexpected favor. Looking at the vinegar-soaked snail brought to her lips, then at the Emperor’s patient and smiling eyes, she finally parted her lips and bit the chopsticks.

Wei Qi’s deep gaze watched the silver chopsticks enter her red lips, smiled, and then picked up a piece of small bamboo shoot.

These were all dishes that Xi Rongyan liked. She loved sweet and sour flavors, and he had arranged them all for her, not wanting her to feel wronged in the palace.

chapters.title: I Will Keep You Company for Dinner at Night
chapters.content:
From the moment the first bite was taken, Xi Rongyan didn’t get a chance to eat by herself.

In the end, she somehow found herself sitting on the Emperor’s lap again, being coaxed to eat more.

Xi Rongyan’s cheeks flushed crimson. Finally, unable to eat another bite, she gently pushed the Emperor’s hand away, her eyes pleading, "Your Majesty, I truly cannot eat any more."

Wei Qi lowered his gaze to Xi Rongyan, who seemed cautious yet obedient. Though still bound by etiquette, she was gentle and compliant.

In the past, feeding her even a single bite would exhaust them both.

Wei Qi did hope she would eat more for her health, but he wouldn’t force her. Taking a handkerchief from a nearby palace maid, he personally wiped her mouth.

Then he asked, "Are you truly full?"

Xi Rongyan nodded hastily, "Yes."

Only then did Wei Qi relax. After she rinsed her mouth, he carried her to the inner chamber and placed her on the bed.

Xi Rongyan looked at Wei Qi in bewilderment, her heart fluttering with unease.

Wei Qi was tall, broad-shouldered, and his presence was overwhelming, almost intimidating.

Wei Qi noticed her expression and understood her thoughts all too well.

He simply sat beside her, softly saying, "Spring makes one drowsy. If you’re tired, sleep for a while. When you wake, I’ll have someone bring you milk soup."

Xi Rongyan blinked in surprise.

Back in her boudoir, she always took a nap in spring, and afterward, she would enjoy a bowl of milk soup. It had been a habit for many years.

But how could this be such a coincidence?

She parted her lips, wanting to ask but not knowing how.

Wei Qi smiled, "I sent someone to your residence to inquire."

Though this resolved her confusion, it shocked her that the Emperor had gone to such lengths to learn her preferences. No wonder all the dishes on the table earlier were her favorites.

Enclosed in his warm embrace, she felt the strong heartbeat within, and for the first time, she didn’t find the Emperor so terrifying.

As Wei Qi’s large hand gently stroked her back, his warm voice, like the sunlight filtering through the branches outside, said, "You’ve grown thinner. I’ll come earlier in the evening to keep you company for dinner."

Xi Rongyan, breathing in the scent of dragon’s saliva incense, listened to the Emperor’s gentle voice, which filled her with a sense of security. She closed her eyes and softly hummed in agreement.

After a moment of hesitation, she quietly lifted her head to look at the Emperor, bit her lip, and carefully spoke, "Your Majesty, could you allow my cousin to come and keep me company?"

"There’s still space next to Hanyuan Palace. It’s lonely for me to live alone. My cousin could come and keep me company."

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan’s fingers nervously tightened. She truly didn’t understand the Emperor’s temperament and didn’t know how he would react.

Seeing the Emperor’s dark eyes looking down at her, her heart pounded.

Even though she knew the Emperor treated her gently and well, she still felt uneasy.

Wei Qi, in truth, was not pleased with others living there.

He remembered Xi Rongyan’s cousin—she was the one who had helped Xi Rongyan escape in his past life.

But she was also the one who had betrayed Xi Rongyan’s whereabouts.

To seek favor and self-preservation, she had easily sold Xi Rongyan out.

If it weren’t for fearing that Xi Rongyan might resent him further, he would have dealt with her long ago.

But now, he didn’t want to refuse Xi Rongyan.

It had been difficult enough for Xi Rongyan to not fear his closeness. If he refused, she might overthink.

Wei Qi pondered for a moment, then bent down to caress Xi Rongyan’s face, "I have this matter in mind. Don’t worry, I will arrange it properly."

Xi Rongyan hadn’t held much hope, but unexpectedly, it seemed the Emperor had agreed.

Her eyes lit up, and she stood to express her gratitude.

Wei Qi watched the sparkle in Xi Rongyan’s eyes, concealing the complexity in his own. He lowered his gaze to hide his expression.

Xi Rongyan always found joy in matters concerning others, yet she rarely gave much thought to herself.

In the past, she had never even looked at him properly.

He didn’t want her to discover the lingering resentment from the past. After all, everything was over.

And now, there was still time for everything.

He gently massaged Xi Rongyan’s smooth, tender palm, concealing his possessive desire well before leaving.

As he stepped out, Wei Qi paused with his hands behind his back. His dark, cold eyes flickered under his dark robes before he ascended the palanquin toward the Empress’s palace.

Inside Yongchun Palace, the Empress, listening to the words of the matron beside her, furiously grabbed a handful of cat fur. A yowl erupted as the cat struggled in Song Helan’s arms before leaping away.

Song Helan took a deep breath, brushed the cat hair from her skirt, and leaned back against the soft cushion. She slanted a cold smile at the matron beside her, "Oh? His Majesty specially went to keep her company for lunch?"

Matron Yu, unnerved by the Empress’s gentle yet chilling gaze, nodded, "Little Linzi reported it. He said His Majesty stayed for a long time."

A mocking smile curled on Song Helan’s lips.

She had accompanied the Emperor for seven years, and the number of times they had shared a midday meal together could be counted on one hand.

Yet, as soon as Xi Rongyan entered the palace, the Emperor treated her with such care.

Matron Yu observed Song Helan’s expression and leaned in, whispering, "Actually, it would be easy for Your Majesty to deal with her."

She then leaned closer to Song Helan’s ear and whispered something.

Song Helan raised an eyebrow and smirked, "Being favored is nothing. There’s no need for me to intervene."

"Let’s wait a few days to see if His Majesty is just seeking novelty."

Matron Yu found this reasonable. Over the years, she had seen that while His Majesty rarely favored the women of the harem, he had never truly loved anyone.

Even the beautiful and enchanting Consort Wang, who was as lovely as Consort Zhen, had never caught His Majesty’s eye—he had never even visited her.

Perhaps this time, it was indeed just novelty.

As they spoke, the curtain was hastily drawn aside from the outside. A palace maid rushed to the Empress’s side, bowing low, "Your Majesty, His Majesty has arrived."

Song Helan paused. It had been a long time since His Majesty had come.

She suppressed the flicker of joy on her face, maintaining her dignified and composed demeanor, yet she rose hastily.

Meanwhile, after the Emperor left, Xi Rongyan slumped onto the bed, exchanging idle words with Yuzhu.

She yawned—ever since spring began, she had been feeling drowsy.

Yuzhu earnestly advised beside her, "His Majesty cares so much for you, even sending someone to inquire about your preferences. Doesn’t that mean he likes you?"

"You must seize the opportunity, Your Ladyship. Tonight, you should take the initiative..."

Before she could finish, Xi Rongyan suddenly pulled the blanket over her head. A muffled voice came from beneath, "Yuzhu, I understand."

Xi Rongyan understood all of this, but when it came to taking the initiative in that matter... she didn’t know if she could bring herself to do it.

Yuzhu was left speechless and could only tiptoe out quietly.

Once she heard no more sounds beside her, Xi Rongyan lightly lifted the blanket, staring blankly at the canopy above.

She turned her head and saw Baozhu sitting quietly beside her.

The wound on Baozhu’s face still bore a red mark. Xi Rongyan reached out to touch it, asking, "Does it still hurt?"

Baozhu shook her head with a smile, "This servant is fine."

Xi Rongyan fell silent, burying her face in the blanket before turning over.

After a long while, she opened her eyes again, lost in thought.

She, too, was anxious.

But deep down, she understood—now that she had entered the palace, she should start looking forward.

---

chapters.title: Do You Want Me to Feed You?
chapters.content:
In the afternoon, as the sky began to darken, Xi Rongyan’s heart grew tense.

The Emperor had said he would come to keep her company for dinner, but the dishes were already prepared and growing cold.

In truth, she was a little hungry.

Just as she hesitated whether to start eating, a palace maid who had been keeping watch outside rushed in, delightedly announcing, "Mistress, His Majesty has arrived!"

Xi Rongyan didn’t know whether to feel relieved or not. She stood to greet him, but before she could perform the proper palace etiquette, the Emperor took her by the shoulder and led her inside.

He softly explained, "I was a bit busy, so I’m late."

As he spoke, he guided her to sit beside him. Naturally, he took a dampened handkerchief from a palace maid’s hand and began wiping her hands, asking, "Did you wait long for me? Are you hungry?"

As soon as he asked, Wei Qi realized it was a foolish question—he already knew she would shake her head.

Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze, staring blankly at her hand resting in the Emperor’s palm, being gently wiped clean. She couldn’t believe the Emperor would take such care of her.

And he was so kind to her.

Even if he arrived late, he didn’t need to explain himself to her.

She lifted her head in a daze, looking at the handsome, gentle face before her. In the flickering light of the palace lanterns, she realized for the first time that the Emperor was truly strikingly handsome.

The Emperor she saw was nothing like the one others described.

Wei Qi finished wiping her hands and placed a silver chopstick in her palm, then asked which dishes she liked. Everything he did was gentle and natural, as if he had done it a thousand times before.

Only then did Xi Rongyan notice that the dishes on the table had been changed. She realized that the Emperor must have known he was late and had the food prepared anew.

The table was now filled with steaming dishes she loved. Under the Emperor’s gaze, she lowered her head and picked up a piece of stir-fried almonds, but couldn’t help glancing at his face.

The Emperor was watching her with a gentle and calm expression, as if the fleeting darkness and ferocity she had glimpsed at noon had been an illusion.

Then, more food was placed into her bowl, and his slightly low voice sounded in her ear, "Looking at me—do you want me to feed you?"

Xi Rongyan froze, her face suddenly flushing red. She quickly lowered her head.

Wei Qi silently tugged at the corner of his lips, his peripheral vision fixed on her.

He recalled a night not long after Gu Yunyu’s incident, when she had come to see him.

It was deep autumn, cold outside. She had been wrapped in thick brocade, her eyes slightly red, her gaze weary, a white silk band around her forehead. Though her hair was simply pinned with a single silver hairpin, in his eyes at the time, she had been breathtakingly beautiful.

A single submissive lowering of her eyes had sent his heart racing, filling him with an urgent desire to possess her.

He didn’t know when he had first harbored the intent to possess her—perhaps it was every time he heard she was entering the palace to see the Empress Dowager, his heart would stir.

He remembered her slow, unadorned figure approaching.

When she had knelt before him to plead for the Gu family, he had already regarded her as his.

He had invited her to share dinner with him, and the table had been filled with dishes he had carefully prepared for her.

There had also been a pot of pear blossom spring wine.

Fearful she might be afraid or unable to relax, he had specially prepared the wine for her.

The wine had been warmed so she wouldn’t catch a chill.

That night, at the banquet for two, her face had been pale with fear, just as cautious and restrained as she was now, unable to eat a single bite properly.

But back then, she had been in the depths of sorrow, barely clinging to life for the sake of her and Gu Yunyu’s child.

He had treated her like prey, pouring her wine with his own hands.

Unfortunately, she hadn’t drunk it. She had been clever enough to sense his intentions and, trembling, had knelt down.

Exposing the fair, slender nape of her neck—the most delicate and vulnerable part of her—to the hunter.

What a pity.

It had been wine he had prepared for her with his own hands.

She could have, under the influence of the wine, submitted to him. But she had defied his expectations with unexpected chastity.

That had not been a pleasant night.

Afterward, the chance to dine peacefully with her had vanished. She had never cooperated.

Now, her face was flushed, and she sat obediently by his side, giving him a completely different feeling.

He knew, deep down, that he preferred it this way.

As long as she didn’t think of leaving, it was fine.

After dinner, Wei Qi held Xi Rongyan against him on a small couch as they read.

Enclosed in the Emperor’s embrace, the sound of turning pages matched the beating of her heart. She shifted stiffly.

Surrounded by Wei Qi’s scent, she didn’t know what to say. The Emperor, it seemed, wasn’t the type to engage in idle chat with her.

Fortunately, a palace servant entered to announce that the bathwater was ready. She seized the opportunity, saying to the Emperor, "This concubine will go bathe now."

Wei Qi’s arm was around her slender waist. Truthfully, he had no mind to read—he simply wanted to hold her longer.

He didn’t know how to converse with her. In his past life, the two of them had never had a proper conversation.

He wasn’t skilled at winning a woman’s heart, either.

The fragrance wafting from her was torturous, but when she mentioned bathing, his body tensed for a moment before he loosened his hold.

He wanted to join her, but knowing her conservative nature, he restrained himself, thinking to take things step by step.

Only when Xi Rongyan was in the bath did she finally breathe a sigh of relief. Baozhu scrubbed her back and whispered, "Earlier, this servant secretly glanced at His Majesty and found that His Majesty is truly handsome. Did you notice, Mistress?"

In truth, up to now, Xi Rongyan hadn’t dared to look at the Emperor properly, let alone study his features.

She knew he was extremely handsome, but his aura was too intimidating.

She had felt it—the killing intent. When the Emperor wasn’t smiling, he was truly someone others dared not approach. Perhaps that was why so many said he was cruel.

Xi Rongyan propped her head up, mumbled a vague response in the steam, and closed her eyes, not wanting to leave the warmth too soon.

She was genuinely nervous.

After adding hot water several times, Baozhu couldn’t help but say, "Mistress, you’ve been soaking for nearly half an hour."

Xi Rongyan knew she couldn’t stay in the bath any longer and finally stood up.

When she emerged, the Emperor was sitting by the bed waiting for her. His deep, dark eyes had been fixed on her the moment she entered, making her heart tighten.

She took small steps toward Wei Qi.

Wei Qi watched Xi Rongyan’s shy demeanor, and truthfully, he enjoyed seeing her like this.

They said a woman only blushed when she harbored feelings for a man. Now that Gu Yunyu was long dead, perhaps she had begun to make room for him in her heart.

Drops of water still clung to her slightly damp hair, sliding down her fair, slender neck.

Before him was her slender waist—he knew how soft it was.

Even as a married woman, her body still carried an allure that made him want to possess her forcefully.

Like a tender, sweet apricot just ripened, its fragrance alone made one want to take a bite.

Yet Wei Qi restrained himself perfectly. He pulled her into his embrace and took a handkerchief from a palace maid to dry her hair.

He had plenty of time and patience.

No one would ever come between them again.

One day, she would realize that he was a thousand times better than Gu Yunyu.

Whatever tenderness and care Gu Yunyu had given her, he could provide as well.

chapters.title: Nightmare
chapters.content:
The delicate shoulders were stained with dark, damp marks.

Her soft, long hair draped over her thin back, damp and tangled.

She was obedient, compliant.

And crystal clear.

Wei Qi's gaze deepened behind Xi Rongyan, where she couldn't see. With just a slight lift of his eyelids, the palace attendants in the inner hall trembled in fear and quickly lowered their heads to retreat.

Yu Zhu had been standing by Xi Rongyan’s side. Sensing a chill, she looked up and met Wei Qi’s gaze, which startled her. Hesitating, she also lowered her head and stepped back.

Xi Rongyan only realized belatedly that all the palace attendants had withdrawn. She was puzzled—why had even Yu Zhu left?

Now, only she and the Emperor remained in the room, and she began to feel nervous again.

She felt the Emperor gently drying her long hair behind her, strand by strand. A strange sensation welled up in her heart—how could the Emperor, of all people, be willing to do such a thing for her?

He was, after all, the exalted Son of Heaven.

His gentle movements made her drowsy, and much of her tension melted away.

The way he dried her hair was so light, and though she had once found the scent of dragon’s saliva incense on him oppressive, she had grown accustomed to it.

His breath occasionally brushed past her ear, and warmth radiated from his chest against her back.

She half-closed her eyes in comfort. Her once-straight back gradually leaned against Wei Qi’s embrace.

Her soft body willingly leaned into him—something that would have been impossible before.

Wei Qi’s hands paused. He placed his palm on her shoulder and looked down at her, completely unguarded, as she leaned against him, seemingly asleep. His breath hitched.

His body moved closer to her on its own, his eyes fixed solely on her slightly parted lips.

She would even take the initiative to lean into his chest.

Wei Qi swallowed hard, but he was careful not to disturb her. Slowly, he laid her down on the bed.

But then, Xi Rongyan dreamed again. She was pinned beneath a tall man, the candlelight dim, surrounded by heavy, oppressive curtains.

All she could see was the rise and fall of the man’s broad chest, marked with a faint, familiar scar. She reached out to touch it, only to realize her hands were firmly pinned above her head, unable to move.

Fear gradually took hold of her heart. She became aware of the dull, deep aches across her body. She struggled to lift her head to see the man’s face, but all she could make out was a pair of ferocious, lust-filled eyes.

They glowed with a crimson light, like a savage beast ready to devour her.

Terrified, she let out a soft cry, her voice trembling and choked.

"Spare me—"

Wei Qi frowned as he looked at the woman in his arms. Her hands pushed against his chest, her legs kicking at him, tears glistening at the corners of her eyes.

In that moment, Wei Qi felt as if he were seeing Xi Rongyan from his past life—she would struggle the moment he came near.

Even now, asleep, her body instinctively resisted his approach.

Even though she had not married Gu Yunyu, did she still despise him this much?

His expression darkened gradually. The hand resting against her cheek trembled slightly, veins rising beneath his skin.

Memories from the past surged forward, and Wei Qi knew he was losing control of his emotions.

He wanted to wake her and demand to know—what was it about him that was inferior to Gu Yunyu?

But just then, Xi Rongyan suddenly awoke, her tearful eyes blinking open.

The man before her was blurry; she couldn’t see his expression clearly. His large silhouette only filled her with fear.

She instinctively thought she was still dreaming and tried to move away, but a large hand supported her shoulder, pressing her into a warm embrace.

Gentle fingers soothed her back, and a deep voice whispered near her neck: "Yan’er, did you have a nightmare?"

The voice was familiar. The powerful heartbeat near her ear, the gentle touch on her back—all of it gradually eased her tension. She looked up, and through her tear-blurred vision, she saw a pair of concerned eyes gazing down at her.

Tears slid from the corners of her eyes down to her temples. She blinked, and the man before her came into focus.

She stared at him, and in that moment, a sense of grievance welled up inside her. She pouted, then buried her face in Wei Qi’s chest, wrapping her arms tightly around his waist as she whispered tremulously, "I’m scared…"

Wei Qi gently stroked Xi Rongyan’s soft hair. In the dim light, he pressed his lips tightly together, patiently soothing her until the person in his arms gradually calmed.

Xi Rongyan, immersed in the Emperor’s tenderness, no longer feared him as much. She looked up again and saw the Emperor also looking down at her. The white robe on his shoulder had been tugged down by her, exposing his skin to the cold night air.

It was still March, and the nights were still chilly.

Yet the Emperor held her and soothed her, not knowing how long he had been doing so.

She only realized now that the Emperor’s embrace was so warm.

She bit her lip, then lowered her head, speaking softly: "Did this concubine just offend Your Majesty?"

Wei Qi felt the fingers gripping his clothes tighten slightly. He sighed softly, then held her as he lay down on the bed, his long fingers gently wiping away the lingering tears at the corners of her eyes. Looking at her flushed eyes, he spoke gently: "Did I scare you?"

Xi Rongyan blinked in surprise, shook her head, then lowered her gaze and whispered, "This concubine just had a nightmare."

Wei Qi wrapped his arm around her waist, pulling her body close to his, his voice hoarse yet tenderly coaxing: "What nightmare?"

Xi Rongyan’s gaze was fixed on the Emperor’s exposed collarbone. She parted her lips, then hesitated.

She couldn’t very well say she had dreamed of a fierce, unknown man…

She still didn’t tell the truth, her voice barely audible: "This concubine dreamed… that a tiger bit me."

The moment the words left her lips, a low chuckle came from the Emperor.

She looked up in surprise, only to see the Emperor’s eyes filled with amusement, followed by a sudden rush of warm breath.

The Emperor leaned down toward her, and her cheeks flushed with heat.

Her face was cupped in the Emperor’s large hand, and she heard his deep voice: "So Yan’er is afraid of tigers. From now on, I will stay with you at night. If you’re scared, just hold onto me."

Xi Rongyan stared blankly into the Emperor’s eyes. Such tenderness made her feel a momentary daze.

Unconsciously, she softly hummed in agreement.

The Emperor lightly bumped his forehead against hers, then pulled her tightly into his embrace. From above her head came his sigh: "Yan’er is always so timid. From now on, rely on me."

"I will never let anyone harm you."

In that moment, Xi Rongyan was truly warmed by the Emperor’s affection. She genuinely felt that the Emperor was being kind to her.

Her hand hesitated for a moment before gently wrapping around the Emperor’s waist, a shy response.

That careful, voluntary gesture made Wei Qi’s eyes flicker.

This was the first time Xi Rongyan had taken the initiative to hug him. His emotions surged—this feeling, more than forcing her, was something he couldn’t resist.

This was what he wanted, what he sought.

Wei Qi’s fingers trembled slightly with excitement. His burning gaze fixed on the person in his arms: "May I kiss you?"

---

chapters.title: Long Admired
chapters.content:
The Emperor’s scorching breath fell upon her face, his fingers still caressing her cheek.

His eyes were gentle, as if he were carefully protecting her, even asking permission to kiss her.

Yet he was the exalted Emperor, the Son of Heaven.

Xi Rongyan’s mind was in turmoil. In a daze, she nodded unconsciously.

Her cheeks felt hot—perhaps the Emperor’s gaze was too intense. She couldn’t bear it and shyly averted her eyes.

But in the next moment, her chin was lifted, her lips captured by the Emperor’s. A heavy shadow fell over her as he pressed her beneath him.

She cautiously opened her eyes, only to see his long, narrow eyes watching her. She quickly closed hers again.

The Emperor kissed her gently, tracing her lips as if tempting her, then moved to her chin and further down.

Xi Rongyan’s body trembled as she felt her collar being pulled open. The exposed skin chilled slightly before being covered by his scorching breath.

The damp kisses stirred unfamiliar, strange heat within her. Tears welled in her eyes, and she instinctively resisted, trying to evade.

Wei Qi’s dark gaze took in the fair, jade-like beauty before him. From the corner of his eye, he observed Xi Rongyan’s reactions. When his lips reached her collarbone, he stopped.

Though if he pulled her collar just a little more, the sight he longed to see would be fully revealed.

Countless nights he had yearned for this body, but now Wei Qi understood—he wanted Xi Rongyan to willingly, happily accept him.

He was meticulous and patient, knowing when to stop. From her slight evasive movement, he knew she wasn’t ready.

He tightened his hold on her waist and kissed her lips again, entwining with her. She didn’t resist, and that was enough.

Yet no matter how much Wei Qi restrained himself, he couldn’t suppress his body’s natural reaction.

Afraid of scaring her, he slightly lifted himself, only then allowing his body to react freely.

The aching, tingling sensation was torture, yet in that pain, he savored the joy of kissing his beloved.

The night deepened. Xi Rongyan felt that the Emperor’s kisses were starting to hurt.

She was also struggling to breathe.

She pushed against his chest and began to move restlessly.

She heard the Emperor let out a muffled groan. When she opened her eyes, she saw sweat on his forehead, his eyes closed as if in great pain.

She panicked and asked, "Your Majesty, what’s wrong?"

Wei Qi opened his eyes and looked at Xi Rongyan’s confused, flustered expression. Enduring the pain below, he only said softly, "Nothing."

With that, he got up and ordered the palace attendants outside to bring water, then wrapped his robe around himself and walked out.

Xi Rongyan stared at the Emperor’s retreating figure for a long time, unable to comprehend what had happened.

But she was already extremely tired. She yawned, pulled the blanket tightly around herself, and without waiting for the Emperor to return, closed her eyes and fell asleep.

When Wei Qi returned after his bath, he saw the person curled up under the blanket and smiled helplessly.

He approached and lifted the blanket. Perhaps a cold draft had entered, for the person inside instinctively leaned toward him.

Even asleep, she was obedient, pressing her head tightly against his chest, her hand as if it had eyes, gripping his sleeve firmly.

Wei Qi couldn’t help but soften his expression. His gaze traced her features, his fingers brushing her cheek—soft, plump, and smooth.

Asleep, Xi Rongyan looked rather adorable.

He recalled the Xi Rongyan from his past life. Even as a mother, her eyes remained clear and innocent, still naive about the ways of the world.

In truth, she hadn’t changed much. Her appearance in his heart had never really changed.

Wei Qi lowered his head slightly to inhale her scent. His fingers couldn’t resist sliding toward her waist, but he forced himself to stop, merely pulling her tightly into his embrace.

When Xi Rongyan woke the next morning, she was startled by what was pressing against her back.

She suddenly remembered the booklet Yu Zhu had shown her and the words her mother had taught her, and her face flushed crimson.

She carefully tried to scoot forward, but the arm around her waist pulled her back forcefully. She froze, not daring to move.

She suddenly felt a sense of relief—thankfully, the Emperor had only held her.

Behind her, Wei Qi smiled, his eyes curving.

He didn’t tease her further. Instead, he turned her over and looked at her blood-red cheeks, raising an eyebrow as he deliberately asked, "What’s wrong? Why is your face so red?"

Xi Rongyan wished she could find a hole to crawl into. She stammered for an excuse: "I-I’m a little hot…"

Wei Qi smiled, looking at the small face framed by dark hair. He found Xi Rongyan’s current shyness and innocence increasingly adorable—more tempting than a flower bud.

His gaze darkened as he looked at her slightly parted red lips, but he only lightly kissed her forehead, indulging her: "Sleep a little more."

"You don’t have to go to the Empress if you don’t want to."

Xi Rongyan’s eyes widened as she looked at Wei Qi. How could she not go to the Empress?

Her almond-shaped eyes were wide, glistening like morning dew on flowers. Wei Qi smiled: "You didn’t sleep well last night. It’s fine if you don’t go."

"I’ll have someone inform the Empress."

Xi Rongyan paused for a moment, then wanted to ask why the Emperor was so kind to her.

But what came out of her mouth was: "That day at the Flower Festival, did this concubine do something to offend Your Majesty?"

Wei Qi’s dark eyes flickered. Hearing Xi Rongyan bring this up now, he let out a low laugh, his fingers resting on her waist as he asked, "Yan’er doesn’t remember?"

Xi Rongyan bit her lip and shook her head.

She truly couldn’t remember a thing.

Wei Qi smiled: "That day, Yan’er held onto me tightly and even took the initiative to kiss me."

As he spoke, he sighed: "I tried to stop you, but Yan’er came closer and said you had admired me for a long time, wanting to offer your—"

Before he could finish, his lips were covered by a soft, fair, and fragrant hand.

Wei Qi’s dark eyes looked at the person whose ears were now completely red. He watched as she loosened her hand, then buried her face in the blanket, her muffled voice like a mosquito’s buzz: "Your Majesty… can you forget about it…?"

Wei Qi chuckled softly. He had never realized how shy and adorable Xi Rongyan could be.

He had always thought she was conservative, dignified, and a little stubborn.

He lifted a corner of the blanket and saw a sliver of her profile—fair as a magnolia, her earlobe slightly red.

His long fingers traced it, and he said softly, "Yan’er need not be shy. I also admire you."

"Have for a long time."

Xi Rongyan, buried in the blanket, froze. She turned her head and saw the Emperor looking at her with a smile in his eyes.

His deep gaze seemed to hold the same tenderness as when Gu Yunyu used to look at her. She felt a little lost, her heart pounding rapidly.

The Emperor said he admired her too.

Had for a long time.

But between her and the Emperor…

Her mind went blank, unsure how to react.

Before she could collect her thoughts, the shadow above her pressed down again. She was pulled tightly into that warm embrace, and from above her head came the Emperor’s hoarse voice: "I only wish that Yan’er truly admires me as you said that day."

"I will not let you down. I will slowly give you all the honor and glory."

"Yan’er only needs to trust me."

chapters.title: You Are the Only One I Love
chapters.content:
The dim, warm light bathed everything in a gentle glow.

Above her was the Emperor’s scorching breath, and before her eyes was his broad chest.

Her heart skipped a beat— the Emperor she remembered had gradually become a stranger.

The Emperor before her was so gentle that it felt as if her memories had gone astray.

A shy blush spread across her face uncontrollably. Her slender fingers pressed lightly into the silk, and she lost herself in his tender words, forgetting even to respond.

Her eyes shimmered like sea tang blossoms swaying in the wind, delicate and trembling, stirring the heart.

Wei Qi gazed at Xi Rongyan’s flushed, distracted face, already deeply satisfied.

He asked for nothing else— only that she not fear him.

If not for the ongoing war in the north that required stabilizing, he might have already arranged for her to be crowned Empress, so she could wholeheartedly trust him.

But it didn’t matter. One day, she would see his sincerity.

In the past, she had hated him with all her heart, blind to every kindness he showed her. Now, given a second chance, he was certain she would come to recognize his goodness.

Yet, the urgent calls from Gao Yi outside interrupted them. Wei Qi felt a rare flicker of impatience.

He had never disliked rising early before.

With a lingering reluctance, he finally pulled away, got up, and began dressing— without asking Xi Rongyan to help him.

Xi Rongyan watched the Emperor’s retreating figure, his words still echoing in her mind, leaving her dazed.

She quickly regained her senses and stood up. Even though the Emperor hadn’t asked her to help him dress, as his concubine, she couldn’t forget her duties.

Xi Rongyan had never been one to rely on favor or make mistakes. She followed him out.

Outside, she saw the palace attendants helping Wei Qi into his outer robes. The black dragon robe, embroidered with golden threads, draped over him. His back was to the candlelight, half his face hidden in shadow— noble and majestic.

Even though the Emperor had just spoken so gently, now, without a smile, he appeared stern and distant, almost unapproachable.

Xi Rongyan steadied her thoughts and was about to step forward when she felt his deep, dark eyes settle on her.

The coldness in his expression melted instantly, and he beckoned her over with a smile. “Yan’er.”

Xi Rongyan softly acknowledged him and took a step forward— only for warmth to envelop her.

The Emperor had pulled her into his embrace.

Wei Qi held her slender frame, gently tucking a loose strand of hair behind her ear. His voice was laced with concern. “The spring chill lingers. Don’t get up so early next time.”

Xi Rongyan placed her fingers on his chest, lightly tracing the dragon embroidery, and in the most submissive manner a concubine could, she whispered, “This concubine wishes to dress Your Majesty.”

Wei Qi stared at Xi Rongyan for a long moment. He had never imagined the day would come when she would willingly dress him.

Even if he knew she might only be doing this because of her current status, a flicker of joy still stirred in his heart.

As long as she was willing to draw near to him, it was enough.

But Wei Qi knew she was sensitive to the cold— even in summer, her hands were chilled.

The sky was still dark outside. It pained him to have her wake so early just to dress him. He couldn’t bear it.

With a sigh, he scooped her up and carried her back to the bed.

He set her down on the bed and gazed at her enchanting face. Her black hair fanned out across the pillow, and the soft light caught the glimmer in her eyes. His fingers sank into her hair as he inhaled deeply, savoring her scent before hoarsely saying, “From now on, you need not rise with me. As I’ve told you, between us, it is as with an ordinary husband and wife.”

“I am not the Son of Heaven before you, nor the Emperor. You need not fear me or seek my favor.”

As he spoke, Wei Qi leaned down and kissed the corner of Xi Rongyan’s lips. His fingers brushed her cheek as he whispered, “Yan’er, you are the only one I truly love. Every word I say to you is from my heart.”

Wei Qi gave her one last deep look before straightening up and leaving at Gao Yi’s next urgent call.

After the Emperor left, Xi Rongyan unconsciously propped herself up. The blanket slipped to her waist, and her waist-length black hair spilled over her chest. In a daze, she touched her cheek, where the warmth of the Emperor’s gentle caress still lingered, faintly scorching.

Yu Zhu entered from outside and, seeing Xi Rongyan’s distracted state, happily exclaimed, “Mistress, His Majesty truly favors you!”

Then, carefully, she asked, “Last night, His Majesty called for water… Did His Majesty… bestow his favor upon you?”

Xi Rongyan snapped out of her reverie and looked at Yu Zhu, softly replying, “His Majesty has not touched me.”

Yu Zhu blinked, stunned. “His Majesty hasn’t… for two nights?”

Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze, her fingertips tracing the hidden embroidery on the silk quilt. Her expression remained calm as she softly said, “Don’t worry. I understand.”

Because she could see that the Emperor was considering her feelings by not touching her— not that he didn’t want to.

So she wasn’t anxious.

Yu Zhu, however, was deeply worried. “How could His Majesty not…?”

She wanted to ask if His Majesty had some hidden ailment.

After all, Mistress had been renowned for her beauty even before entering the palace. It was impossible for His Majesty not to desire her.

Xi Rongyan glanced at Yu Zhu, as if sensing her wild thoughts, and softly said, “Don’t ask. Go fetch some water for me to freshen up.”

“And have Bao Zhu come help me dress.”

Yu Zhu quickly nodded and turned to fetch water and call for Bao Zhu.

---

Wei Qi returned to Xuan Zheng Hall, where candles already filled the hall, casting a bright glow.

A few trusted ministers for the morning court session were already waiting outside. Wei Qi stood with his hands behind his back, gazing out the window, and quietly ordered, “Every word Zhen Pin speaks when paying respects to the Empress today must be reported back to me, without omission.”

Wei Qi understood Xi Rongyan well. Even though he had told her she didn’t need to go to the Empress, he knew her nature— she was meticulous and rule-abiding, and would certainly go.

Recalling the flush in her eyes yesterday, he wondered what kind of humiliation she had endured among those women.

Gao Yi was long used to the Emperor’s unusual concern for Zhen Pin. Even if the Emperor were to depose the Empress and install Zhen Pin in her place, he wouldn’t find it strange.

After all, the Emperor, who had never been hurried in the mornings, had already been rushed several times because of Zhen Pin.

Such a scene had never occurred in any other palace.

With a respectful “Yes,” Gao Yi quickly went to make the arrangements.

Wei Qi then summoned Ling Gu Gu from Han Yuan Palace for questioning.

Ling Gu Gu arrived swiftly, bowing her head, her heart pounding as she awaited the Emperor’s questions.

Wei Qi glanced indifferently at the kneeling figure before calmly asking about everything Xi Rongyan had done since yesterday until this morning.

---

chapters.title: Special Favor
chapters.content:
Ling Gu Gu recounted in meticulous detail everything Xi Rongyan had done in Han Yuan Palace from the previous day until this morning.

Wei Qi’s fingers traced the ring on his thumb, thinking that once the northern war was over, it would be time to clean up the women in the rear palace.

Meanwhile, Xi Rongyan had indeed prepared to visit the Empress.

She had always been one to uphold propriety and couldn’t possibly refuse to go, lest she draw even more attention from the others in the rear palace.

However, when she stepped outside, a palanquin was waiting for her. Still, she did not board it.

According to regulations, only those of concubine rank or higher were permitted to use a palanquin within the palace; others required special imperial favor.

As she walked, she spotted Qi Fei in the distance, seated in her palanquin, with Xie Yu Min walking attentively behind her.

Seeing this, Xi Rongyan didn’t know what to feel— only then did she understand why her cousin had come to her palace the day before.

A thought suddenly struck her: if the Emperor hadn’t arranged for her to live alone in Guan Ju Palace, would she, too, have to tread so carefully? She didn’t think so.

Qi Fei was an old companion from the Emperor’s princely days, held high rank, and was close to the Empress. Though these advantages allowed her to act boldly, they were a double-edged sword— sooner or later, they would cut her as well.

From her palanquin, Qi Fei had already noticed Xi Rongyan. She saw her in a crescent-white orchid cloak, her hair adorned with only two jade ornaments, her ears still bearing that pair of jadeite earrings.

Standing there quietly, her face was soft, her fine brows and red lips giving her a delicate, graceful allure— yet in Qi Fei’s eyes, it was infuriating.

She muttered under her breath, calling her a vixen.

Who knew what tricks she had used in bed to ensnare the Emperor, yet she still put on an act of purity.

Lifting her chin, Qi Fei seemed to look down on someone like Xi Rongyan. When she saw Xi Rongyan bow to her, she gave her a cold glance and passed by without a word.

Xi Rongyan hadn’t heard Qi Fei’s insult. She waited for Xie Yu Min, who had been following behind.

Xie Yu Min saw Xi Rongyan waiting for her, but hesitation flickered in her heart.

Yesterday, after visiting Xi Rongyan, she had been summoned by Qi Fei, who had mocked her coldly. Not only that, but her allowances had been cut.

In the rear palace, almost everyone was loyal to the Empress. The servants of the Imperial Household Department were used to flattering the powerful and bullying the weak, reading the situation carefully. At Qi Fei’s command, they would secretly cause trouble— sending damaged or inferior goods, or cold food.

Everything in the rear palace was under the Empress’s control. The Emperor had never once visited her, so no matter how great her suffering, she had to endure it alone.

Now, if Qi Fei saw her speaking with Xi Rongyan again, she would likely face more mistreatment afterward.

But she understood Xi Rongyan— she had never been malicious. It was she, Xie Yu Min, who had changed after two years of hardship in the palace.

If she had known back then that the Emperor, who had once been the envy of all, would turn out to be so cold and indifferent, she never would have harbored such ambitions.

Once, she had been renowned among the noble ladies of the capital, proud and haughty, believing she would surely be the exceptional one.

She had thought that once she entered the palace, she would certainly gain the Emperor’s favor and bring glory to her family.

Now, all those hopes were dead.

She could only bitterly laugh at her past ignorance.

Xi Rongyan noticed the hesitation on Xie Yu Min’s face, then saw her cautiously glance at Qi Fei ahead, whose expression was cold as she looked back at Xie Yu Min.

Xi Rongyan paused slightly, understanding her cousin’s concerns.

She didn’t wait any longer and started walking forward. But then Xie Yu Min called out to her from behind, “Mei Mei.”

Xi Rongyan turned around and saw Xie Yu Min approaching. Noticing her expression, she couldn’t help but ask softly, “Sister, do you have concerns about walking with me? I don’t want to implicate you.”

Xie Yu Min was taken aback— so she had seen through her.

She looked into Xi Rongyan’s clear, bright eyes.

Those almond-shaped eyes, so distinct in their black and white, always made people feel as if they were the closest to her.

Back in their maiden days, it was often said that anyone who looked into Xi Rongyan’s eyes would come to like her. Xie Yu Min had once admired them too, but now, they stirred a strange feeling in her.

Recalling how the Emperor had even come to share a midday meal with her yesterday, a strange desolation rose in her heart.

She forced a smile and walked alongside Xi Rongyan. “It’s nothing. Everyone knows how close we are.”

Xi Rongyan nodded slightly, but the words felt like a lump in her throat.

Xie Yu Min then asked, “Did everything go well last night when you attended His Majesty?”

Her gaze flickered over the faint marks on Xi Rongyan’s collarbone as she smiled. “His Majesty must cherish you greatly.”

Xi Rongyan shook her head at Xie Yu Min’s sudden question. “Sister, don’t tease me.”

Xie Yu Min smiled, feeling a little foolish for asking.

Xi Rongyan then softly said to Xie Yu Min, “Yesterday, I asked His Majesty about having you come stay with me. But he said he would think about it. I don’t know if he will agree.”

Xie Yu Min looked at Xi Rongyan’s earnest expression, then lowered her head and softly said, “It’s fine.”

Then she asked, “Will His Majesty visit you again tonight?”

Xi Rongyan shook her head again. “I don’t know.”

Xie Yu Min glanced at the faint marks on Xi Rongyan’s neck and pressed her lips together.

In the two years since she had entered the palace, the Emperor had only visited her once.

He hadn’t even touched her— he had only sat with her for a while before leaving.

She had exhausted every trick she knew, to no avail. To this day, she still didn’t understand what she had done that night to displease him.

Xie Yu Min forced another smile and fell silent.

When they reached the Empress’s palace, Xie Yu Min gently pushed Xi Rongyan’s hand and whispered, “Mei Mei, your position is higher. Walk ahead.”

Xi Rongyan glanced at Xie Yu Min’s expression and nodded, walking ahead.

They weren’t the last to arrive, but as soon as Xi Rongyan entered, she felt the gazes of the others fixed on her.

Strangely, though, the women who had mocked her coldly yesterday were unusually quiet today.

She approached the Empress and respectfully greeted her. The Empress smiled and gestured for her to take a seat to the side.

Xi Rongyan removed her cloak, handed it to Bao Zhu behind her, and sat down. Across from her, Qi Fei glanced at Xi Rongyan before looking away.

She scanned the others— though their expressions weren’t warm, they were unusually quiet.

In that moment, Xi Rongyan understood.

These women all took their cues from the Empress.

Yesterday, it had been the Empress’s people who spoke first, and only then did the others follow.

Today, since the Empress’s people remained silent, they didn’t dare speak either.

Once everyone had arrived, the Empress began her daily lecture on etiquette and rules.

Empress Song carried a natural, composed demeanor, sitting upright as she spoke, commanding respect.

Xi Rongyan looked around and roughly grasped the hierarchy.

The Four Consorts and the Empress had all been with the Emperor since his days as a prince. Qi Fei and Xian Fei were both daughters of northern generals, naturally aligned with the Empress.

No wonder everyone was so obedient to the Empress.

No wonder her aunt had said that the rear palace was entirely under the Empress’s control.

Xi Rongyan didn’t find this strange. The Empress was, after all, the Empress— the Emperor’s childhood sweetheart and wife. She had even borne the first imperial son, and her family was illustrious. No one could shake her position.

She understood why the Empress subtly made things difficult for her, but she couldn’t help sighing at the Empress’s lack of tolerance.

From her seat, the Empress occasionally cast glances at Xi Rongyan before suddenly speaking. “Zhen Pin, you stay.”

chapters.title: Imperial Favor
chapters.content:
As soon as Xi Rongyan heard the Empress ask her to stay again, she knew the Empress must be asking about Consort Xian once more.
