The hot steam swirled above the bath, beading sweat on Xi Rongyan’s forehead. This place filled her with an inexplicable dread.

As if a pair of cold, merciless eyes were watching her from the mist.

Binding her here.

Then she looked at the bath before her, and in the steam, she seemed to see unspeakable scenes.

The glass platform by the pool—she felt as if she had dreamed of it before. She had once been pinned down there by that terrifying man.

Her heart fluttered with unease. She didn’t want to enter the water. She looked around, but the curtains were filled with white mist and burning incense. She couldn’t see Yuzhu or Baozhu anywhere.

Wearing only her innermost undergarments and thick trousers, goosebumps rose on her skin. Yet she called out for Baozhu, wanting her to stay.

The hanging curtains swayed slightly, revealing a shadow behind them. Her heart relaxed—until she lifted the curtain and saw it wasn’t Baozhu.

Emperor Wei Qi stood before her, dressed in dark robes, his golden crown glinting faintly. His sharp, phoenix-like eyes beneath his sword-like brows were both fierce and unfathomable.

His gaze was dark and deep.

The lantern light reflected in the Emperor’s eyes, making his noble features seem both refined and alien.

For a moment, she thought of the golden dragon carved on the wall.

And of a pair of cold, merciless eyes.

She instinctively took a step back, only to find herself falling into a warm embrace.

The Emperor’s large hand rested on her exposed shoulder, his wide sleeve shielding her. He lowered his head, concern in his voice. “What’s wrong? Don’t you like it here?”

Xi Rongyan met the Emperor’s worried gaze, and the chill that had settled in her body seemed to warm again.

She suppressed her unease and lightly shook her head.

Wei Qi sighed, gently cupping her face. “At night, when I hold you, your hands are always cold.”

“I asked the imperial physician. He said soaking in warm water would help.”

As he spoke, Wei Qi tightened his grip on her hand. “You may come here anytime. There will always be attendants ready.”

The sudden unease that had risen in Xi Rongyan’s heart unexpectedly settled.

She had always had cold hands, yet the Emperor had noticed even this small detail.

Touched, she looked at him and softly said, “This concubine thanks Your Majesty.”

Wei Qi gazed at her dewy eyes, smiled, then kissed her forehead before pulling her toward the bath.

He led her into the water but remained seated on the edge, silently watching.

Xi Rongyan felt strange being alone in the bath while the Emperor watched. She couldn’t relax.

Hesitating, she asked, “Your Majesty, won’t you bathe as well?”

Wei Qi’s dark eyes studied her. “Do you want me to join you?”

Xi Rongyan faltered. In her mind, she weighed the difference between the Emperor watching her bathe and bathing with him. There didn’t seem to be much difference.

Besides, she couldn’t very well say she didn’t want him to.

She steeled herself and nodded.

Wei Qi smiled, then began undressing in front of her.

Xi Rongyan couldn’t bear to watch. She quickly turned away.

By the time she came to her senses, a firm chest pressed against her back.

The Emperor had turned her around in his embrace. The steam swirled around them, her cheeks burning. She lowered her head, and under his scorching breath, she didn’t dare lift her eyelids.

Her gaze fell on his bare chest, where droplets of water slid downward.

But her eyes fixed on a red mark on the left side of his chest—exactly where the man in her dreams had a scar.

She paused, her fingers unconsciously reaching out to trace it.

The touch was real, eerily similar to the sensation in her dreams.

Wei Qi was startled when her hand touched his chest. He took a deep breath, then captured her fingers.

Xi Rongyan looked up at him, seeing the complexity in his gaze as he studied her. It made her inexplicably nervous.

She thought of the scar on his chest.

It was no wonder Wei Qi couldn’t take his eyes off her. At this moment, Xi Rongyan, in his eyes, was more tempting than ever.

His gaze didn’t drift lower.

If he did, he wouldn’t be able to resist.

Her pink undergarment, embroidered with butterflies and flowers, clung to her body. Her black hair cascaded over it. With just a glance, he could imagine countless alluring scenes.

In his past life, she had been so modest, always covering herself, never letting him see her properly.

Once, he had been so angry—she was already his, her husband was dead, even the Gu family had accepted her as his. What was she still hiding?

They had shared intimacy many times, but at first, he had restrained himself out of respect for her modesty. Later, he had truly been angry with her.

That time, he had stripped her bare and bound her to the bed, forcing her to watch as he examined every inch of her skin.

That night had been pleasurable for him, but afterward, she had grown colder toward him.

Cold as ice.

She hadn’t spoken a single word to him.

Later, Wei Qi had regretted it.

Regretted his impatience.

He had known she was modest by nature, yet his own insecurity had driven him to force her acceptance.

If he had been more patient with her, perhaps their relationship wouldn’t have deteriorated into such an irreparable state.

Now, Wei Qi didn’t dare push her even a little. Even the smallest touch required him to gauge her mood.

At this moment, her full, red lips exuded a sweet fragrance. The jade earrings swayed slightly. Amidst the mist, she was like moonlight on clouds, a hibiscus on a branch—so beautiful he dared not touch, lest he disturb her.

Wei Qi swallowed hard, his body leaning down. He truly didn’t know how much longer he could resist not touching her.

He reached for a jade cup from the tray on the shore. It contained peach blossom tea.

She liked it, so he had come to like it too.

He brought the cup to her lips, his gaze fixed on her red lips, his voice hoarse. “Are you thirsty?”

The Emperor had already brought the cup to her lips. Xi Rongyan hesitated for a moment before nodding and taking a sip.

The water glistened on her lips like enticing ripples. The cup slipped from her fingers into the bath. Wei Qi could no longer restrain himself. He lowered his head and kissed her lips.

Xi Rongyan’s back pressed against the edge of the pool. As if afraid she might be hurt, the Emperor quickly placed his hand behind her back for support.

Though Xi Rongyan was extremely shy, she repeatedly told herself to act naturally.

Her aunt had said that once she entered the palace, she would belong to the Emperor. What was there to be shy about?

She tilted her head back, and in the Emperor’s kiss, she could no longer think clearly.

The steam made her dizzy. She closed her eyes and recalled Yuzhu’s words from earlier.

It was bound to happen sooner or later.

Her heart wrestled with itself. She should forget everything from the past.

Her fingertips trembled, then settled on the Emperor’s back—a shy, tentative response.

When Xi Rongyan’s fingers touched his back, Wei Qi sharply inhaled.

He looked down at her half-closed eyes, at the flushed blush on her cheeks and eyelids, so alluring it stirred his soul.

He could no longer control himself. Holding Xi Rongyan, he stepped out of the bath and headed straight for the inner chamber’s bedchamber.

---

chapters.title: First Night
chapters.content:
A trail of water droplets fell onto the smooth jade tiles, spreading toward the golden-lacquered and kingfisher-feather inlaid glass screen.

The screen reflected the intertwined figures within. The palace attendants had silently withdrawn.

Xi Rongyan, completely bare, was wrapped in a brocade quilt. Dazed, she watched as the Emperor sat on the edge of the bed, his bare upper body pressing down toward her, his rapid breath washing over her.

She heard his hoarse question: “May I touch you?”

Xi Rongyan’s face burned crimson, her eyes shimmering with moisture. His direct question only deepened her shyness.

She bit her lip almost to the point of drawing blood, her fingers clutching the quilt tightly. She averted her gaze, unable to meet his eyes, but gave a very subtle nod.

At this moment, her heart was racing so much that she couldn’t recall any of the advice Yuzhu had given her.

She only knew that her fate was sealed. Struggling was useless.

She couldn’t say whether she truly accepted it or not.

Or perhaps it was because the man before her was the Emperor.

Wei Qi lowered his head, his lips gently pressing against hers, as if trying to soothe her anxiety.

He whispered, “I’ll be gentle. If it hurts, tell me.”

Xi Rongyan’s head still spun as if floating on clouds. She gave a muffled “mm” in response, then quickly glanced at him.

Seeing his dark eyes fixed on her, she hastily closed her own.

Wei Qi smiled at her shy, timid demeanor. One hand removed his damp trousers. Patiently, he began kissing her from her collarbone downward.

He had imagined doing this countless times—kissing her, cherishing her. Unfortunately, such opportunities had been rare.

Because she had rarely allowed it without resistance.

He knew the body beneath him was trembling. He, too, was tense.

He could only explore her cautiously, afraid his actions might displease her.

Yet, though his intent was to please her, it was he who struggled to maintain control.

The flickering lamplight cast shadows. Sweat beaded on Wei Qi’s back.

His fingers trembled.

His dark eyes observed her emotions, his half-lidded gaze deep and inscrutable.

He asked softly, “Is this alright now?”

Xi Rongyan only felt an indescribable heat throughout her body. Squinting, her vision of the man before her was blurred. All she could clearly perceive was the deep, low sound of his voice.

She parted her lips, softly and shyly murmuring, “Mm.”

Wei Qi, gazing at those bright, moist eyes, let out a low breath and pressed down.

Xi Rongyan also felt tormented. She wanted to say stop, but forced herself to endure.

Her mother had told her before she entered the palace: endure it, and it would be over.

She just hadn’t expected it to last this long.

Suddenly, she let out a soft cry. Her hand pressed against Wei Qi’s chest, tears welling in her eyes.

Wei Qi froze, quickly bending down to soothe her. “I’ll be even gentler.”

Xi Rongyan, tears in her eyes, pushed against his shoulder, nodding as she endured.

But Wei Qi couldn’t bear to see her endure like this.

He had seen her like this countless times before, and he never wanted her to suffer again.

He wanted her to desire him as fiercely as he desired her.

He gently soothed her, drenched in sweat, yet observing her every expression, not wanting to leave her with an unpleasant impression.

The palace lantern by the bed swayed, only a few flickering candlelights remaining. The screen still reflected their figures.

By the time faint sounds of palace attendants stirred outside the curtains the next morning, Xi Rongyan was deeply asleep, buried in Wei Qi’s embrace.

Wei Qi held her, reluctant to get up.

He knew she probably wasn’t feeling well. In truth, he had only taken her once the previous night, spending more time comforting her.

He had added a bit of aphrodisiac incense to the fragrance, not much—just enough to ease her discomfort.

The woman in his arms was completely bare, a faint flush still lingering on her cheeks. Damp strands of hair clung to her face as she slightly lowered her head, snuggling tightly against his chest.

His expression softened—a rare sight.

Her shallow breaths brushed against his chest, a pleasant, tingling sensation. He lowered his head, reveling in the soft warmth of her body.

In his past life, they had rarely shared a bed peacefully. She wouldn’t let him hold her, always turning her back to him.

In truth, Wei Qi had never wanted to hurt her. If she had been even a little more obedient, he wouldn’t have used force.

But Wei Qi understood that in their past life, an immense chasm had divided them—a scar in her heart, and indeed, he had employed underhanded means. He had wronged her.

It was only natural that she hated him.

Outside, Gao Yi’s cautious voice urged again. Wei Qi lowered his eyelids, looking at the woman in his arms, his fingers twitching slightly.

He had clothes brought in and personally dressed her, covering the faint red marks on her skin.

Wei Qi was meticulous, his movements gentle, not waking her.

The nearby palace attendants didn’t dare watch this scene, retreating to a corner.

Wei Qi tucked the brocade quilt back around Xi Rongyan and quietly left.

Outside, Gao Yi had been too afraid to urge further. Many people were already waiting at Xuanzheng Hall. If the Emperor didn’t arrive soon, he didn’t know what to do.

Now, seeing the Emperor finally emerge, he let out a huge sigh of relief.

Wei Qi stood at the palace doorway, hands clasped behind his back. His gaze slanted downward, glancing at Gao Yi. “Go to the Empress yourself and inform her that Zhen Pin will not be paying her respects today.”

Gao Yi let out an “eh?” and looked up, only to find the Emperor already boarding the palanquin.

Baozhu and Yuzhu, who had been waiting outside the hall all night, wanted to enter upon seeing the Emperor leave. Gao Yi stopped them. “Let Zhen Pin Consort sleep a little longer.”

“This is a place where His Majesty usually bathes and rests. No one comes here.”

Yuzhu asked worriedly, “But what if we’re late to the Empress Dowager’s greetings?”

Gao Yi smiled. “His Majesty has already ordered that Zhen Pin Consort doesn’t need to go today. You two just stay here and watch over her. Let Zhen Pin Consort have a good rest.”

“I’ll go inform the Empress now.”

With that, he smiled and left.

Yuzhu watched Gao Gonggong’s retreating figure, suddenly realizing something.

---

chapters.title: Better Than Her Past Self
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan woke to bright daylight.

Sunlight filtered through the thin curtains, casting a warm glow. Dust motes danced in the air, settling on her thin white undergarment.

She sat up, still feeling a little dizzy. Lowering her head, she pressed her forehead, staring at the strands of hair tangled on the quilt. Her mind was blank.

Until a teacup was presented before her: “Mistress, moisten your throat.”

Xi Rongyan took it somewhat sluggishly, turning to look at Baozhu.

The light hit her eyes, and she squinted slightly, uncomfortable. Then her thoughts returned, and she asked with a start, “What time is it?”

Standing beside her, Yuzhu smiled. “Mistress need not worry. His Majesty had Gao Gonggong inform them—you don’t need to pay respects to the Empress today.”

Xi Rongyan blinked, then relaxed, slowly leaning back against the soft pillow.

She felt as if her entire body lacked strength. A dull ache lingered in her lower abdomen. Even after enduring it, she didn’t feel much better.

Yuzhu’s gaze fell on the red marks on Xi Rongyan’s neck. After a moment’s hesitation, she asked, “Last night… His Majesty…”

Xi Rongyan’s face flushed again. She took a small sip from the teacup, then softly murmured, “Mm.”

Yuzhu finally let out a breath of relief.

It seemed His Majesty was fine.

She added, “Last night was truly your first time attending to His Majesty. His Majesty excused you from greeting the Empress—he pities your condition.”

“His Majesty truly cares for you, Mistress.”

Xi Rongyan couldn’t help but recall last night. Every time the Emperor moved, he had asked her. Though she had been a little annoyed, when she looked into his eyes, it seemed he, too, was suffering, yet he always considered her feelings. It had moved her.

No matter what, the Emperor had been extremely gentle with her.

She softly murmured in agreement, then placed the teacup in Baozhu’s hand beside her, intending to get up.

This was still Chonghua Palace. Staying here always made her uneasy.

As she moved, she still felt uncomfortable—not exactly painful, just a dull ache.

But the book had said it would feel pleasant.

She called for Baozhu to bring her clothes. Baozhu acknowledged and left, only to immediately bump into the Emperor entering. She froze, about to speak, but seeing the Emperor’s indifferent glance, she closed her mouth.

Gao Yi, standing behind the Emperor, waved his hand at her. She hesitated, then quickly withdrew.

Wei Qi’s steps were light. With his hands clasped behind his back, he walked to the other side of the screen. He could clearly hear Xi Rongyan’s soft voice, still hoarse and lazy from just waking. “Is that book just nonsense?”

“Why don’t I feel the slightest bit of pleasure? My body still feels uncomfortable.”

Wei Qi raised an eyebrow.

Inside, Yuzhu laughed. “Mistress, it’s only your first time.”

"Will it be more comfortable the second time?"

"Comfortable how?"

Yu Zhu looked at Xi Rongyan's clear, innocent eyes and helplessly smiled, "My lady, it is you who serves His Majesty."

Xi Rongyan paused, then sighed dejectedly, "I had forgotten. I don’t know how to serve others, nor can I learn those things."

Yu Zhu comforted her, "Just follow the instructions in the manual. Besides, His Majesty may not come here often."

Xi Rongyan then breathed a sigh of relief, "That’s true. Maybe he won’t come next time."

There were so many women in the harem.

Wei Qi raised his eyebrows again.

It seemed that even after being busy for half the night, he still hadn’t served her well.

He wasn’t angry, though. This version of Xi Rongyan was much better than the cold and indifferent one from his past life.

In fact, he found the current Xi Rongyan rather endearing. Wei Qi was nearly ten years older than her, and sometimes when he held her in his arms, he even felt that she needed his care in every way.

In his past life, he had only thought she was delicate and needed protection, but she rarely let him take care of her.

Perhaps back then, she was already a mother, her gentleness more composed, and there was a cold resistance in her demeanor toward him, making her every move more steady.

Inside the room, Yu Zhu was startled by Xi Rongyan’s words and quickly said, "In the future, my lady must not say such things outside. If someone with ill intentions hears and deliberately sows discord, it will be hard to explain."

Xi Rongyan was naturally not so foolish. She had always been cautious with her words outside, and she would not say such things to anyone but those close to her.

She knew that Yu Zhu was the most loyal maid her mother had sent to her side.

Wei Qi only heard Xi Rongyan softly hum in response, then ask about Bao Zhu who had gone to fetch clothes.

Wei Qi, hearing that someone inside was about to come out, finally moved and walked behind the screen.

Xi Rongyan was surprised to see the Emperor suddenly enter. She hadn’t expected His Majesty to come at this time.

Then she thought of her earlier conversation with Yu Zhu and wondered if the Emperor had heard it. Her face paled, feeling a little guilty, and she asked softly, "Your Majesty, why have you come?"

Wei Qi could tell what she was thinking from her expression. He walked to the bedside and sat down, looking at her. "I happened to have some free time, so I came to see you."

As he spoke, Wei Qi subtly observed Xi Rongyan’s expression, then asked, "Did you sleep well?"

Xi Rongyan, hearing that the Emperor still cared for her at this moment, thought that he probably hadn’t heard their earlier conversation, and she secretly felt relieved.

She had rarely slept so long before. Although she didn’t know when she had fallen asleep last night, she had slept peacefully.

She nodded, then looked at the Emperor and thanked him for not going to the Empress’s place this morning.

---

chapters.title: Does It Hurt?
chapters.content:
Yu Zhu was still in the room. Wei Qi glanced at her, and Yu Zhu belatedly realized and quickly left.

After leaving, she ran into Bao Zhu outside and hurriedly asked, "When did His Majesty arrive?"

Bao Zhu didn’t dare to hide the truth, "Just now, when I went out to fetch clothes, he came."

Yu Zhu thought to herself, didn’t that mean His Majesty had heard?

But looking at His Majesty’s face, there was no trace of emotion, and he was still concerned about her lady. It didn’t seem like he had heard anything.

She frowned at Bao Zhu, "His Majesty came, and you didn’t even make a sound?"

Bao Zhu felt wronged, "His Majesty’s gaze is so cold. How would I dare to speak? I was directly asked to leave by Eunuch Gao."

Gao Yi, standing not far away, glanced at the two of them and thought to himself that they were truly tactless. His Majesty wanted to be alone with Precious Consort, so why would they approach?

They even blamed him for it. If he hadn’t asked them to leave, he would have offended His Majesty and suffered the consequences.

His Majesty hadn’t even looked at the memorials. After the morning court, he had hurried here to see Precious Consort, waiting to be intimate with her again.

Inside, Wei Qi had already pulled Xi Rongyan out from the blankets and held her in his lap.

Xi Rongyan realized that His Majesty liked holding her.

Every time he saw her, he would hold her.

Moreover, His Majesty was very considerate. As if afraid she would be cold, he draped his cloak over her shoulders.

Her fingers were held and kneaded by His Majesty, but he didn’t speak. Xi Rongyan also noticed that His Majesty didn’t talk much. Most of the time, he just held her in silence.

She didn’t understand what His Majesty was thinking.

She looked up at him, seeing his chin, his high nose bridge.

She also noticed a faint tear mole at the corner of His Majesty’s eye, making his sharp and handsome features even more striking.

Wei Qi knew Xi Rongyan was looking at him. He lowered his gaze slightly and saw his own reflection in her eyes. He couldn’t help but curl his lips.

He remained silent, allowing her to look at him. In the past, he had longed for her to look at him properly, but now it seemed too easy.

His fingers pinched the soft flesh at her waist. Being scrutinized by her like this, he felt a trace of nervousness.

He found it amusing himself.

Finally, when he saw her lower her head again, he followed suit.

He really wanted to ask her if he looked good, but he felt the question was meaningless.

In his past life, he had asked her many such questions—what was wrong with him. But now, he no longer cared.

The room was quiet again. Wei Qi’s gaze swept over her tense fingers clutching her sleeve, and he covered them with his own before looking down and asking her softly, "Does it hurt?"

Hearing this, Xi Rongyan wished she could shrink her neck into the ground. She quickly shook her head, "No."

Wei Qi looked at her without speaking, but gently placed his palm on her lower abdomen. His large hand was warm, giving her a sense of comfort.

Xi Rongyan looked up in a daze, meeting His Majesty’s gaze.

It was profound and carried a calming stillness that put her at ease.

She was so captivated that she felt a sense of familiarity, as if she had seen it many times before.

But she and His Majesty had never really interacted before.

Once, when she and her mother entered the palace to accompany the Empress Dowager, they had encountered His Majesty. At that time, His Majesty’s gaze had been indifferent and stern. When his eyes had swept over her, she had felt a little flustered.

Now, His Majesty’s gaze was completely different.

Wei Qi saw Xi Rongyan looking at him again and smiled, "Is there something on my face that you find so interesting?"

Xi Rongyan was taken aback and quickly lowered her head again.

At this moment, a palace maid’s voice came from outside, announcing the arrival of breakfast. Wei Qi let them in, then reached out and took a bowl of almond porridge. Under the watchful eyes of the nearby palace maid, he naturally brought a spoonful to Xi Rongyan’s lips to feed her.

Xi Rongyan looked in surprise at the almond porridge brought to her lips. It was her favorite from before.

The fragrance of the almond porridge wafted to her nose, and she remembered that His Majesty had specifically inquired about her preferences.

Now, seeing His Majesty feeding her the almond porridge, it reminded her of her days in the boudoir.

Her eyes suddenly stung, and she lowered her head to take a bite.

She then reached out to take the spoon herself, but His Majesty brought another spoonful to her lips, his voice low and gentle, "I’ll feed you."

The way he looked down at her carried a deep and scorching affection, like a river with undercurrents, calm on the surface but swirling with vortices beneath.

Xi Rongyan silently lowered her head, recalling that since the first day she entered the palace, His Majesty had always been extremely good and caring toward her.

She had been very reluctant to enter the palace and be with so many women. Deep down, whether it was her lingering sadness over the Gu family or her unwillingness, she had some resistance to getting close to His Majesty.

But now, that resistance seemed to be growing weaker, and even she herself was gradually compromising.

She took another bite, her mind still a little dizzy, feeling His Majesty’s gentleness while trying to stay clear-headed.

She thought of Wang Baoran.

She understood that His Majesty’s favor might not last.

Xi Rongyan kept her head down and didn’t speak. When His Majesty fed her, she ate. The small bowl didn’t have much, and Wei Qi wanted her to eat more, so he brought another bowl.

Xi Rongyan glanced at it, obediently not refusing, and silently ate it as well.

In the end, Wei Qi wiped her hands and the corners of her mouth.

Xi Rongyan had been holding back her words. When the palace attendants came in to dress her and His Majesty was holding her to fasten her jade pendant, she finally lifted her head from His Majesty’s embrace and softly asked, "Your Majesty, why are you so good to this concubine?"

In truth, as soon as she asked, Xi Rongyan regretted it.

It wasn’t something she should have asked.

Her aunt had said that the late Emperor would favor one person every so often, and no woman could maintain his favor for long.

Perhaps it was just novelty.

Wei Qi looked down at Xi Rongyan, then continued fastening the jade pendant for her, softly saying, "Has Rongyan forgotten what I told you before?"

Xi Rongyan was taken aback. His Majesty had said before...

His Majesty seemed to have indeed said that he liked her.

But what she was curious about was how His Majesty could like her.

They had clearly had no prior interaction...

She felt lost, sitting on the edge of the bed, watching His Majesty fasten the jade pendant for her, and she wondered why His Majesty was so skilled at this.

Did His Majesty often do this for other concubines as well?

Wei Qi just glanced at Xi Rongyan and knew what she was thinking.

He looked at her downcast, clear eyes and helplessly smiled, "I have only done this for you."

Xi Rongyan widened her eyes.

Wei Qi, however, didn’t want to explain further.

In his past life, he had done even more for her.

There was a period when he often dressed her.

That was when Xi Rongyan had been at her most difficult, so stubborn and cold.

Wei Qi had been exhausted, but seeing her haggard appearance pained him.

So he had given her medicine to make her mind foggy.

So that she could eat properly.

At that time, Xi Rongyan had needed care in almost every aspect.

Whenever he had the time, Wei Qi would personally take care of her. That period had been the most peaceful time for the two of them.

---

chapters.title: Understanding His Liking and Sincerity
chapters.content:
However, less than a month later, Wei Qi stopped giving Xi Rongyan medicine.

Because the imperial physician said that the medicine would harm her body and affect her ability to bear children in the future.

Moreover, someone who suddenly stopped causing trouble seemed to no longer be Xi Rongyan.

Wei Qi’s thoughts kept switching between the past and the present. Looking at Xi Rongyan from two different times, he increasingly realized the warm and endearing aura she carried.

Holding her in his arms was soft, soothing the turbulence in his mood.

Finally, when Xi Rongyan was pulled up by His Majesty, she still felt a sense of unreality.

It wasn’t until she took a few steps that her mind cleared up considerably.

His Majesty walked very slowly, holding her hand tightly.

When they were outside the palace, he fastened a cloak for her, looking at her and softly saying, "I will come to accompany you at noon."

"Don’t wait for me to eat. If I’m not here, you should eat first."

Xi Rongyan agreed, then looked up at His Majesty.

A cool breeze brushed against her loosely tied hair, and a strand of hair swept across her eyes. His Majesty seemed sometimes distant, sometimes close, making her unable to fathom him.

Wei Qi also looked at Xi Rongyan, at the ivory-white cloak draped over her, her delicate and fair appearance, and the way she looked at him. It seemed that her fear had gradually melted away.

Overcome with emotion, he lowered his head, cupped her face, and gave her a light kiss on the lips outside.

A fleeting kiss, without scorching passion, but full of deep meaning.

He hoped that one day, Xi Rongyan would understand his liking and sincerity toward her.

Xi Rongyan returned to the Hanyuan Palace and lay on the spring couch, unable to help but recall the kiss His Majesty had given her just now.

She covered her face, feeling her cheeks burn, and called for Bao Zhu to bring tea.

Bao Zhu had just brought the tea when a palace maid came to announce that Consort Xie had arrived.

Hearing that her cousin had come, Xi Rongyan quickly ordered Bao Zhu to invite her in.

When Xie Yumian entered, Xi Rongyan was sitting on the spring couch, bathed in light, her entire being radiating a glow.

Behind her, a vase held hibiscus flowers, matching the hairpin in her hair, setting off the rosy hue on her face.

It was as if she had been nourished well, full and flushed.

Xie Yumian paused, then looked at Xi Rongyan’s smiling eyes as she stood up and came forward. The scent of dragon’s saliva incense from her mixed with the lotus fragrance from Xi Rongyan. For a moment, she felt that this scent made her a little nauseous.

She stiffly forced a smile on her face, then was led by Xi Rongyan to sit on the spring couch.

Xi Rongyan ordered someone to bring pastries and tea, then picked up a piece of rose milk pastry and smilingly offered it to Xie Yumian, "Sister, try some. We used to love eating milk pastries. This one is extremely good and fragrant."

"Paired with the fragrance of pre-rain tea, it’s delicious."

Xie Yumian was taken aback. The rose fragrance spread in front of her. She didn’t take it but asked, "Did His Majesty bestow this?"

Xi Rongyan smiled, "Last time, His Majesty let me try a bite. I thought it was delicious, so His Majesty..."

Halfway through her sentence, Xi Rongyan suddenly stopped, hiding her smile. "Sister, don’t misunderstand. I only brought it because I thought you would like it."

Xie Yumian smiled, took it from Xi Rongyan’s hand, glanced down, suppressed her nausea, and took a bite.

She smiled, "How could I overthink it? I know you have me in your heart."

Xi Rongyan was relieved and leaned toward Xie Yumian, softly saying, "Last time, regarding the matter I discussed with you, I actually asked His Majesty several times."

"Previously, His Majesty said to let Empress handle this matter. I know that Consort Qi and Empress are close, and I was afraid it would implicate you, so I asked His Majesty again later. But His Majesty still hasn’t given me a definite answer."

"Sister, I can’t be sure of His Majesty’s intentions."

"I’m even more afraid that I won’t be able to help you in the end."

Xie Yumian looked at Xi Rongyan’s face indifferently.

Delicate eyebrows, watery eyes, a light yellow spring dress, the neckline embroidered with a circle of pearls, the light pink patterns on it exquisite and beautiful, making her look even more ethereal.

Her gaze then shifted down to the ivory fan in Xi Rongyan’s hand.

The ivory color matched Xi Rongyan’s skin tone perfectly, but it stirred an indescribable emotion in her heart.

His Majesty had stayed with her for more than ten consecutive days. This was no longer ordinary favor.

He had never allowed any concubine to enter the Zhonghua Palace, yet he had spent a night there with her.

The thought of Xi Rongyan and His Majesty taking a mandarin duck bath in the Zhonghua Palace’s pool while she waited in the cold room, hoping to truly leave that place, made everything seem ridiculous in comparison.

Xi Rongyan was now the only one in the harem with such favor. Was it so difficult for her to make such a small request?

Was it because she had regretted it, wanting to monopolize His Majesty’s favor and not wanting her to come to Guanju Palace?

She watched as Xi Rongyan became more and more favored, and herself become more and more like a joke.

How hypocritical were the words Xi Rongyan had just said?

Once upon a time, Xi Rongyan would have said such things too.

She had truly changed.

In the palace, past affections didn’t matter much. After all, who didn’t want to monopolize His Majesty’s favor?

She understood. Every woman in the palace wanted it, and Xi Rongyan was no exception.

Xie Yumian smiled faintly, placed the half-eaten pastry back on the plate, took a sip of tea, and softly said to Xi Rongyan, "I do hope that you will get better and better. It’s fine if I can’t help."

Xi Rongyan held her teacup, her eyebrows lowered, looking graceful and elegant in the light. "I know that Consort Qi is not very kind to you, Sister. In the future, if you are short on anything, I will send it to you. If she continues to be so excessive, I will go with you to report it to Empress."

"I still have the Empress Dowager to back me up. Even if I offend someone, it’s not a big deal. Even if I don’t provoke anyone, it won’t bring me any good."

When Xi Rongyan’s gaze fell, she looked especially pitiful—delicate eyebrows, cherry lips, and starry eyes. In the past, no one could resist her soft-spoken words, and neither could she.

But now, looking at this face, she was gradually growing tired of it.

Why was she always so likable?

Even His Majesty liked her so much.

Xie Yumian lightly hummed, then asked with a half-smile, as if joking, "If I really go to Guanju Palace and His Majesty sees me, what if he favors me in the future?"

The steam from the tea settled on Xi Rongyan’s eyebrows. She seriously replied, "If Sister really becomes favored in the future, I will genuinely be happy for you."

Xie Yumian smiled and asked again, "What if His Majesty only favors me in the future and no longer favors you?"

Xi Rongyan smiled, "Then I will still be happy for you."

"I also believe that in the future, when I encounter difficulties, Sister will help me."

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan turned her head to look out the window. The peach blossoms outside were in full bloom, creating a beautiful scene. She faced the light and softly said, "Once, I only wanted to live without the troubles of the inner court."

"But my fate is truly a bit unfortunate. Two marriages didn’t go well, and it was a twist of fate that I ended up in the palace."

"The night before I entered the palace, I had already made up my mind. If I am not favored, I will quietly stay out of trouble and in the future request to serve and accompany the Empress Dowager."

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan turned back to look at Xie Yumian, "I truly thought this way."

"Sister should understand me. I have always sought peace and quiet."

chapters.title: Splendid Attire
chapters.content:
Xie Yumian paused, looking at Xi Rongyan’s light-colored eyes, which showed no change from how they used to be when she spoke to her.

Her heart still stirred.

She and Xi Rongyan had known each other since childhood and knew that she had always preferred quiet.

She lowered her gaze, her emotions complex.

Suddenly, she asked in a low voice, "Do you still think about Young Master Gu?"

Xi Rongyan was taken aback by Xie Yumian’s sudden question.

In truth, it was impossible to say she hadn’t thought of him.

On the night before entering the palace, she had been thinking of Yun Yu Gege.

But Yun Yu Gege was dead.

All she could do was grieve.

Xi Rongyan looked down at the exquisitely embroidered hibiscus flower on her knee. "That’s all in the past now."

"I have no choice but to accept it."

Xie Yumian merely nodded. Then, in a low voice, she said, "I truly miss the old days."

Xi Rongyan also nodded. "So do I."

Xie Yumian left just before noon. Xi Rongyan saw her out. After Xie Yumian left the Han Yuan Hall, she looked at the empty and desolate Guan Ju Palace. A petal from the peach tree drifted into her eye, and she lowered her gaze before leaving.

She had only walked halfway when a palace servant hurried toward her. Xie Yumian recognized her—she was Qin Mom, who served Her Majesty the Empress.

Qin Mom approached Xie Yumian politely and said, "Her Majesty the Empress requests the presence of Consort Xie at this moment."

She looked up at Xie Yumian. "Her Majesty is waiting for Consort Xie."

Xie Yumian’s heart tightened.

These days, Consort Qi had been subtly mocking her, venting all her jealousy toward Xi Rongyan onto her. She had even united with other concubines to ostracize her, making her days increasingly difficult.

Now, Her Majesty the Empress was summoning her. She carried a heavy, unspoken grievance in her heart. Then, she thought of Xi Rongyan, dressed in splendid attire, sitting leisurely on the spring couch, calmly enjoying the serene spring scenery. The contrast made her feel even more downcast.

With a heavy heart, she went to the Empress. Passing through layers of curtains, she walked in with her head lowered, showing respect.

Song Helan sat gracefully on the noble consort’s couch, her posture relaxed as she playfully teased the cat in her lap.

Upon seeing Xie Yumian approach, she watched her cautiously and respectfully greet her, then said gently, "Come sit beside me."

Xie Yumian was still very careful in front of the Empress. Her mind raced with thoughts about what the Empress might say to her.

She recalled the last time the Empress had summoned her—it was to ask about some past matters concerning Xi Rongyan. It had seemed like casual chatter, and the Empress hadn’t probed too deeply.

So what would the Empress say this time?

Song Helan waited until Xie Yumian was seated beside her. She ordered a servant to pour tea for Xie Yumian before slowly asking, "How was Consort Xie’s relationship with Consort Zhen in the past?"

Xie Yumian hesitated for a moment before replying, "In the past, my family and Consort Zhen’s family were close, so we often interacted."

Song Helan drew out a long "oh," then stroked the white cat in her lap and sighed. "But I feel that Consort Xie’s relationship with Consort Zhen is nothing special."

Xie Yumian looked up at the Empress. Beneath the golden hairpins and phoenix ornaments, the Empress’s face was calm and elegant, with a faint, slightly disdainful smile, as if mocking her for trying to cling to a connection with Xi Rongyan.

She clenched the handkerchief in her hand until her palm ached. Then she said, "This concubine does not understand Her Majesty’s meaning."

Song Helan observed all of Xie Yumian’s emotions. She smiled again.

Slowly, she said, "Just now, His Majesty sent someone to relay a message, saying that I should arrange for you to move to another palace. In any case, you cannot stay in Guan Ju Palace."

As she spoke, Song Helan glanced at Xie Yumian. "If you had a good relationship with Consort Zhen, and she is so favored now, wouldn’t she be able to let you stay in Guan Ju Palace?"

"There’s still an empty side hall in Guan Ju Palace."

Xie Yumian’s face suddenly paled.

Her fingers trembled slightly.

Then she heard the Empress’s cold voice: "But if you have any dissatisfaction with me or Consort Qi, you can tell me."

"Did you think that by having Consort Zhen speak to His Majesty about this, you could make His Majesty think that I can’t even handle such a small matter?"

A stern, cold snort suddenly rang in her ears: "Do you think that just because Consort Zhen is favored, you can also afford to ignore me?"

Xie Yumian’s heart jolted violently. She quickly knelt before the Empress and begged for forgiveness. "Please, Your Majesty, see clearly—this concubine has no such intention."

"It was Consort Zhen who wanted this concubine to keep her company. She took the initiative to suggest it. This concubine—"

Before she could finish, the Empress interrupted with another cold snort: "You dare lie to me."

"If Consort Zhen truly wanted you to keep her company, why didn’t she let you move directly into Guan Ju Palace?"

"Do you think I don’t know? You see that Consort Zhen is favored, so you think you can be favored too and no longer need to respect me."

"Do you think you can be as favored as Consort Zhen?"

Cold sweat broke out on Xie Yumian’s forehead, and panic filled her heart. She had no way to defend herself and could only repeatedly beg for forgiveness.

Her fingernails, pressing into the carpet, dug deep. A hint of hatred flickered in the depths of her eyes.

She had truly believed that Xi Rongyan would let her stay in Guan Ju Palace.

Now, not only had she offended Consort Hua, but she had also offended the Empress. All of this was thanks to Xi Rongyan.

What of their past sisterly affection? It had long since vanished like smoke.

In the palace, what sisterly affection could there be among women?

Song Helan observed Xie Yumian’s pale face and the emotions hidden in her eyes. A cold smile lurked beneath her composed expression, but her face soon returned to a gentle, compassionate look. She reached out to help Xie Yumian to her feet, looking at her with a sigh. "Looking at you like this, I almost feel some sympathy for you."

"Forget it. I won’t pursue this matter further. From now on, you will move to the side hall of the former Consort Xian’s Hua Yang Palace—the Hui Ning Hall."

"Hua Yang Palace is closest to Guan Ju Palace. You can still visit Consort Zhen often to chat."

As she spoke, she seemed regretful: "Originally, I intended to help you by arranging for you to stay in Guan Ju Palace. But His Majesty sent someone to give orders, so I can only make this arrangement."

"You will move there this afternoon."

When Xie Yumian left the Empress’s presence, the most intense noon sunlight shone directly upon her. Her figure swayed slightly, and she let out a bitter laugh.

So the vast Guan Ju Palace truly had no place for her.

A servant beside her steadied her unsteady body and whispered, "Consort Zhen is too much. You were sincere to her, yet she treats your heart like this?"

"If it weren’t for Her Majesty’s leniency today, who knows what might have happened?"

Xie Yumian’s fingers trembled on the servant’s hand. After a long moment, she coldly uttered, "Now that she has His Majesty’s favor, how could she still remember our past sisterly bond?"

"Perhaps she is simply afraid that I might gain His Majesty’s attention."

With that, she took a deep breath, released her hand, and walked forward into the blinding light.

She thought again of what Xi Rongyan had said that morning—about wanting to live quietly without competing for favor. Xie Yumian let out a cold laugh. She almost wanted to see what expression Xi Rongyan would wear when she truly lost favor.

---

chapters.title: Exclusive Favor
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan only learned that her cousin had moved to Hua Yang Palace on the second day.

Early in the morning, when she went to pay her respects to the Empress, she noticed something was off as soon as she entered. Everyone looked at her strangely.

Even Wang Baoran looked at her with a faint sense of oddity and a hint of mockery.

Xi Rongyan subtly guessed that something had happened but kept her expression calm.

After leaving the Empress’s chambers, a palanquin was waiting to carry her away. Xie Yumian passed by her side, letting out a soft, ambiguous laugh. Xi Rongyan turned her head slightly and saw that Xie Yumian had already walked past her.

She caught the unclear meaning in that laugh and reached out to grab Xie Yumian’s sleeve. "Cousin."

Xie Yumian turned to look at Xi Rongyan. She saw the light blue cloak she wore, embroidered with auspicious birds and dragons in golden thread that shimmered in the light. Even though Xi Rongyan wore little makeup and only a jade hairpin, she still exuded an air of nobility.

That cloak, without a doubt, had been specially made for her by His Majesty.

She was already so favored—yet she still had to guard against her?

Xie Yumian gave a soft laugh, then gently pushed Xi Rongyan’s hand away. In a quiet voice, she said, "There are still things in my palace that need arranging. I’ll speak with you when I have time."

With that, Xie Yumian turned and walked away in another direction.

Xi Rongyan watched Xie Yumian’s reaction and was about to call out to her again when someone approached—Wang Baoran.

Wang Baoran looked at Xi Rongyan with a complex expression and asked in a low voice, "Consort Xie is your cousin. Why didn’t you let her stay in Guan Ju Palace? Instead, you had His Majesty move her to Hua Yang Palace?"

Xi Rongyan paused, her heart already understanding the day’s strange occurrences.

She said quietly, "I never asked His Majesty to do such a thing."

"How did this rumor start?"

Wang Baoran sighed. "It seems you still don’t know—Consort Xie moved to Hua Yang Palace yesterday afternoon."

"Now the entire harem is saying that you alone are favored and that you couldn’t bear to have Consort Xie in Guan Ju Palace competing with you."

As she spoke, Wang Baoran looked at Xi Rongyan, seeing her gentle and graceful demeanor, and said softly, "You should go explain to Consort Xie. It’s good to have someone trustworthy by your side."

Xi Rongyan frowned slightly. She hadn’t expected her cousin to have moved to Hua Yang Palace the day before.

She had spent the entire afternoon indoors yesterday and hadn’t heard the news. His Majesty had arrived very late last night, and she had already been asleep, so she hadn’t been able to ask.

Xi Rongyan turned to Wang Baoran. Though she didn’t know her intentions in offering this reminder, she still said softly, "Thank you for the warning, Sister."

Then, in a low voice, she added, "Sister, you seem perceptive. The rumors in the palace are likely spread with other intentions. Believing them would only fall into someone else’s trap."

"Don’t believe those words either."

Wang Baoran paused, standing in place as she watched Xi Rongyan board the palanquin and leave, her departing figure graceful and clear.

As she gathered her sleeves and was about to leave, she turned her head and saw Hui Fei standing behind her. Hui Fei’s elaborate high bun made her appear taller and even more imposing.

Hui Fei’s smile was ambiguous, with a trace of coldness. She said with a faint smile, "I didn’t realize when Wang Xiuyi became so close to Consort Zhen."

Wang Baoran quickly lowered her head. "This concubine’s relationship with Consort Zhen is nothing special. I merely happened to bump into her and exchanged a few words."

Hui Fei let out a cold snort, her gaze filled with disdain for Wang Baoran. "You used to be favored by His Majesty for a time. Now you’ve lost all your spirit?"

"Do you think that by flattering her, she’ll give you benefits?"

"Consort Xie’s own family doesn’t care about her—what use would she have for you?"

With that, Hui Fei let out a leisurely sigh. "If Consort Zhen hadn’t arrived, you would still be the most favored in the palace. Tsk tsk, now His Majesty doesn’t even glance at you. I almost feel sorry for you."

"But let me give you one piece of advice: don’t try to be a wallflower, or you might break your own neck."

With that, she left with her servants in a grand procession, leaving Wang Baoran standing alone.

Wang Baoran watched Hui Fei’s retreating figure, then lowered her gaze and walked forward.

She understood Hui Fei’s last words—they were a warning.

If she became close to Xi Rongyan, it would mean opposing Her Majesty the Empress. Her survival in the palace would become very difficult.

They wanted her to be a blade, but she refused to be a pawn in their schemes.

However, Xi Rongyan’s treatment of Consort Xie truly puzzled her. She had once thought she understood Xi Rongyan somewhat, but now she was confused again.

His Majesty had even excused Xi Rongyan from paying respects to the Empress and allowed her free access to Zhong Hua Palace and Ming De Hall, places where concubines were never permitted.

So why wouldn’t she even allow Consort Xie to stay in Guan Ju Palace?

Wang Baoran furrowed her brows, no longer sure what kind of person Xi Rongyan truly was.

chapters.title: Yan'er, Respond to Zhen
chapters.content:
On her end, Xi Rongyan went to Huayang Palace to see Xie Yumian. When she saw Xie Yumian give her a lukewarm smile, Xi Rongyan understood in her heart that Xie Yumian still believed the rumors spread by others.

Xie Yumian was tidying up books, and Xi Rongyan walked over to help. She leaned in and softly asked, "Sister, do you believe me, or do you believe the words others use to sow discord?"

Xie Yumian looked up and smiled, "Little sister, you're overthinking."

Xi Rongyan, seeing Xie Yumian's expression, softly said again, "If I didn't want to help you, sister, why would I have agreed in the first place?"

"I didn't fully understand His Majesty's intentions either. I also said back then that His Majesty might not agree. His Majesty said this matter should be handled by the Empress. How did you know it was His Majesty who arranged for you to stay in Huayang Palace?"

"What if it was the Empress deliberately sowing discord?"

Xie Yumian's hands paused.

This matter was indeed told to her by the Empress, who had said it was arranged by His Majesty.

But no matter what, His Majesty favored Xi Rongyan so much. If Xi Rongyan truly put her heart into it, how could His Majesty not care?

Xie Yumian composed herself, looked up at Xi Rongyan, pressed her lips together, put down the book in her hands, pulled Xi Rongyan to sit down, and smiled, "Little sister, no need to explain. I don’t blame you."

"Whether it's Huayang Palace or Guanju Palace, the bond between you and me remains unchanged. It's the same no matter where we are."

Xi Rongyan saw that the smile on Xie Yumian's face was not as warm as before, and she understood in her heart that Xie Yumian had not truly let go.

She softly said, "I couldn't help you, sister. That was not my intention."

"It's just that His Majesty is the Son of Heaven. Even if I am currently favored, it doesn’t mean His Majesty will agree to everything I ask."

"I do understand the difficulties you faced under Concubine Qi. In the future, if they trouble you again, don’t endure it silently. The palace has its rules, and His Majesty is not unreasonable. Moreover, your father is also an official in the court. You are no longer under Concubine Qi, and I will definitely help you."

Xie Yumian pressed her lips together, paused for a moment, then held Xi Rongyan's hand, "What you said is right. There is no Concubine Qi in Huayang Palace, so it’s fine for me to stay here. Besides, it’s close to Guanju Palace. Whether I come to you or you come to me, it’s convenient."

"After leaving the Empress’s place, we can still return together."

As she spoke, Xie Yumian gave a lonely smile, "But His Majesty dotes on you, little sister. You have people carrying you wherever you go. Maybe I can’t walk the same path as you anymore."

Xi Rongyan saw that Xie Yumian seemed to have relaxed, and her heart eased a little. She softly said, "Sister, don’t say things like that. I never liked riding in a sedan chair. From now on, I will walk with you."

Xie Yumian smiled, looking at the dimly lit room with barely any light, comparing it to Xi Rongyan’s Hanyuan Hall, the difference was immeasurable.

Xi Rongyan clearly enjoyed all the good things, yet she said she didn’t like them.

On the surface, they were close like sisters, but behind the scenes, she was on guard against her.

Xie Yumian lowered her head, looking at the hand tightly held by Xi Rongyan, and still felt a sense of irony.

She didn’t want to ask her anything, like how she spoke to His Majesty, or how she was supposed to know.

The Empress’s words from yesterday still lingered in her mind. His Majesty had never truly favored anyone before. This request was not excessive at all; it was just a matter of a single word from Xi Rongyan.

She gave a bitter smile. A single word, yet Xi Rongyan was unwilling.

She looked at Xi Rongyan again, "This place has been empty for some days. Although it was cleaned yesterday afternoon, there’s still some dust. Little sister, it’s better if you come here to sit after a few more days."

Xi Rongyan paused, "It’s fine. As long as sister understands and believes me, I am happy."

When leaving, Xie Yumian saw Xi Rongyan off to the door, still speaking softly and gently as before, "I don’t blame you for this. I never have."

"You and I are sisters who grew up together. Our families are also allied. How could we hold grudges over such things?"

"What you told me today, I understand it all."

Xi Rongyan looked into Xie Yumian’s eyes, but for some reason, her heart still tightened. She softly said, "When we were young, sister always told me her secrets, trusting that I wouldn’t tell anyone."

"Now, I hope sister also believes in me."

Xie Yumian looked at Xi Rongyan’s quiet eyes. In a moment of clarity, she felt as if she had seen the days when they were extremely close.

It was like a fleeting dream.

She lowered her gaze and gently nodded, "Alright."

After Xi Rongyan had walked far away, Xie Yumian turned around.

As soon as she turned, she saw the palace maids in Huayang Palace giving her ambiguous looks.

She recalled yesterday.

Yesterday, when she moved here, Concubine Qi had looked at her with a cold gaze, as if she wanted to flay her alive.

When she came to Huayang Palace, Huang Guiren, who used to live here, didn’t have a good expression for her either. She thought Xie Yumian had previously relied on Concubine Qi and was now trying to ingratiate herself with Xi Rongyan, but ended up pleasing neither side.

Xi Rongyan was currently in high favor. Neither Concubine Qi nor the Empress dared to do anything to her, but they treated Xie Yumian differently.

She ignored those glances and silently returned to her palace.

On her end, Xi Rongyan returned to Hanyuan Hall and sat on the luohan bed, but she had no appetite. With her worries, she couldn’t eat.

She only hoped that her cousin truly believed her. Her cousin was someone close to her. If she believed those deliberately sown words of discord, it would play right into some people’s hands.

Yuzhu, beside her, tried to persuade her, "The matter with Consort Xie was not the mistress’s fault in the first place."

"The mistress indeed asked His Majesty many times about this. The current outcome is also something the mistress didn’t expect."

"Moreover, the mistress had already said back then that His Majesty might not agree. Consort Xie agreed as well. The mistress has nothing to feel guilty about."

Xi Rongyan propped up her chin, her fingertips sliding along the teacup, her expression downcast, "People outside think that because I am favored, I can make anything happen."

"In reality, they also know that even if they ask, His Majesty might not agree. They just want to sow discord between me and my cousin."

Yuzhu said, "Fortunately, just now, Consort Xie believed the mistress. She probably wasn’t swayed by the discord."

As she spoke, she moved a plate of cherries in front of Xi Rongyan, "These are freshly ripened cherries sent from the south. His Majesty dotes on the mistress so much that he sends plate after plate to the mistress’s palace. No one else gets them."

Xi Rongyan glanced at them and only softly said, "I hope so."

When Wei Qi entered, he saw Xi Rongyan lying on the small table.

Her dark blue dress was slightly wrinkled from her posture, and the pink hem of her skirt was embroidered with peonies, looking delicate and eye-catching.

Her dark hair was lustrous, and her jade hairpin sparkled. Even though she had her back to him, she exuded a touching beauty.

Wei Qi knew that Xi Rongyan had just come back from Huayang Palace. He pressed his lips together and walked over.

He waved his hand, signaling everyone in the room to leave, then quietly walked to Xi Rongyan’s side and sat behind her.

In truth, Xi Rongyan had recognized the familiar scent as soon as His Majesty entered, but she only glanced at the figure from the corner of her eye and pretended not to notice him.

She watched the warm wind blow the peach blossoms outside the window. A petal drifted in through the window and landed in front of her. She lowered her gaze.

Then, she was pulled into a warm embrace.

Xi Rongyan sat in the Emperor’s lap, watching as the Emperor picked a cherry and brought it to her lips. She slightly turned her head away and did not open her mouth.

In reality, Xi Rongyan knew her limits and had never been arrogant because of her favor.

She was subtly expressing her distress, carefully observing the Emperor’s mood, and testing his reaction to her actions.

These days, she understood that the Emperor seemed gentle and considerate toward her. He was also aware of her cousin’s situation and wanted to try once more to truly help her cousin.

If it was the Empress’s decision, perhaps there was still a chance.

Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan like this, her dark eyebrows lowered, long lashes trembling slightly, like a spoiled and coquettish person.

The cherry at his fingertips hovered for a long time, but she acted as if she didn’t see it, not even deigning to open her mouth, let alone lift her eyes to look at him.

Wei Qi pressed his lips together, put down the cherry, and then lifted Xi Rongyan’s chin with his finger.

What he saw was a pair of eyes hidden beneath lowered lashes, their dark pupils turned to the side, refusing to meet his gaze.

He couldn’t tell if she was angry or not.

This demeanor was somewhat similar to Xi Rongyan from his past life. Her weak and powerless resistance was sometimes unbearably cute, as if whoever she refused to look at would suffer.

Back then, Wei Qi indeed couldn’t stand her not looking at him.

If she didn’t look at him, it was as if she couldn’t bear to have him in her sight. Back then, asking her to glance at him even once seemed like a luxury.

Now it seemed that she had this habit from a young age.

Somehow, he suddenly felt a sense of relief.

It was just this temperament.

He had heard that when she was young, her father and brothers had spoiled her, making her well-mannered in public but prone to little tantrums with those close to her.

Did that mean he was someone she considered close?

A warmth surged in his heart. His throat rolled, and he pulled her into his embrace, lowering his head to lift her chin and kiss her.

The small table was pushed to the corner, and the teacup on it wobbled and fell, making a dull thud.

Wei Qi looked at the beautiful person beneath him, utterly enchanted by her coquettishness. His body tensed, and his fingers had already slipped under her clothes.

Feeling her slight evasion, he breathed heavily, his hoarse voice filled with emotion, "Yan'er, respond to Zhen."

chapters.title: She Loves Her Acting Cute
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan never expected the Emperor to act like this.

Feeling the Emperor’s fingers kneading inside, though there was no one in the room, it was still broad daylight. She shyly closed her eyes, pressing her fingers against the Emperor’s chest, but it had no effect.

Her lips were blocked, and she let out a few muffled sounds, her clumsy response only stirring the man’s desire further.

Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan’s flushed face and knew she probably wouldn’t be willing right now. So he held her, kissed her enough, then lifted her to sit in his lap.

The person in his arms was still breathing lightly. He slowly stroked her back and adjusted her collar, which had come loose, covering the spring scenery beneath.

When she had calmed down, Wei Qi lowered his head, his dark eyes fixed on hers, and asked, "Are you unhappy today?"

Xi Rongyan’s cheeks were still tinged with a light blush. She lowered her head, still caught in her shyness, then paused slightly at the Emperor’s words and averted her gaze. "No."

Her fair, delicate cheeks were like pear blossoms, the faint red at the corners of her eyes, and the subtle fragrance on her body—when she turned her gaze away, she looked like a child throwing a tantrum.

Xi Rongyan had only done this because she heard no anger in the Emperor’s voice.

When she was a child, she often begged her elder brother like this, and it always worked.

Her mother had said that occasionally acting cute could be useful.

Wei Qi lowered his gaze slightly, his palm resting on Xi Rongyan’s slender back. He bent down, lifted her chin, and raised an eyebrow at her. "If you’re not unhappy, why are you throwing a little tantrum?"

Xi Rongyan finally glanced at Wei Qi quickly, wondering if now was the right time to speak.

This was the first time she had acted coy with someone other than her brother, and she couldn’t help feeling a little uneasy.

But if she wanted to achieve her goal, maybe trying wouldn’t hurt.

Her eyes welled up with tears almost instantly. She leaned against the Emperor’s shoulder but shook her head. "This concubine just suddenly feels heartbroken."

Wei Qi raised an eyebrow, cupping Xi Rongyan’s face. It was wet, her tearful eyes still glistening, looking so wronged that it pained him just to see her like this.

She cried so easily.

If in his past life, Xi Rongyan had even a fraction of this ability to act coy and wronged, he wouldn’t have been angry with her.

She wouldn’t have suffered so much.

Even though he knew Xi Rongyan was probably crying on purpose in front of him, he still lowered his gaze, pityingly wiping away her tears with his fingers. Her watery eyes, brimming with sorrow, even her nose was red.

He knew what she meant, but he wanted her to belong to him completely.

He wanted her to rely only on him in the harem.

He wanted her to forget all the past people and events.

Moreover, Xie Yumian had never truly cared for her.

He sighed silently. She was truly like water, her tears endlessly flowing, even the fine hairs at her temples were damp.

He pulled her into his arms, gently patting her back to comfort her, but suddenly thought—had Xi Rongyan, in his past life, also leaned in that dead man’s arms, crying like this?

His long fingers paused. Wei Qi closed his eyes, concealing all his emotions.

A pair of soft hands wrapped around his waist, and a warmth rose in his heart again.

Xi Rongyan’s initiative in embracing him was something he still couldn’t resist.

Last night, he had arrived late, and she had already fallen asleep, not even waiting for him.

The suppressed desire now flared up again at her coy behavior, making him feel restless.

He still restrained himself, holding her up and looking at her leisurely, his expression slightly serious. "If you have any grievances, tell me. I will always stand up for you."

Xi Rongyan felt the Emperor’s warm fingers gently wiping her tears, his movements tender and careful. She slowly opened her eyes. Though her vision was blurred by tears, the Emperor’s gentle gaze still gave her some confidence.

Finally, she lowered her head and nestled into the Emperor’s arms, choking back a sob. "This concubine heard that my cousin has been sent to Huayang Palace. This concubine couldn’t help her and feels sad."

"I also feel lonely without her by my side."

Wei Qi looked down as she softly threw herself into his arms, her soft body rarely taking the initiative to press against him. It was hard for her reserved nature.

In truth, he had never intended to agree to her request.

He didn’t even want Xie Yumian staying in Huayang Palace.

Originally, he hadn’t wanted Xie Yumian to appear in front of Xi Rongyan at all.

In his past life, Wei Qi had thought of letting Xie Yumian keep Xi Rongyan company, so she would have someone to talk to in the palace, preventing her from overthinking and improving her mood.

But who would have thought that woman would secretly advise Xi Rongyan while also seducing and provoking him under the guise of discussing Xi Rongyan’s affairs.

She even spoke ill of Xi Rongyan in front of her.

If it had been earlier, Wei Qi would have killed her long ago. But back then, Xi Rongyan had only been willing to get close to that woman.

Only when Xie Yumian was present did Xi Rongyan have any appetite to eat.

How much of Xie Yumian’s feelings for Xi Rongyan were genuine? She had only acted according to the situation, never truly for Xi Rongyan’s sake.

He had sent Xie Yumian to Huayang Palace only to fulfill half of Xi Rongyan’s wishes.

He had long since arranged for people to keep a close watch on Xie Yumian, wanting Xi Rongyan to see her true face.

In this harem, the only one who truly cared for her, the only one who was good to her, was him.

The so-called cousin she had grown up with was no different, yet she devoted herself to others.

Wei Qi sighed softly, reaching out to lift her face. His gaze was dark as he looked at her tear-streaked face. It was already difficult for him to do this much for someone else.

He never blamed her. He understood her nature—she was affectionate toward those around her, with no guard.

He would guard her for her.

He silently bent down, kissing her eyes, then looked at her and said in a low voice, "If you feel lonely, I’ll have someone send two parrots to you."

"Or, after you leave the Empress’s place in the morning, you can wait for me at Xuanzheng Hall. When I have time, I’ll come keep you company."

"In the afternoon, after I finish my work, I’ll accompany you for a walk in the garden."

Xi Rongyan paused, finally looking at the Emperor. "Why did Your Majesty arrange for my cousin to go to Huayang Palace?"

"Can’t she come to Guanju Palace to keep me company?"

Wei Qi calmly lowered his head. "Rongyan, once I’ve made a decision, I won’t change it."

"I am the ruler. A ruler’s word is not to be taken lightly. If I hesitate and change my decisions arbitrarily, how can my subordinates trust me?"

As he spoke, Wei Qi’s dark eyes softened slightly. He pulled Xi Rongyan closer into his arms and said in a low voice, "When Chengqian Palace is ready, you’ll move there. Your cousin won’t be alone there."

"It’s no different from Huayang Palace."

He caressed her cheek. "Chengqian Palace is closest to Mingde Hall. That place was specially reserved for you."

Xi Rongyan suddenly understood—sending her cousin to Huayang Palace was indeed the Emperor’s intention.

She also vaguely understood that the Emperor did not want her cousin in Guanju Palace.

But she still had doubts in her heart. She knew Chengqian Palace was the best palace, and the Emperor had been extremely good to her since she entered the palace.

She reached out and wrapped her arms around the Emperor, pressing her face against his chest.

The room fell into a deep silence.

Wei Qi quietly held her in his arms, closing his eyes as he thought about the past.

Even as he held this warm, soft body tightly, he still felt a lingering fear of loss.

As if one day, she would still leave him.

Only by tightly binding her to his side, ensuring that the only one she could rely on was him, making her completely forget the past, would he feel slightly at ease.

He knew that, in truth, he had never changed.

His possessiveness toward her was still strong, and he was even more uncertain about what he might do if, one day, she truly left him.

But he was also afraid that Xi Rongyan would fear him.

In the past, his forceful methods were meant to make her afraid, to make her obey. Now, he was afraid she would be scared of him.

Wei Qi took a deep breath, bending down to clasp her hand, intertwining their fingers. He lowered his head to inhale the scent at her neck, then asked hoarsely, "Are you hungry?"

The Emperor’s hot breath fell on her, and she felt something pressing against her. Xi Rongyan realized what it was, her cheeks burning as she stiffly nodded, hoping the Emperor would let her go soon.

By now, it was already noon. Since Xi Rongyan had no appetite earlier, no food had been served yet.

Wei Qi ordered the servants to prepare lunch, then turned her face to look at her, his deep eyes gazing at her tear-stained face. "If you’re hungry, eat more later."

Xi Rongyan, flustered by the Emperor’s gaze, hastily nodded.

Wei Qi looked at the red lips before him. The desire that had been interrupted earlier was now rekindled by the alluring fragrance. He swallowed hard, pinched her cheek, and asked, "I heard you used to enjoy admiring flowers. I’ll have someone send some blooming flowers to your room."

"What kind of flowers do you like? I’ll have more sent."

Xi Rongyan liked growing flowers but did not like cutting them to keep indoors.

But the Emperor’s gaze was burning, so she lowered her head and nodded.

Wei Qi watched as she lowered her head, the pearl earrings dangling by her neck, the pink collar revealing her fair neck. Unable to resist, his dark eyes lingered, and he bent down to gently bite the tender flesh.

This was truly torturous.

Her temperament was like fine porcelain—he couldn’t take her as recklessly as he had in his past life. She wouldn’t take the initiative, making his restraint unbearable.

He really wanted to just sit here...

Xi Rongyan suddenly felt a tickle on her neck and let out a soft "eh," turning her head in surprise to look at Wei Qi. "Your Majesty..."

Wei Qi’s deep black eyes met Xi Rongyan’s. If he didn’t bite her, he would go mad.

But seeing the faint teeth marks on her fair neck, his heart ached. "Did it hurt?"

As he spoke, he gently kissed the spot. "I’ll be gentler next time."

The hot breath on her skin sent a slight tingling through Xi Rongyan’s body, and she couldn’t help but let out a soft moan.

Wei Qi paused, his burning gaze sweeping over Xi Rongyan. Her misty brows and red lips, the long-suppressed desire made him truly unable to restrain himself any longer.

Suddenly, he no longer wanted to suppress the restlessness in his heart. He lowered his head and kissed the fragrance.

Xi Rongyan only felt her body being pressed down by the Emperor, and before she knew it, she was being kissed again.

His slightly rough breathing was still something she wasn’t used to. Being pressed down by the Emperor in broad daylight, with servants standing outside, she pushed at him, not understanding why the Emperor seemed so urgent today...

Just then, a voice from outside announced that the meal was ready. Wei Qi barely restrained the desire to devour her right there, kissing her deeply a few more times before sitting up with her in his arms.

He even carefully smoothed out the slight wrinkles in her clothes before leading her out to eat.

In the past, after meals, Wei Qi rarely stayed with Xi Rongyan. Today, even when she felt drowsy and wanted to nap, he showed no sign of leaving.

She couldn’t help but ask, "Is Your Majesty not busy today?"

Wei Qi had originally intended to be intimate with her, but seeing her sleepy eyes, he eventually gave up the idea.

As he was about to leave, he took off the jade pendant from his hand and placed it in Xi Rongyan’s palm, looking at her. "From now on, whether you go to Xuanzheng Hall or Mingde Hall to find me, the guards will not stop you when they see this."

As he spoke, Wei Qi bent down and kissed her forehead. His calm black eyes exuded a reassuring gaze. "Rongyan, no matter what happens, come to me if something is wrong."

"No one in the palace can bully you. Do you understand?"

Xi Rongyan held the jade pendant the Emperor had given her, looking into his eyes. She was stunned for a long time before nodding blankly.

Wei Qi was reassured. He gave a gentle, low laugh before rising to his feet.

---

chapters.title: His Possessiveness Toward Her Was Still Strong
chapters.content:
After Wei Qi left, Xi Rongyan held the jade pendant and looked at it for a long time. She thought of the Emperor’s gentle eyes, different from Yu Yu’s gentleness, yet it still made her feel at ease.

She buried her face in the soft pillow, her heart inexplicably racing.

Baozhu looked at the jade pendant in Xi Rongyan’s hand and said happily, "The Emperor gave His Majesty’s personal jade pendant to you, which means the Emperor truly likes you."

Xi Rongyan silently tightened her grip on the jade pendant, then looked down at the dragon pattern on it. It faintly carried the Emperor’s scent, as if he had always worn it.

And now he had given it to her.

Baozhu added softly, "Moreover, I think the Emperor treats you differently."

Xi Rongyan turned her head and asked, "Have you seen how the Emperor acts with others?"

Baozhu scratched her head. "This servant hasn’t seen that."

Xi Rongyan smiled slightly, not dwelling on the matter.

She placed the jade pendant in Baozhu’s hands. "Take this and keep it safe. Don’t let anyone see where you put it."

"This is the Emperor’s belonging. If it’s lost, it might cause trouble."

Baozhu smiled. "Don’t worry, mistress. This servant will keep it safe."

After Wei Qi left Guanju Palace and returned to Mingde Hall, he asked Gao Yi, "What did Zhen Pin say when she went to see her today?"

Gao Yi reported everything in detail, then looked up at the Emperor. "The messenger said that Consort Xie did not do anything else today and treated Zhen Pin no differently."

"She stayed in her room in the palace and did not go out to see anyone."

Wei Qi clasped his hands behind his back, narrowing his eyes. "Keep a closer watch."

Gao Yi quickly agreed.

At this moment, someone announced that the Crown Prince was waiting outside the hall. Wei Qi then remembered that today was the day to examine Wei Heng’s studies.

When Wei Heng entered, his small frame was impeccable as he knelt and performed the grand salute to Wei Qi.

Wei Qi still looked at his son with a cold gaze, listening to the teacher who had entered with him explain Wei Heng’s recent studies in detail.

After hearing that Wei Heng could recite the Analects backward, he raised an eyebrow and had Wei Heng recite the Wei Zheng chapter.

Wei Heng looked directly into his father’s eyes, reciting with composure, "To govern by virtue is like the North Star, which remains in its place while all the other stars pay homage to it..."

In a short time, Wei Heng recited fluently.

Wei Qi casually asked, "What is your interpretation of 'examine his motives, observe his conduct, and understand his heart'?"

Wei Heng furrowed his brows, thinking for a moment before answering, "This son believes that examining his motives is to observe his actions, observing his conduct is to investigate the reasons, and understanding his heart is to know his intentions."

"Just as in the imperial examinations, candidates are not selected based solely on their essays; one must also consider their reputation in their hometown, their teacher’s influence, and their usual interests."

"When supervising officials, one must investigate their corrupt practices, their methods of amassing wealth, and whether they are extravagant. With these three aspects verified, there is nowhere to hide."

"This son also often reflects on whether his own words and deeds are worthy of a prince’s virtue, examining himself three times a day, fearing that his virtue may not match his position and that he may disappoint Your Majesty’s teachings."

chapters.title: Shall We Tonight?
chapters.content:
Wei Heng’s voice was calm and steady, just like his father’s usual composure.

Hearing his words, the teacher beside him also let out a sigh of relief.

Wei Heng was the legitimate eldest son, and no matter what, he was destined to be the crown prince. He had been educated with the expectations of a heir to the throne, so he was also taught the art of ruling, hoping that the eldest prince would become a wise ruler in the future.

Although the Grand Prince was still two months away from turning six, his mind and maturity were far beyond that of a six-year-old child—he was extremely intelligent.

He cautiously observed the Emperor’s expression. He had thought that the Grand Prince’s excellence would earn the Emperor’s praise, but instead, he saw the Emperor’s face remain cold. When the Emperor’s sharp black eyes swept over him, his heart jumped, and cold sweat broke out on his forehead.

He could not fathom the mind of the Emperor.

Wei Qi only glanced at Wei Heng indifferently after he finished speaking, but showed no intention of speaking.

He tapped his fingers on the armrest, his face revealing no emotion.

The hall fell into a long silence.

After a long while, Wei Qi finally waved his hand, signaling Wei Heng to leave.

Wei Heng looked at his father with a mixture of surprise and disappointment, not understanding why his father would not even give him a single word of evaluation.

The Empress Dowager always said that as long as he did well in his studies, the Emperor would be pleased.

If the Emperor was pleased, then in the future, he could become the Emperor.

And he only liked being the Emperor.

Wei Qi looked at his son’s puzzled eyes and could also see the indifference and coldness deep within them.

He tightly pressed his lips together, still not giving him a single word, only waving his hand to dismiss him.

Wei Heng’s heart was filled with grievance and frustration, yet he respectfully and silently retreated.

The Empress was waiting outside the hall. Seeing her son come out so quickly, she couldn’t help but ask worriedly, “What happened? Did your father praise you?”

Wei Heng lowered his head, ignoring his mother, and just kept walking forward.

Empress Song Helan then asked the teacher who followed him out. After hearing the answer, she watched her son’s retreating figure and then looked at the tightly closed palace doors. A long-suppressed anger suddenly welled up in her heart.

So many years had passed.

She had endured for as many years as she had been married to the Emperor.

Back then, everyone envied her for being bestowed in marriage by the late Emperor to the third prince, who was not only divinely handsome but also had distinguished military achievements. But now, thinking back, it was the thing she regretted the most.

It was fine if the Emperor was cold to her, but why was he also so indifferent to their child?

What had the child done wrong?

Her fingers trembled slightly. For a moment, she had an impulse to push open the palace doors in front of her and rush in to question him—after all these years, what had she done wrong?

To question why he treated her this way.

But in the end, all her resentment and grievance turned into a rational, faint smile.

She left with dignity, still the noble and exalted Empress in the eyes of others.

She would definitely make her son the crown prince, the future Emperor.

Because these were the things she deserved after all these years of endurance.

Wei Qi summoned Wei Heng’s teacher again.

Grand Tutor Lin was the number one scholar in the imperial examination, highly talented, and had been personally selected by Wei Qi to teach Wei Heng.
