Wei Qi stood up from the dragon desk, walked slowly to Grand Tutor Lin with his hands behind his back, and said indifferently, “Tutor Lin, you have worked hard in educating Heng’er. From now on, you should rest well at home. I will find another teacher for Heng’er.”

Grand Tutor Lin’s face was filled with astonishment, and he looked up at the Emperor in disbelief. “But does Your Majesty think that this humble official has been negligent in teaching the prince? If so, this humble official is willing to resign and return to his hometown.”

Wei Qi’s face still showed the same cold indifference, not the slightest change despite Grand Tutor Lin’s unwillingness and fear.

He simply said calmly, with a voice that was almost heartless, “Tutor Lin, do not overthink it. I am only considering your health.”

“Do not disappoint my consideration for you.”

The calm voice made Grand Tutor Lin’s heart tremble once again. The Emperor’s meaning was already very clear. He understood the Emperor’s temperament—if he asked further, he would only bring humiliation upon himself.

He had only asked out of a moment of unwillingness.

Clearly, he had taught the Grand Prince to be steady, knowledgeable, and intelligent, yet the Emperor wanted to change the prince’s teacher.

He felt wronged.

But now, he didn’t even dare to voice his grievance. He quickly retreated.

In the afternoon, when Xi Rongyan woke up from her nap, a eunuch delivered several potted landscapes to her palace.

There was a uniquely shaped weeping begonia and a precious southern sea begonia.

There were also imperial robe yellow and drunken Xi Shi peonies.

On the incense table, a jade vase held a rose.

Xi Rongyan came out and looked around. The room was like a garden, filled with the fragrance of flowers.

Then she heard a few crisp chirps. She looked at the small stand beside the chair and saw a cage hanging underneath, inside which were two pure white parrots.

She gently teased one, and it called out, “Wanfu.”

The other one called out, “Jixiang.”

Xi Rongyan’s interest was piqued. “These two are well-trained.”

Beside her, Baozhu laughed. “Aren’t they? They sound so delightful.”

“The Emperor specially sent them to you, my lady, to make you happy.”

Xi Rongyan called Yuzhu to bring some bird food. She sat on a small chair and fed them one by one with great interest.

On the small high shelf beside her, the potted landscapes were placed. The pink weeping begonia was vivid and beautiful, forming a small scene.

When Wei Qi came over at night, he happened to see Xi Rongyan teaching the parrots to speak. “Noble Consort Jixiang.”

“Noble Consort Wanfu.”

Xi Rongyan’s eyes curved into a smile as she said to Baozhu beside her, “Look, they learn quickly.”

It wasn’t until she noticed a shadow falling in front of her that Xi Rongyan realized the Emperor had arrived. She quickly stood up and went to greet him.

Wei Qi casually put his arm around her shoulder and walked over to the birdcage, sitting down. “Do you like them?”

Xi Rongyan smiled and nodded. “I do.”

She also thanked the Emperor.

Wei Qi used his finger to tease the parrots, but his peripheral vision was always on Xi Rongyan.

Seeing that she was still interested in feeding the birds, and looking at the remaining food in her hand, he didn’t know how much longer she would feed them.

He asked, “Have you washed up?”

Xi Rongyan’s gaze was on the parrots. “Not yet.”

Wei Qi then ordered someone to bring water.

When the water arrived, he didn’t wait for Xi Rongyan to finish feeding the birds. Instead, he took her hand and led her to the inner palace.

Xi Rongyan had no choice but to go wash up. When she came out, she saw the Emperor sitting on the edge of the bed waiting for her.

His dark eyes burned with a scorching gaze that made her heart skip a beat.

The Emperor reached out to her. “Rongyan, come here.”

Xi Rongyan slowly walked over. As soon as she reached the Emperor, he took her hand and pulled her into his embrace.

He looked down at her, his dark eyes like swirling, seductive whirlpools. “Rongyan, shall we tonight?”

---

chapters.title: Unable to Control His Emotions
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan’s face heated up again, and in an instant, she understood the Emperor’s meaning.

Last night, she had felt his hands wandering over her body. In fact, she had been woken up once in the middle of the night by his movements, but she didn’t dare to open her eyes. The Emperor’s breath on her was too hot, so hot that she worried whether she could endure it.

Now, the Emperor was asking her so directly again. She stumbled over her words, not knowing how to respond.

She couldn’t refuse the Emperor, but she also couldn’t bring herself to say those uninhibited words.

Wei Qi didn’t expect Xi Rongyan to respond.

Their previous encounter had been far from enough.

He slowly bent down, tentatively kissing her, then observing her reaction.

When he saw Xi Rongyan’s flushed cheeks and her compliant eyes, he finally let go of his worries and slowly pulled her into his embrace.

Little by little, he undid her clothes.

He cared too much about Xi Rongyan’s feelings, about how she felt toward him.

He gently and patiently soothed her body, hoping she would also desire him.

Finally, when he heard Xi Rongyan’s soft, melodious cry, he let out a satisfied sigh.

He slightly tilted his head back, closing his eyes. At the moment of greatest pleasure, scenes from his past life flashed through his mind.

There had been a period when his intimate relations with Xi Rongyan were frequent. Those days had been satisfying for him because he had never indulged his desires before.

Only with Xi Rongyan did he allow himself to be completely uninhibited.

But now, it was even more satisfying than back then.

Xi Rongyan felt as if she were being carried by waves to the shore, thinking she could finally escape, only for another wave to quickly come and push her back to the crest.

Rising and falling, the Emperor in front of her seemed to be the only lifeline she had. She tightly clutched his clothes, letting out soft moans that even she found unfamiliar.

The movements in the warm bed continued until the middle of the night.

Wei Qi panted slightly, his fingers resting on Xi Rongyan’s cheek, which was damp with a thin layer of sweat.

By now, she was exhausted and had fallen asleep in his arms. The hand resting on his shoulder was weakly sliding down.

He took her hand, holding it in his palm, then lowered his head to kiss the corner of her lips before picking her up to bathe.

When they returned, the bed had already been remade. However, Wei Qi, still holding Xi Rongyan, sat on the edge of the bed, his gaze falling on the hairpin placed beside the pillow.

The hairpin should have been under the pillow before. When the bedding was changed earlier, it had been placed beside the pillow.

He gently laid Xi Rongyan down on the bed, pulled the blanket over her, but his tall figure remained seated on the edge of the bed.

He quietly held the hairpin in his hand, examining it closely under the dim candlelight.

This white jade hairpin, carved into the shape of a peach branch, was very familiar to Wei Qi. In his past life, when Xi Rongyan had come to the palace to seek his help, she had worn this very hairpin in her hair.

After that day, Xi Rongyan had stayed in the Chengqian Palace, which he had prepared for her.

At first, Wei Qi had not paid attention to the hairpin.

It was later, on a day when he went to see her, that he noticed her holding the hairpin in a daze.

Because Xi Rongyan would be startled whenever she heard he was coming, Wei Qi often visited her quietly.

The first time he saw her holding the hairpin, he didn’t think much of it.

The second time, he stood behind her, watching as she held the hairpin and shed tears. He realized then that this hairpin must be special.

He took it to heart. That night, while she slept, he sat on the edge of the bed just as he did today, staring at the hairpin.

There was nothing particularly special about the hairpin, but Wei Qi knew it must be different.

He questioned the old servants who had attended to her and learned that this hairpin was a betrothal gift from Gu Yunyu to Xi Rongyan after the Gu and Xi families had formed a marriage alliance.

Gu Yunyu had spent many days and nights carving it with his own hands.

After their marriage, Xi Rongyan had always worn it in her hair.

At that time, Wei Qi naturally could not tolerate this hairpin. He had used her child to coerce her, forcing her to break the hairpin with her own hands.

That day, he had watched as she cried until she fainted, her palm bleeding from the broken hairpin. Even though he had a heart of stone and had been truly cruel to her, at that moment, no one’s heart ached more than his.

All because of Gu Yunyu.

He had miscalculated.

When his desire to possess Xi Rongyan reached a point where even he could not restrain himself, he knew he could no longer endure it.

He had caused trouble for the Gu family.

Then, after the incident, he had sought out Gu Yunyu.

His intention was clear: he wanted Gu Yunyu to find a new love, divorce Xi Rongyan. Not only would he not pursue the Gu family’s mistakes, but he would also give Gu Yunyu an opportunity for rapid promotion.

He could even let the Gu family remain safe and sound.

But Gu Yunyu had chosen an unexpected way to leave.

He had hanged himself at home.

He left behind a divorce letter and a confession.

Gu Yunyu had indeed fulfilled his promise, made that day in the Xuanzheng Hall, kneeling before him in fear—he would no longer have any connection with Xi Rongyan.

But he had made Xi Rongyan remember him forever.

That spineless man seemed to have a bit of backbone after all.

His original intention had been to make Gu Yunyu heartless toward Xi Rongyan so that she would turn to him. Instead, Gu Yunyu had chosen to die like this.

Forcing him to push Xi Rongyan even further.

Wei Qi narrowed his eyes, looking at the peach blossom hairpin on his finger. The dangerous and cold expression on his face was only fully revealed when Xi Rongyan could not see it.

His rough fingertips traced the exquisite carvings. He remained silent for a long time before gently placing the hairpin back under the pillow.

He pulled Xi Rongyan back into his embrace. Her soft breathing fell on his neck, so gentle, so quiet.

His fingers moved down to her waist. Wei Qi closed his eyes, took a deep breath, and the desire that had subsided surged back, making it impossible for him to control himself.

Every time he thought of the name Gu Yunyu, he could not control his emotions.

That man, who seemed so gentle and somewhat cowardly in his eyes, actually made him feel as if he could never surpass him.

The fingers gripping Xi Rongyan’s waist were already veined. Wei Qi could no longer endure it. He lowered his head and kissed the sleeping woman in his arms.

His movements were not particularly gentle, but the sleeping person showed no sign of waking. Only her fingers instinctively pressed against his chest in resistance.

This night was another long one. Wei Qi was like an untiring beast, only settling into the darkness at the moment the candlelight extinguished, tightly holding his prey in his arms.

When Xi Rongyan woke up the next day, she felt sore all over. Even the slightest movement was uncomfortable.

The scorching heat from the chest behind her made her feel as if her back was covered in a fine sheen of sweat. She moved slightly, trying to break free from Wei Qi’s embrace to catch her breath.

But the strong arm around her waist had no intention of letting her go. As soon as she moved slightly, the arm tightened, pressing her firmly against the chest behind her.

A wet, shallow bite landed on the nape of her neck. A lazy and hoarse voice came from behind her, “Awake?”

chapters.title: Yan'er, Don't Leave Me
chapters.content:
When Xi Rongyan heard the Emperor’s hoarse voice, she couldn’t help but recall last night when he had bitten her earlobe and asked, “Do you like it?”

At that time, her mind had already gone blank, and her body’s sensations seemed beyond her control.

She didn’t dare turn to look at the Emperor’s face, so she lowered her head and buried it in the blankets, nodding.

Wei Qi turned her around, but she still kept her head down, pressing her forehead against his chest. Her light breathing brushed against him like a feather. He lifted her shy chin.

His deep, dark eyes reflected the candlelight, gazing at him with clarity, devoid of any seduction or allure, yet always drawing him deeper into her gaze.

He felt her softness and purity. At this moment, she was like a flower drenched in dew, on the verge of blooming—most enchanting, making him unable to let her go.

The cold, emotionless Xi Rongyan from before was gone.

So this was what it felt like to possess her.

Just seeing her made his heart race; he wanted to be near her.

Wei Qi traced Xi Rongyan’s chin, then her cheek, the tenderness in his eyes stunning her.

She heard the Emperor softly call her name: “Yan’er.”

Xi Rongyan froze for a moment, then heard him say, “Don’t leave me.”

At that moment, her mind was in such chaos that she couldn’t think straight.

The Emperor’s voice was so low, carrying a hint of humility, as if he were begging her.

She didn’t understand her own feelings in that instant. She only felt as though she were slowly sinking into the Emperor’s tenderness.

But she couldn’t tell if his tenderness was meant only for her, or if it was just that he happened to favor her at the moment.

It took her a long while to gather her thoughts. She softly replied, “This concubine will not leave Your Majesty.”

Wei Qi silently watched Xi Rongyan’s bewildered eyes, then lowered his gaze, wordlessly pulling her into a tight embrace.

He wrapped his hand around her exposed shoulder.

When Wei Qi left, he was already dressed impeccably, his face restored to its noble and dignified bearing.

He sat on the edge of the bed, bending slightly, brushing aside the strands of hair near Xi Rongyan’s cheek with his fingers. His gaze fell on the faint red mark on her collarbone, exposed by her loosely tied robe.

He felt only tenderness, knowing he still hadn’t treated her gently enough. Last night, he had failed to control his emotions.

Guilt weighed on him as he leaned down, his face close to Xi Rongyan’s cheek. In that warm, fragrant moment of skin against skin, Wei Qi wished he could give her all his sincerity, hoping she could see it clearly.

In a hoarse voice, he said, “You don’t need to go to the Empress’s place this morning. I’ll have someone inform her.”

With that, Wei Qi slightly straightened, his long fingers reaching out to intertwine with Xi Rongyan’s. His dark eyes locked onto hers. “Yan’er, when you have time, go for a walk in the garden. I’ll come join you once I’m done with my work.”

“After some days, I’ll take you out of the palace.”

Xi Rongyan watched the Emperor’s departing figure, and before she knew it, she had propped herself up.

After Yu Zhu entered, she adjusted Xi Rongyan’s robe and chuckled, “Last night, when the mistress was fast asleep, it was His Majesty who carried you to bathe. He did everything himself—even when dressing you, he didn’t let anyone else enter.”

As she spoke, Yu Zhu looked at Xi Rongyan’s face. “Mistress, this servant sees that His Majesty truly treats you very well.”

Xi Rongyan fell silent for a moment. It seemed many people in the palace had said the same thing since she arrived. As she lowered her gaze, she recalled the Emperor’s tender expression from earlier.

She pinched the sleeve of her robe, then lifted her hand to her cheek, feeling a faint warmth.

In the afternoon, Xie Yumian came to invite Xi Rongyan to the garden for a chat.

Xi Rongyan had been in the palace for over half a month and hadn’t visited the garden yet. Remembering the Emperor’s suggestion to go when she had time, she felt a spark of interest.

Before leaving, Xie Yumian sat in Xi Rongyan’s room, observing the precious potted flowers and the carefully arranged objects. She turned to watch Xi Rongyan, who was lowering her head to feed the parrot with quiet focus.

The light pink brocade robe with peony embroidery was unlike the standard palace attire sent by the Imperial Household Department. Clearly, Xi Rongyan’s clothes were different.

The style, pattern, and craftsmanship were exquisite, and the colors suited her perfectly, as if custom-made for her.

The pearls embroidered along the cuffs and collar glistened subtly, just like how she sat in the light now, her brows and eyes like a painting, with a faint smile.

Suddenly, Xie Yumian asked, “Do you still think of Young Master Gu these days, little sister?”

Xi Rongyan’s movements froze.

Xie Yumian watched her pause, her gaze falling on the momentary melancholy in Xi Rongyan’s eyes. She continued, “I heard that when Young Master Gu met with his accident, he still had the jade pendant you gave him in his possession.”

“At that time, he went to the spring suburbs with his friends and said he would pick the first blooming peach blossom for you.”

As she spoke, Xie Yumian sighed regretfully, “What a pity, Young Master Gu’s deep affection for you.”

“And what a pity that your love for him was fated to be shallow.”

The birdseed slipped from Xi Rongyan’s fingers onto the nearby dish. She stared blankly at the snow-white parrot in the cage, parting her lips but unable to speak.

She knew all of this already.

During the days when Brother Gu Yunyu had his accident, she had deliberately tried not to think about it.

Every time she did, the grief kept her awake all night.

Now, as her cousin brought up these old wounds again, her heart still ached, and her eyes stung.

She had heard that when Brother Gu Yunyu met his accident, he had been holding the peach blossom he intended to bring her, stained with blood.

That day, Gu Huaiyi, the third young lady of the Gu family, had thrown the bloodstained peach blossom at her feet, crying, “Now you, this jinx, must be satisfied.”

The petals, dyed red by blood, had scattered all over the ground. That day, Xi Rongyan felt as if her heart had been clawed open.

She didn’t even dare to recall that scene again.

Her fingers tightened slightly, and Xi Rongyan felt as though something was stuck in her throat, unable to speak.

She lowered her head, holding the teacup, and took a silent sip. The things she had tried so hard to forget were being dug up again, and her heart still ached. She softly said, “Sister, please don’t bring up the past anymore.”

Xie Yumian looked at Xi Rongyan’s downcast eyes and knew her emotions were genuine.

She still had feelings for Gu Yunyu.

Xie Yumian placed her hand on Xi Rongyan’s, her face showing sadness as she looked at her. “We used to be the closest, sharing everything. How did I not know that you had feelings for Young Master Gu as well?”

“But now, seeing you enter the palace, your life will be wasted in the harem. Even if you are favored now, I know you are not happy.”

“The only one who was ever truly sincere to you was Young Master Gu.”

“I only bring it up because it pains me for you.”

Xi Rongyan saw the redness in Xie Yumian’s eyes and lightly pressed her lips together.

In the past, her cousin had known best about her and Brother Gu Yunyu.

During the Lantern Festival, her cousin had accompanied her, masked, to see the lanterns. At that time, Brother Gu Yunyu had stood quietly by her side. Even without speaking, the sense of relaxation and peace had filled her entire being.

She remembered every little detail, but she didn’t dare to recall them.

Because it was all in the past.

---

chapters.title: From Now On, I Will Restraint Myself
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan remained silent, unsure of what to say.

After that incident, there had been a moment when she thought she would never marry. But her fate was often beyond her control.

Entering the palace had not been her wish.

But now that she was here, she shouldn’t dwell on it.

Xi Rongyan hesitated, then simply lowered her gaze without speaking.

Xie Yumian sighed, “If you don’t speak, I can still see that you haven’t forgotten him.”

Xi Rongyan looked up at Xie Yumian. “Sister, please don’t bring up the past anymore. I don’t want to think about it. It’s all over.”

Xie Yumian’s expression was complex. “You know the bond between us since childhood. But when we talk, no one else will know.”

“And besides, Young Master Gu died so innocently. They say his spleen ruptured, and he lost so much blood. Can you truly remain unmoved?”

Yu Zhu, standing behind Xi Rongyan, saw the scene and quickly whispered to Xie Yumian, “Madam Xie, please say less. You know our mistress is soft-hearted. If you keep bringing this up, she’ll be heartbroken for days again.”

Xi Rongyan closed her eyes briefly, her face slightly pale.

The past she had tried so hard to ignore was being brought up again, like a wound that had yet to heal being torn open, causing even more pain.

She stared blankly at the two parrots in the cage in front of her, her voice barely a whisper. “When it happened, how could I not be moved? How could I not be heartbroken?”

“Sister, don’t accuse me of being heartless. I am not a cold and unfeeling person.”

“But what can I do? Do you want me to remember him for the rest of my life?”

Xie Yumian paused, then looked at Xi Rongyan’s downcast eyes. “I know you’ve always been kind and sentimental. I only bring this up because it pains me for Young Master Gu.”

“Don’t blame me, little sister.”

Xi Rongyan’s eyes darkened with a soft shadow, her long lashes trembling slightly, but she shook her head. “I don’t blame you, sister.”

“You should also understand that even if I remember him for the rest of my life, he won’t come back.”

“And now, I just need to walk the path I’m on.”

Xie Yumian looked at Xi Rongyan’s seemingly calm face and pitied her, softly saying, “Young Master Gu is indeed gone, but no other man will treat you as well as he did.”

“The Emperor used to favor Wang Xiuyi for two years, but now he doesn’t visit her anymore.”

“I only feel sorry for you. Such a good match in the past, and now you’re trapped in the depths of the palace. How long can the favor last?”

Xi Rongyan still lowered her gaze, sitting upright on the soft couch. The green jade bracelet on her wrist glowed with a warm luster. She elegantly held a fan, as if she hadn’t taken Xie Yumian’s words to heart, and softly said, “Sister, you should know that constantly dwelling on the past won’t make the present any better.”

Xie Yumian was taken aback. She sighed softly, “It’s my fault for bringing up the past. Let’s not think about it anymore. Let’s go for a walk in the garden.”

But Xi Rongyan had already lost interest.

She slightly turned her head, looking at the peach tree outside, then lowered her gaze again, softly saying, “I’ll accompany you next time, sister.”

Xie Yumian looked at the emotion on Xi Rongyan’s face, hesitated, and then nodded.

She sat for a while longer, and as the sky began to darken, she finally got up to leave.

Xie Yumian stepped out of Guan Ju Palace, lowering her head to look at the drifting peach blossom petals. She clasped her hands together and walked forward with a distant expression.

Meanwhile, Xi Rongyan, sitting in the inner hall, stared at the parrot for a long time before calling Bao Zhu to close the windows.

As the windows shut, the already dim light was blocked, and the room grew darker.

Xi Rongyan sat on the luohan bed with her back to the window, silently resting her chin on the small table, lost in thought.

Yu Zhu saw her expression and feared she would be heartbroken over Xie Yumian’s words. She quietly approached and softly said, “Mistress, you shouldn’t dwell on what Madam Xie said today.”

“Those things are in the past. If you keep thinking about them, you’ll only make yourself suffer.”

Xi Rongyan closed her eyes. The golden thread embroidered peony on her robe shimmered slightly in the folds. The earrings at her temples hung quietly, and the shadow beneath her eyelids revealed a faint trace of sorrow.

Scenes from the past flashed before her eyes.

She also recalled the day she entered the palace, when the other concubines had mocked her.

They thought she was heartless.

Her fingertip traced the butterfly on her fan, her face devoid of any extra expression.

What her cousin had brought up today shouldn’t have been mentioned.

She couldn’t fully trust the palace servants either. If rumors spread, it would be unfavorable for her.

She pondered the deeper meaning behind her cousin’s words, then suppressed her emotions.

When Wei Qi came to accompany Xi Rongyan for dinner in the afternoon, he saw her sitting at the small table, lowering her head to practice calligraphy.

The lit candles illuminated her soft hair, serene and beautiful.

He glanced at the tightly shut windows. The palace lanterns lit up her slow-moving figure as she rose. Wei Qi silently walked toward her.

He took her hand and had her sit beside him, scanning the room. The peach blossoms that had once been in the blue and white porcelain vase on the incense table were now gone.

He suppressed the thoughts in his heart and held Xi Rongyan’s hand in his palm, asking, “Did you go out for a walk today?”

Xi Rongyan shook her head. “No.”

Wei Qi didn’t ask further. He knew Xie Yumian had come over today and brought up that dead man.

Wei Qi’s mood darkened slightly. That Xie Yumian truly seemed determined to court death.

He subtly observed Xi Rongyan’s current expression, then pulled her onto his lap, gripping her hand tightly.

In fact, during the days right after Gu Yunyu’s accident, Wei Qi had been particularly attentive to Xi Rongyan’s situation.

Spies had sent two encrypted letters into the palace daily. He had watched as she cried for Gu Yunyu all night, fainted from grief, and then fell ill with a cold.

He didn’t know how he had endured those nights.

He had almost rushed to her side and claimed her immediately.

Those unbearable nights had passed. Even if Xi Rongyan was still grieving for that dead man now, it was better than back then.

The worst night for him had been when he learned she had considered going to Ciyun Temple to become a nun for the rest of her life, all for Gu Yunyu.

For Gu Yunyu, she had actually considered such a path.

What was this compared to that?

He would treat it as atonement for the wrongs he had done to her in a past life.

Wei Qi’s face remained calm, flawless, as he helped her with food as usual, then wiped her hands after the meal.

He had Gao Yi bring the unfinished memorials, holding her as he sat on the chair in the study, quietly reviewing them.

His large, gentle fingers lightly stroked Xi Rongyan’s back, not minding when she lifted her head to look at the memorials in his hands.

After a long while, Xi Rongyan, sitting in the Emperor’s lap, couldn’t help but ask, “Your Majesty, doesn’t holding this concubine tire you?”

Only then did Wei Qi lower his gaze, shifting his attention to Xi Rongyan’s face.

His silent eyes held a calming stillness, yet also a sharpness that seemed to see through everything.

It made Xi Rongyan feel an inexplicable flutter in her heart.

Wei Qi set down the memorial in his hand, his fingers wrapping around her waist as he looked at the slight fatigue in her eyes. “Are you tired?”

Xi Rongyan didn’t know whether to say she was tired or not. She shifted slightly in the Emperor’s embrace, her gaze falling on his dark robe, then shook her head.

Wei Qi silently studied Xi Rongyan’s expression for a long moment.

The redness at the corners of her eyes had yet to fade. He reached out to touch her eyelids and asked, “Did you not sleep well last night?”

As he spoke, Wei Qi bent down, his tall and broad chest enveloping Xi Rongyan. He inhaled the fragrance from her hair and softly said, “Yan’er, from now on, I will restrain myself.”

“It won’t be for much longer.”

chapters.title: Does Yan'er Like Zhen?
chapters.content:
The warm embrace left Xi Rongyan dazed and at a loss.

She stiffened in the Emperor's arms, unsure how to react.

She knew the Emperor was referring to last night.

Last night, in the middle of the night, she had been half-asleep when the Emperor picked her up again. But she had been too tired then, her resistance negligible, and indeed, she hadn’t slept well.

Now that the Emperor brought it up again, her fingers dug into his waist, she bit her lip, and softly hummed in response.

Wei Qi held her for a long time. He wanted to speak, to keep her company for a while, but even as he opened his mouth, he found his own questions dull.

He still tried, asking, "Did those two parrots bother you today?"

Xi Rongyan shook her head. "They’re very obedient. They only call for me when they’re hungry."

Wei Qi chuckled, lowering his head to look at her, raising an eyebrow. "They call for you when they’re hungry?"

Xi Rongyan, realizing the Emperor didn’t know, said, "They even shout ‘food, food’ when they’re hungry."

"I taught them for a few days. It’s quite amusing."

The parrots had been sent over, but Wei Qi hadn’t so much as glanced at them before having them delivered here.

Now, seeing a hint of different emotion finally appear on Xi Rongyan’s face, he let out a low laugh and said, "Then I’ll have someone send two more over for you another day."

Xi Rongyan quickly shook her head. "Two are enough. If there are four, they’ll really make too much noise."

Wei Qi smiled, reaching out to pinch her cheek. "If they bother you, come find Zhen. Zhen’s place is quite lonely."

As he spoke, Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan and softly said, "You’ve never once come to find Zhen on your own initiative."

Xi Rongyan was left speechless.

Could a concubine just casually go to the Emperor’s quarters?

Moreover, the Emperor spent most of his days in Xuanzheng Hall, a place where concubines weren’t allowed to freely enter.

Then she recalled the jade pendant the Emperor had given her—was that his way of allowing her to go?

Xi Rongyan bit her lip, lowering her gaze. "Your Majesty is burdened with countless affairs of state. This concubine dares not disturb you."

Wei Qi smiled, then lifted her into his arms again. "Zhen likes it when you come to find Zhen. At least then Zhen can feel that you care for Zhen in your heart."

Xi Rongyan looked up in surprise, meeting the Emperor’s gaze as he also lowered his head to look at her. His eyes were gentle, with a hint of a smile.

Then she saw the Emperor smile at her and ask, "Yan’er, do you like Zhen?"

Did she like the Emperor? She didn’t know.

Xi Rongyan’s heart was a tangled mess.

But she knew the Emperor was her reliance in the harem. He had indeed been extremely good to her, treating her with warmth and consideration in every way. She understood all of this in her heart.

Yet, she was also painfully clear-headed.

She opened her mouth, and naturally, the answer was about to slip out when the Emperor suddenly lowered his head and kissed the corner of her lips. "Sleep."

Her words were forcibly swallowed back into her throat.

That night, as they fell asleep, the Emperor only held her, with no other intentions.

Xi Rongyan had still felt some aches in her body, and seeing that the Emperor made no further moves, she secretly sighed in relief.

If it were like last night again, she truly wouldn’t be able to endure it.

She rested her head in the crook of the Emperor’s arm, but even with her eyes closed, she dreamed of bloody scenes.

She dreamed of Brother Yunyu, pale-faced, standing before her, asking why she had so quickly thrown herself into another man’s arms. He asked if she had forgotten everything he had done for her in the past.

Brother Yunyu had a dagger embedded in his chest, and he reached out to her with a bloodied hand.

Xi Rongyan jolted awake from the dream, her surroundings silent, her heart pounding like a drum.

Her cousin’s words today had stirred up the memories she had tried so hard to forget, memories she never wanted to revisit.

In the dim bed curtains, she lifted her head to look at the Emperor, then buried her face in the nape of his neck. Her heart was beating wildly, thump, thump, not knowing what to do.

Then she turned away from the Emperor’s embrace.

Behind her, Wei Qi opened his eyes, watching her turned back. His expression gradually darkened.

He had clearly heard her murmur "Brother Yunyu" in her dream.

In the morning, when Xi Rongyan woke, she found that the Emperor had already been up for a long time.

She propped herself up from the bed, and the Emperor was just entering from outside.

Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan’s tired, sleepy eyes and said softly, "You don’t need to wake up early with Zhen. Sleep a little longer."

Xi Rongyan looked up at the Emperor in the light. His calm, handsome face flickered in the candlelight, and the slight darkness in his eyes made her feel a flicker of fear in that moment.

She nodded, then lowered her gaze.

Before leaving, Wei Qi still pulled her into his arms for a hug, his fingers gently stroking her loose black hair before finally departing.

The sky was still not bright, and the chilly spring of the third month had not yet fully passed.

The eunuchs held lanterns on either side of Wei Qi, their light illuminating his dragon robes swaying in the breeze as he walked slowly forward.

His expression was no longer the gentle one he had worn inside the room. The coldness in his eyes even made the nearby Gao Yi shiver.

---

In the morning, after Xi Rongyan left the Empress’s place, Qi Consort walked beside her, glanced at her, and sneered, "What made you think to go to Her Majesty the Empress today?"

With another cold laugh, she slanted a glance at Xi Rongyan and whispered, "I’d like to see how long you can stay in favor."

With that, she brushed past Xi Rongyan.

Xi Rongyan watched Qi Consort’s retreating back, surrounded by her entourage, and felt nothing.

Xie Yuwen then took the initiative to walk up to Xi Rongyan, linking arms with her. "Let’s walk back together."

She asked, "What did Consort Qi say to you just now?"

"Did she say anything to make things difficult for you?"

Xi Rongyan shook her head. "Nothing much. I didn’t take it to heart."

Xie Yuwen laughed. "That’s true. His Majesty has stayed with you for more than half a month. She wouldn’t dare do anything to you."

Xi Rongyan said nothing, instead asking Xie Yuwen, "Is everything well with you in Huayang Palace, sister?"

Xie Yuwen’s face stiffened for a moment before she forced a smile. "Very well."

In Huayang Palace, Consort Huang, who had once been close to the Virtuous Consort, certainly wouldn’t treat her well. Behind her back, she was ignored and gossiped about—Xie Yuwen understood all of this in her heart.

But all of this was because of Xi Rongyan, wasn’t it?

And now she was pretending to care.

Wang Baoran stood behind, watching Xie Yuwen and Xi Rongyan’s backs. As she was about to leave in another direction, a palace maid from the Empress’s palace approached her and whispered, "Her Majesty the Empress invites Wang Xiuyi to come in for a talk."

Wang Baoran paused, then quickly responded with a respectful expression.

She entered the Empress’s chambers cautiously, greeting her with extreme care. She knew all too well what kind of person the Empress was.

Beneath her gentle facade lay a cold indifference. She had never shown mercy to any concubine or servant who made a mistake.

In the past, the Emperor had never concerned himself with the harem, rarely entering it, so the Empress had held the power of life and death over them.

Song Helan did not let Wang Baoran sit, merely sitting upright in her place as she looked at Wang Baoran with a faint smile. "I’ve heard you’ve been getting along quite well with Consort Zhen lately."

Wang Baoran kept her face calm. "This concubine’s relationship with Her Majesty Consort Zhen cannot be called close. We merely exchange a few words when we meet."

Song Helan glanced at Wang Baoran, smiling. "Don’t be nervous. I’m not here to reprimand you."

"I was worried that you and Consort Zhen might not get along, given that you were once favored. Now that I see you can coexist peacefully, I’m relieved."

As she spoke, Song Helan sighed regretfully. "Before, when His Majesty favored you so, I had even thought that once you showed signs of pregnancy, I would suggest to His Majesty to elevate your status. Now, it seems, that’s a pity."

---

chapters.title: The Black Dragon Robe
chapters.content:
Wang Baoran understood the Empress’s intentions all too well.

The person in the harem most afraid of Xi Rongyan gaining favor and bearing a prince was probably her.

She forced a sad expression. "It’s only because this concubine lacks the fortune."

Song Helan watched Wang Baoran’s expression impassively, fiddling with her nails before slowly saying, "How do you know you don’t have the fortune if you don’t try?"

"Your father is getting old, your eldest brother isn’t very capable, and your second brother still hasn’t entered officialdom."

"If you were to gain His Majesty’s favor, your brothers would naturally have a future."

Wang Baoran pressed her lips together.

When the Emperor had first ascended the throne, her family had pinned their hopes on her and sent her into the palace.

Her father had spent his whole life scheming and climbing, yet he was only a minor official, a Shaoqing in the Honglu Temple, a fifth-rank position.

Her family was not like other noble clans. They had only followed her grandfather to the capital, with few connections, and her father was not the type to cultivate relationships.

Other noble families’ sons, no matter how mediocre, could still receive recommendations, enter officialdom through family connections, or serve as attendants or guards in the Emperor’s presence. But her father couldn’t pull any strings, and her eldest brother had repeatedly failed the imperial examinations, making it difficult to find a good marriage in the capital.

She knew her family’s struggles and that her father had placed all his hopes on her.

From the moment she entered the palace, she understood the Emperor’s cold nature. Flattery and ingratiation had no effect on him.

She had been cautious and careful by his side, not seeking immediate gains, at least appearing favored in the eyes of others.

She had thought that over time, the Emperor would grow accustomed to her, perhaps even develop feelings for her that he didn’t have for others.

But then, Xi Rongyan entered the palace.

Now, the Empress had spoken, her meaning clear: she wanted her to compete with Xi Rongyan.

If she said she didn’t want to compete, in the Empress’s eyes, she would likely become a target, forced to compete.

Wang Baoran pondered briefly, then lifted her gaze, a hint of reluctance in her eyes. "This concubine also desires His Majesty’s favor. It’s just that this concubine doesn’t understand why His Majesty favors Consort Zhen so much."

"I’ve been getting close to Consort Zhen precisely to gain her trust and see what methods she’s using."

Song Helan was satisfied with Wang Baoran’s reaction. She smiled. "I have high hopes for you."

As she spoke, she had someone bring a small box to Wang Baoran. "Your looks are not inferior to Consort Zhen’s. With a little more adornment, you might even surpass her."

"These jewelry pieces are my gift to you. Dress yourself up properly in the future."

"Who knows? Maybe one day, His Majesty will remember you again."

Wang Baoran quickly accepted the box with gratitude, then knelt to perform a grand salute to the Empress.

Song Helan was very pleased with Wang Baoran’s reaction. She smiled slightly and added, "Speaking of which, my Zhongjing Houfu’s eldest branch has a younger sister of marriageable age. She would make a fine match for your eldest brother."

"Once your family and my Houfu are connected by marriage, we’ll be relatives. As for your second brother entering officialdom, when the time comes for the imperial examinations, my Houfu will naturally lend a hand where we can."

Wang Baoran was taken aback, looking up at the Empress’s meaningful smile before lowering her gaze again in gratitude.

After leaving the Empress’s chambers, Wang Baoran looked at the heavy box in her hands, her expression complex.

For someone like her, with no background, surviving in the depths of the palace was too difficult. She couldn’t afford to offend either side.

It seemed even her hope to watch the Empress and Xi Rongyan fight wasn’t so easy.

As she continued walking, a palace servant behind her whispered, "Her Majesty the Empress holds you in such high regard. You should align yourself with her. If you can connect with the Zhongjing Houfu, you’ll have connections in the future."

Wang Baoran silently glanced at her but said nothing.

Everything came with conditions. No one gave anything for free.

---

Meanwhile, Xi Rongyan and Xie Yuwen had gone to sit in the Wanchun Pavilion in the garden.

The weather wasn’t particularly good today—slightly overcast, as if it might rain soon.

In a little while, it would be the Qingming Festival, and the sky did look like it was about to pour.

Next to the Wanchun Pavilion grew willow trees, and beneath the pavilion stretched a lake, on which small boats floated for the concubines to enjoy the scenery.

Xie Yuwen suggested going on a boat to look around, but Xi Rongyan wasn’t in the mood. She leaned on the red-lacquered railing, quietly gazing at the reflection in the water. The magnolia flowers around her were also reflected in the water, as if she weren’t in the depths of the palace but back in the courtyard behind her boudoir.

Xie Yuwen then softly reminisced, "Looking at that boat reminds me of the year you and I went to see the lotus flowers. We sat in a small boat admiring them, and then your fan fell into the water. At that time, Young Master Gu was on the shore, watching us from afar. When he saw your fan fall, he jumped into the lake without hesitation."

"Back then, you were so frightened, watching Young Master Gu search for your fan in the water. Didn’t you even cry for him?"

Xi Rongyan froze, then closed her eyes.

Yu Zhu, standing behind her, watched with anxiety.

When they had first entered the palace, her mistress had encouraged her to interact more with Lady Xie. Now, she was afraid of them talking at all.

Why bring up old wounds? That person was already dead.

Xie Yuwen saw Xi Rongyan’s pale face and, seeing that she wasn’t speaking, took a folded fan from a servant behind her and placed it in front of Xi Rongyan. "Sister, do you remember this fan?"

Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze, taking the fan from Xie Yuwen’s hand and unfolding it. Her fingers trembled involuntarily.

Of course she remembered this fan, and that day.

It was just a fan. She had told Brother Yunyu not to bother, that it was fine to let it go.

But Brother Yunyu had said it was her favorite jade-bone fan and had searched for it in the water for a long time.

Later, when the fan was found, the surface was dirty. Brother Yunyu had given her his own fan, which had a plum blossom pattern she had painted on it herself.

She had merely painted on it on a whim, yet Brother Yunyu had always carried it with him.

Xi Rongyan turned her head to look at Xie Yuwen. "How did this fan end up with you, sister?"

Xie Yuwen smiled. "You’ve forgotten? At the time, I also asked you to paint one for me, similar to Young Master Gu’s."

Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze, tightening her grip for a moment before placing the fan back in Xie Yuwen’s hand. "Oh, I see."

Xie Yuwen, however, placed the fan back into Xi Rongyan’s hand. "You keep it, sister. This fan might serve as a memento for you."

Xi Rongyan shook her head, quietly looking at Xie Yuwen. "Sister, it’s all in the past."

"I told you yesterday as well—let’s not bring it up again."

"There are many people in the palace. You should understand."

Xie Yuwen didn’t insist, merely sighing naturally. "You’re right."

"Still, be careful, sister."

"But lately, I don’t know why, but I keep thinking about the past."

"Back then, we could still go out to see temple fairs, visit shops, and watch plays. Now, we can only stay here, comforting each other with conversation."

Xi Rongyan looked into the distance, then back at the nearby blossoms, silent, not knowing what to say.

It seemed that every word they spoke could dredge up a past that could never be returned to.

Just then, a eunuch’s voice suddenly announced from behind that the Emperor was approaching. Both women were startled and quickly rose from their seats. Looking up, they saw the Emperor’s black dragon robe as he walked toward them.

Xie Yuwen lowered her head, seeing the black boots with dragon embroidery before her, then heard a steady voice above her. "Rise."

Her heart pounded as she lifted her head, and in that instant, she met the Emperor’s gaze—he was looking at her.

chapters.title: Yan'er, You've Suffered
chapters.content:
The Emperor's eyes were cold yet composed.

Yet they could unknowingly draw one in, making them long to be the most special one in his gaze.

Who in this world wouldn't want to be the special one by the side of the most noble man?

Xie Yumian's cheeks flushed unconsciously, but when she saw the Emperor's gaze shift to Xi Rongyan, her expression turned cold again.

Xi Rongyan hadn't expected to encounter the Emperor in the garden that morning. The gentle breeze brushed against her sore eyes, and she didn't dare to look up at the Emperor. She kept her eyelids lowered, feeling somewhat nervous.

The Emperor, however, reached out and brushed away the redness at the corner of her eye, then pulled her shoulder toward a quiet path.

Xie Yumian watched as the Emperor walked away with Xi Rongyan in his arms, without so much as a glance back at her.

Her fingers tightened, and a sense of injustice welled up in her heart.

She didn't understand. She had entered the palace earlier than Xi Rongyan. In the Emperor's eyes, what exactly was she lacking compared to Xi Rongyan?

Gao Yi still stood in place, looking at Xie Yumian with a smile. "Consort Xie, you do resemble Consort Zhen quite a bit."

Xie Yumian was taken aback and turned her head to look at Gao Yi. "What do you mean by that, Eunuch Gao?"

Gao Yi smiled. "Earlier, His Majesty mentioned to me that Consort Xie resembles Consort Zhen. Today, seeing you both standing together, it truly is the case."

"I didn't expect His Majesty to have noticed that."

As he spoke, Gao Yi leaned closer to Xie Yumian in a seemingly familiar manner and smiled again. "Looking at it this way, Consort Xie will have a bright future ahead."

After saying this, Gao Yi smiled at Xie Yumian once more before hurrying off in the direction the Emperor had gone.

Xie Yumian, however, remained frozen in place, her mind repeatedly replaying the words Eunuch Gao had just said to her.

No wonder the Emperor had looked at her as soon as he arrived.

If only Xi Rongyan were out of the picture, would the Emperor look at her more?

If Xi Rongyan could gain favor, why couldn't she?

Eunuch Gao was always by the Emperor's side. Just now, he had spoken to her with such meaningful words. Could it be that the Emperor might also like her?

She stared blankly at the fan in her hand, her fingers tightening their grip.

It wasn't that she had wronged Xi Rongyan first; it was Xi Rongyan who had wronged her.

Meanwhile, Xi Rongyan was being led deeper into the garden by the Emperor. The garden was very quiet, as if someone was guarding it from afar, and not a single person was in sight.

Suddenly, the Emperor paused, and Xi Rongyan stopped as well.

She felt her chin being lifted by the Emperor, and when she looked up, she met a pair of deep, dark eyes, still filled with gentle concern. "Why are your eyes red?"

Xi Rongyan, seeing the Emperor's concerned gaze, felt a sudden pang of guilt.

She quickly shook her head, her voice hoarse. "It's just that some dust blew into my eyes."

Emperor Wei Qi sighed, bending down to gently kiss her eyes. "Is that so?"

As he spoke, Wei Qi wrapped his arm around Xi Rongyan's waist, pressing her against the flower stand, and bent down to look at her. "I've heard that Yan'er used to be skilled at painting flowers. Could you paint a fan for me?"

Xi Rongyan looked up in surprise. Just moments ago, she had been talking to her cousin about the past, and now the Emperor was asking her for a fan. She worried that the Emperor had overheard her conversation with her cousin.

Seeing Xi Rongyan's dazed expression, Wei Qi's eyes darkened with a hint of disappointment. "Does Yan'er not want to?"

Xi Rongyan quickly replied, "This concubine is naturally willing."

Wei Qi let out a low laugh, then lowered his head and captured her full, rosy lips in a kiss. "I know Yan'er has me in her heart."

Xi Rongyan tilted her head up slightly, the Emperor's kiss gentle and lingering. Her mind went blank, and by the time it ended, she was leaning against the Emperor's chest, breathing lightly.

If not for the Emperor's hand supporting her waist, she felt as if her entire body had gone limp.

The Emperor, however, still asked calmly, "When can I get Yan'er's fan?"

Xi Rongyan finally regained a bit of her senses and softly asked, "What kind of flower does Your Majesty want?"

Wei Qi smiled. "I like whatever Yan'er paints."

At lunchtime, Xi Rongyan dined in the Mingde Hall. After the meal, the Emperor even brought her medicine, feeding her spoonful by spoonful.

Curious, Xi Rongyan asked what the medicine was. She took a sip and found it extremely bitter.

She had never been able to take medicine since she was a child; every time she had to drink it, she would vomit.

This time was no exception, and the bitterness made her forehead sweat.

Seeing her reaction, Wei Qi paused, set the medicine bowl aside, and pulled her tightly into his embrace, gently patting her back.

He knew that Xi Rongyan had always had difficulty taking medicine.

The first time he had fed her medicine, she had vomited all over him. He had thought she was so disgusted by him that even the medicine he fed her made her sick. That time, he had tightly gripped her chin, forced her mouth open, and poured the entire bowl of medicine down her throat.

When she vomited, he had continued to pour more into her mouth. In the end, both of their clothes were soaked, her face pale as she curled up in a ball, clutching her chest.

When he approached her, he realized her jaw was dislocated. Tears and her disheveled hair were scattered across her face. She didn't make a sound despite the pain; the tears simply fell blankly down her cheeks.

He had spent the whole night holding her and coaxing her, but she hadn't spoken a single word to him since.

Later, he learned from her brother that she genuinely feared taking medicine.

Since she was a child, she had rarely been ill and thus rarely taken medicine. The mere smell of it from afar made her nauseous. Back then, medicine was prepared far away from her.

If she ever fell ill, it took a lot of coaxing to get her to take the medicine.

It was innate, and fortunately, she hadn't been ill much from childhood to adulthood.

Wei Qi deeply regretted how he had treated her that day.

In truth, Wei Qi didn't want her to take medicine now either. But her body was weak, and recently, Xie Yumian had brought up past events, and he couldn't just kill that woman to make Xi Rongyan hate her.

He was indeed somewhat afraid. He couldn't wait for her to slowly accept him and wanted to quickly replace that dead man's place with a child.

This medicine was specially prepared for Xi Rongyan to help her conceive faster.

They had had a child before, but it had died less than a month into the pregnancy.

It was Xi Rongyan who had killed their child.

Wei Qi felt the trembling body in his arms, his gaze dark and silent with a hint of gloom.

He closed his eyes until the trembling stopped. Then, he placed a very sweet plum into her mouth and carefully fed her another bite. "The weather has been chilly this spring. This is a medicine to warm the body. I had the Imperial Physician prepare it specially for you. It will be good for your health."

"Yan'er, just one small bowl a day. Endure it, and it will be over soon."

Xi Rongyan had the plum in her mouth, but the sweetness still couldn't mask the overwhelming bitterness.

She looked at the Emperor's concerned gaze, enduring the dry heaving in her stomach, and obediently nodded.

Fortunately, the Emperor fed her slowly, so she didn't vomit. But after finishing the bowl, she felt extremely unwell.

Wei Qi used a white handkerchief to wipe away the medicine residue from Xi Rongyan's lips. Watching her bite her lip in silent endurance, he was reminded of the time she had curled up, tears falling silently.

He lowered his head and kissed her, tenderly sweeping away every trace of bitterness in her mouth. Then, he tightly gripped her waist and pressed her against his chest.

It wasn't until Xi Rongyan let out a soft whimper that he released her.

The woman in his arms had teary eyes, her dark hair cascading softly. Her lips were a delicate red, and the earrings at her ears swayed at his fingertips. Her fair skin had a faint blush of spring passion, clear and alluring to the extreme.

In front of her, he always suppressed his desires. Even though she had been in the palace for so long, the only time he had truly taken her was that one night.

He licked the bitterness from his mouth, then lowered his head to rest on her shoulder, still hiding all the emotions he could barely suppress in his eyes. Then, he softly said, "Yan'er, you've suffered."

Just like that night when he had held the fragile, pale woman whose collar was soaked in medicine and apologized.

---

chapters.title: Painting the Fan
chapters.content:
The low, deep voice was like a tender murmur in the night, filled with affection and indulgence, as if she were a treasure being cherished by the man before her.

Her cheek pressed against the Emperor's warm chest, and she lightly lifted her eyes to see his rolling Adam's apple and strong arms holding her, which calmed her restless heart.

She found herself growing somewhat attached to the Emperor's scent and warmth.

The ground reflected the overlapping shadows of the two of them. She stared at it in a daze, her restless fingers unconsciously tightening their grip on the Emperor's clothes.

She was like a lone boat, her emotions beyond her control, wandering and turning, with countless twists and turns.

She didn't know where her heart truly belonged.

She closed her eyes and buried her face deeply into the Emperor's chest.

The next day, the Emperor sent someone to deliver a blank folding fan to Xi Rongyan.

Looking at the fan, Xi Rongyan understood the Emperor's intention.

She felt a bit nervous, afraid that her painting wouldn't be good enough. So she went to the study and had Baozhu quickly prepare the inkstone.

Xie Yumian happened to be there and asked about it.

As Xi Rongyan spread the paper, she recounted the events of the previous day.

Xie Yumian paused, thinking that it was quite a coincidence.

In this world, perhaps no man could tolerate his woman having another man in her heart. The Emperor, being the supreme ruler, was no exception.

She wanted the Emperor to know that Xi Rongyan still had someone else in her heart.

Then, Xi Rongyan would likely never gain favor again.

Xi Rongyan selected a suitable brush, dipped it in ink, and decided to sketch a small draft on paper first.

Ever since the Gu family's incident, she hadn't painted in a long time. Now, two months had passed. She looked down at the blank paper before her, then at the unfamiliar surroundings of the study, which were so different from her former boudoir, and felt a different frame of mind.

Xie Yumian, sitting beside her, asked with a smile, "What are you planning to paint, sister?"

Xi Rongyan thought carefully for a moment. "Orchids, perhaps. They are the juniors of flowers, elegant and refined."

"The Emperor is usually reserved and speaks little. He probably doesn't like flowers that are too garish."

Xie Yumian smiled again. "Then why don't you paint plum blossoms for the Emperor, like the ones you painted for Young Master Gu?"

"Wouldn't that better suit the Emperor's cold and detached nature?"

Xi Rongyan hesitated.

She didn't actually think the Emperor was cold and detached. She felt that the Emperor was probably just naturally stern and reserved, yet gentle.

She shook her head. "Forget the plum blossoms."

With that, she lowered her head and began to paint.

Xie Yumian glanced at Xi Rongyan's profile indifferently, then smiled.

By afternoon, the finished fan was sent to the Xuanzheng Hall.

Wei Qi leaned back in his chair and slowly unfolded the fan. A painting of orchids appeared before his eyes on the silk surface.

The brushwork was exquisite, the foundation solid, and it was filled with delicate thoughts.

Wei Qi smiled.

He then ordered Gao Yi to select some of the recently tribute glassware from Tianzhu and Persian brocade to be sent to the Hanyuan Hall.

That night, just as he was about to go to the Hanyuan Hall, Gao Yi came again with a message: Wei Heng was ill.

Wei Qi paused in his steps but still proceeded to the Changchun Palace.

He hadn't visited the Changchun Palace in two consecutive months. As soon as he entered, he saw the Empress, with red-rimmed eyes, coming out to greet him. She looked haggard and, upon seeing him, immediately leaned into his arms, sobbing. "Heng'er has been unwell since this morning. I knew Your Majesty is busy with state affairs and didn't want to disturb you."

"But just now, Physician Wang and Physician Chen came to see him. They said if Heng'er's high fever doesn't break, I'm afraid... I'm afraid he might..."

Wei Qi frowned slightly as he looked at the weeping woman in his arms. The golden hairpin in her hair shimmered as it swayed, the phoenix hairpin catching his eye. He pressed his lips tightly together, then looked up and patted her shoulder, his voice low. "I'll go see him."

Empress Song Helan, understanding, stepped back from Wei Qi's embrace, wiped her tears, and followed behind the Emperor.

Wei Qi walked toward the eastern chamber's bedroom. At the very back, a small figure lay on the bed.

He approached, and on the bed, Wei Heng had his eyes tightly closed, his face pale, and his lips dry and peeling. A palace maid knelt beside him, occasionally using a hot towel to wipe the sweat from Wei Heng's forehead.

Wei Qi frowned as he sat by the bed. Out of the corner of his eye, he glanced at the still-tearful Empress and asked, "What happened?"

Song Helan composed herself and looked at the Emperor, choking back sobs. "Heng'er has always trusted and relied on his former teacher, Mr. Lin. He often said that Mr. Lin taught him many principles of being a person and a minister."

"Now that Heng'er has a new teacher, he has been upset and hasn't eaten well for several days. Last night, he suddenly got up and sat outside, exposed to the cold wind all night."

"This morning, when he fell ill, the first thing Heng'er said to me was that Father Emperor doesn't like him anymore."

As she spoke, tears welled up even more in Song Helan's eyes. "Heng'er has always studied diligently. He often said that as long as he worked hard and performed well in front of Father Emperor, Father Emperor would like him."

"But after the last examination in front of Your Majesty, Heng'er has been depressed. Since Mr. Lin left, Heng'er has been even more despondent."

"That's why..."

Wei Qi listened indifferently, then glanced at Song Helan with the same detachment.

His fingers tapped on his knee, and the jade ring on his thumb exuded a cold and imposing aura against his dark robe.

Grand Tutor Lin had served through three dynasties, and the Lin family was a century-old prominent family in the capital, with many descendants and students. He had been specially chosen by Wei Qi to be Wei Heng's teacher.

Wei Heng was his legitimate eldest son. One day, if he could become a qualified crown prince, Wei Qi had intended to entrust the throne to him.

But he had changed his mind.

The Empress knelt before him again, tears in her eyes as she choked out, "I don't ask Your Majesty to change his mind. It's just that Heng'er has always hoped that Your Majesty would look at him more. If Heng'er wakes up tomorrow morning and sees Your Majesty, he will surely be happy."

"He also knows that his Father Emperor cares for him."

Wei Qi's cold and inscrutable face still revealed no emotion, even in the flickering light of the palace lanterns.

No one could ever fathom his thoughts.

Song Helan looked up at the Emperor's expression, suppressing a long-held resentment deep within her.

Even now, as the Emperor sat by Wei Heng's bedside, his face showed no trace of concern.

In many ways, she felt that the Emperor seemed emotionless, cold, and even expressionless.

After seven years of marriage, she had never truly understood the Emperor.

Now, the Emperor had suddenly changed Wei Heng's teacher, and she couldn't see through his intentions, but she could sense something amiss.

Even if the Emperor's public reason was that Grand Tutor Lin was too old, she didn't believe it.

After a long silence, Wei Qi finally lowered his eyes to look at the Empress kneeling before him. He frowned. "You need not kneel."

"Heng'er is seriously ill. Naturally, I am concerned."

"I will stay in the Changchun Palace tonight."

With that, he turned his head and ordered Gao Yi to summon Physician Chen again to stay and watch over Wei Heng all night.

Song Helan's heart suddenly eased.

No matter how cold the Emperor was, Heng'er was still his eldest son, and he had always cared for him.

She stood up and sat beside the Emperor, looking at his thin lips. She wanted to lean against him but maintained her composure, speaking softly with a hoarse voice, "Your Majesty still has morning court tomorrow. Let me stay here and keep watch."

chapters.title: Always Playing Small Only Makes Her More Arrogant
chapters.content:
The two of them usually only exchanged polite pleasantries in public, and had almost no private conversations even when standing together.

Scenes like today, where they sat together, were rare.

In the past, when Wei Qi was in the northern region, he was almost always in the military camp and rarely returned to the palace.

Wei Heng had not been in good health as a child, and she had always been the one to take care of him alone. The Emperor would at most ask a few questions or visit briefly after the child recovered, and that would count as concern.

Later, after the Emperor ascended the throne, he became even busier and inquired about Heng even less.

In the past, Song Helan did not mind much either. The Emperor being busy and not favoring his concubines was a good thing for her.

Now, she had to use her child to seize a place in the Emperor’s heart.

At least she was his wife of seven years, and her father had always loyally supported the Emperor in taking the throne.

Wei Qi glanced at the Empress and saw her eyes red and swollen, on the verge of tears. He said, "You go rest first. There’s no need for you to worry about this."

Song Helan shook her head in distress. "Heng’er is so ill, this subject concubine cannot sleep either."

Wei Qi said nothing more, stood up, and walked to the window, clasping his hands behind his back.

Song Helan stared blankly at the Emperor’s back, hesitated for a moment, then still walked over and asked softly, "Last time during the examination, did Heng’er disappoint Your Majesty?"

Wei Qi remained silent, as if he hadn’t heard the Empress’s words.

Song Helan stood there for a long time.

But she was already used to this. There had been many such scenes in the past.

When the Emperor did not want to talk, no matter what she said, she would only receive silence in return.

She had tried many times before. The Emperor neither rejected her nor responded, as if she did not exist at all.

When Physician Chen arrived and saw the Emperor was also there, he quickly knelt down.

Wei Qi turned and asked Physician Chen, "What caused the illness to be so severe?"

Physician Chen hurriedly replied, "The Crown Prince was invaded by wind-cold, and his unstable emotions led to severe chills and high fever, which caused him to faint."

"As long as the high fever subsides and we warm the meridians and unblock the collaterals, he will gradually recover."

Wei Qi nodded and did not ask further. He only ordered Physician Chen to stay and watch over, then left.

Song Helan quickly followed behind the Emperor and hurriedly ordered the palace servants to bring hot water.

Wei Qi heard the Empress’s arrangements from behind. His steps, which had already reached the doorway, paused once more.

He wearily rubbed his brow. Remembering that he had said he would stay in Changchun Palace, he ultimately did not leave and turned back.

A memorial had already been submitted saying that changing Heng’er’s teacher was unwise, and for now, it was necessary to stabilize the court’s opinions.

Song Helan’s heart rejoiced, and she quickly went to attend to the Emperor closely.

Wei Qi waved his hand, had the servants follow to help him wash up, then sat on the edge of the bed. He glanced at the Empress sitting beside him, frowned slightly, and then lay down first.

Song Helan was already used to such interactions. If she did not take the initiative, it was as if the Emperor had never noticed her at all.

But she had long stopped hoping that the Emperor would treat her with tenderness or that they would share affection again.

All she wanted was her own future power.

All the love she once had for the Emperor had long since been worn away. She also knew that the Emperor would not touch her.

Since Heng’er was born, the Emperor had never touched her again.

She felt no sadness. Lying beside the Emperor, she did not even reach out to touch him with her fingers.

Having the Emperor stay with her was only to show the outside world that the Emperor still cared for his eldest son.

The next day, all the palaces received the news that the morning assembly at the Empress’s place was canceled.

It turned out that the Crown Prince was ill, and the Emperor had stayed by his side all night in Changchun Palace, so the morning assembly was canceled for the day.

The Crown Prince was the Emperor’s only son. Now that he was seriously ill, many concubines, regardless of their intentions, had to go and visit him.

Xi Rongyan also prepared to go in the morning.

When she arrived, there were already several concubines standing in the outer room, all looking inside with concern.

When Xi Rongyan arrived, she was also stopped outside and told that the Crown Prince needed quiet rest and it was inconvenient to visit.

She looked around and saw that no one left despite this. They all stood outside waiting.

It seemed they all knew the Emperor was inside and wanted to show their concern for the Crown Prince in front of the Emperor.

Xie Yumian came to Xi Rongyan’s side and whispered, "Did the Emperor go to your place last night?"

Xi Rongyan shook her head.

Xie Yumian leaned close to Xi Rongyan’s ear and whispered, "It seems the Emperor really stayed in Changchun Palace all night."

As she spoke, she looked at Xi Rongyan’s face, pulled her to a corner, and said, "It seems the Emperor still values the Crown Prince highly. Maybe he will be established as the Crown Prince soon."

Xi Rongyan did not understand why her cousin was telling her this, and with so many people standing around, it was really not appropriate to discuss this.

She whispered, "That is the Emperor’s business. We should not speculate."

Xie Yumian raised her eyebrows at Xi Rongyan, curled her lips, and said nothing.

She was now somewhat tired of Xi Rongyan’s always feigned indifference.

At this moment, Consort Qi walked to Xi Rongyan’s side, lifted her chin, and glanced at Xi Rongyan with a sideways look, then sneered, "Look at Zhen Concubine’s ruddy face. It seems she has been well-nourished by the Emperor these days."

"Who knows what you’re thinking inside. Yet you come here to put on airs."

Xi Rongyan looked up at Consort Qi and said softly, "Consort Qi, please be careful with your words. The Crown Prince is seriously ill. It is my duty as a concubine to be concerned and come to visit."

Consort Qi coldly laughed, "You do have a way with words."

Then she lowered her head and leaned close to Xi Rongyan, "I’d like to see how long you can stay in favor."

Xi Rongyan met Consort Qi’s gaze, which was filled with unmasked malice, and frowned.

She also whispered, "Does Consort Qi resent every concubine who gains the Emperor’s favor?"

"There are so many of us. Consort Qi must be too busy to resent them all."

Consort Qi’s expression changed, and she gritted her teeth, "How dare you speak to me like this?"

In the past, Xi Rongyan had always tried to keep a low profile, but Consort Qi had always looked down on her.

In terms of background, Consort Qi, Lu Rongyue, did not come from a traditional noble family. Her father had a rough background, had followed the Emperor into battle, and had once saved the Emperor’s life. After the Emperor ascended the throne, he granted the Lu family the title of Earl.

When she first followed the Emperor, she was merely a concubine. Now that she had gained power, relying on her past connection as a former concubine in the Emperor’s princely residence and her closeness to the Empress, she bullied and suppressed the lower-ranking concubines in the harem.

As if everyone should bow and scrape before her.

Xi Rongyan simply stared calmly into Consort Qi’s somewhat furious eyes. "I am only speaking the truth."

"Is Consort Qi so angry because of shame?"

Consort Qi was so angry that she gritted her teeth. She raised her hand to discipline Xi Rongyan but stopped herself in mid-air.

The precedent of the Virtuous Consort was still fresh in her mind.

Moreover, Xi Rongyan was currently in favor, and she was the Empress Dowager’s niece. It was not the right time to discipline her.

If Xi Rongyan complained to the Empress Dowager, even the Empress might not be able to protect her.

She withdrew her hand, coldly huffed, and turned away from Xi Rongyan.

Xie Yumian was surprised by Xi Rongyan’s words to Consort Qi just now and could not help but ask, "Just now, sister, weren’t you afraid of offending Consort Qi?"

Xi Rongyan turned her head to look at Xie Yumian and whispered, "I probably offended her the day I entered the palace."

"They think I am the Empress Dowager’s person. No matter what I do, they will guard against me."

"Besides, whether one offends or not depends on whether one is respectful. Always bowing and scraping will only make her more arrogant."

Xie Yumian looked at Xi Rongyan in surprise. She had not expected Xi Rongyan to have such a strong side.

After standing for a while, a voice came from inside, announcing that the Emperor was coming out. Everyone outside automatically stood to the sides, making way.

---

chapters.title: Pulled Her Into His Embrace
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan did not stand in a conspicuous place but stayed in the most inconspicuous corner at the back.

Her gaze passed through the exquisite hairpins and ornaments of the women standing in front of her, looking toward the Emperor who emerged from the inner room.

His dark silhouette carried a cold aura. His noble and majestic face was weary and indifferent, yet his deep, sharp eyes remained piercing. He walked out together with the Empress, whose hand rested on his arm.

The sight of the two of them walking out together caused the outside to fall silent, and no one dared to look too closely.

Xi Rongyan, along with the others, lowered her head.

From the corner of her eye, she saw the Emperor’s dark robe and the Empress’s skirt hems overlapping as they walked, then the Emperor left first.

The Empress remained in place, telling them all to rise and then to disperse.

A few who were close to the Empress wanted to go in and help attend to her. The Empress, with weary eyes, scanned through the crowd and glanced at Xi Rongyan, then shook her head and told everyone to return.

Hearing that the Crown Prince inside needed rest and had not yet woken up, no one dared to make noise, and they all left quietly.

Xi Rongyan also left with the others. After going out, she heard the low voices of others.

"Rumor has it that the Emperor stayed by the Crown Prince’s side all night and promised that once the Crown Prince recovers, he will be established as the Crown Prince."

Someone else whispered, "The Crown Prince is the Empress’s son. Even if someone else bears a prince in the future, how can they compare to the Crown Prince?"

"The Crown Prince’s teacher was personally selected by the Emperor, precisely for the purpose of grooming him as the future heir."

These words, whether intentional or not, were all heard by Xi Rongyan.

Xi Rongyan’s expression remained calm, and she felt no fluctuation in her heart.

Wang Baoran, standing beside her, observed Xi Rongyan’s expression and came over to chat with her. "Since the Emperor favors you so much, sister, when you have a prince in the future, even if he is not the Crown Prince, you will have support."

Xi Rongyan glanced at Wang Baoran. She had somewhat understood her intentions from her occasional attempts to engage in conversation.

She wanted her to compete with the Empress.

But what did she truly think deep in her heart?

She smiled. "I only follow fate. I only serve the Emperor well and ask for nothing more."

Wang Baoran paused, then smiled again. "Sister, come to my place to talk."

Xi Rongyan shook her head and whispered, "Now that the Crown Prince is seriously ill, it is not appropriate for us to gather often, lest others think we are happy about it."

"I will come find you to talk when there is time later."

Wang Baoran was somewhat impressed by Xi Rongyan’s caution.

She said to Xi Rongyan, who was about to turn away, "This harem is full of the Emperor’s women, but there is only one Emperor."

"Those who appear indifferent on the surface are only burying their ambitions deeper."

"When the opportunity arises, no one will let it slip away."

"The Emperor’s favor toward you is your opportunity. With the Empress Dowager behind you, perhaps you will be the next noble consort in this palace."

After saying this, Wang Baoran left. Xi Rongyan looked at her, then pursed her lips and walked back.

Yuzhu, following behind Xi Rongyan, whispered, "Just now, Consort Wang’s words were telling you to seize the opportunity and compete with the Empress, weren’t they?"

Xi Rongyan lowered her gaze. "I understood."

Yuzhu asked, "Then what does my lady think?"

Xi Rongyan quietly said, "She said that no woman in the harem would let go of the opportunity to rise above others. What about her?"

"What position is she in?"

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan looked up and sighed. "She wants me to bring down the Empress. No matter what her intentions are, we must still be careful."

Yuzhu nodded in agreement. "My lady is right to keep a low profile. The Empress has a prince, and her father is the Emperor’s confidant. She is not so easy to bring down."

Xi Rongyan said nothing and silently walked back.

For several consecutive days, the sky was overcast with a light drizzle.

It was said that the Crown Prince’s illness was still severe. Although he had woken up, he had developed a cough.

The Emperor stayed in Changchun Palace for three consecutive days, and the Empress also did not preside over the morning assembly for three days.

The concubines, however, did not miss a single day of visiting the Empress’s palace.

Xi Rongyan naturally went as well.

On this day, she went with an umbrella. As soon as she arrived at Changchun Palace, she saw the Emperor coming out, and the two of them came face to face.

A fine mist of rain filled the air. Xi Rongyan wore a pale white moonlight cloak, which was also dotted with tiny water droplets blown by the wind.

Wei Qi looked down at Xi Rongyan as she performed the palace greeting, and reached out to support her.

He then took a step forward, lifted her chin, and made her look at him.

The two of them stood in the rain curtain. Behind them, people held umbrellas, and eunuchs and maids stood silently to the side. It was quite conspicuous.

Xi Rongyan also felt it was too eye-catching.

From the corner of her eye, she saw the concubines coming to visit. Although she could not see clearly who they were, she still felt somewhat uncomfortable.

Wei Qi could clearly see Xi Rongyan’s evasive expression. He had not visited her for the past few nights, and today the weather had suddenly turned cold. He was still worried about her health.

Looking at her fair face, Xi Rongyan had been particularly plain these days. Her white jade earrings and the string of pearls around her neck were not noticeable unless one looked closely.

His gaze then fell on the apricot-colored collar of her dress, elegant like a painting.

He lowered his body slightly and asked her, "The wind has been cold these days. You don’t need to come here."

Xi Rongyan was startled and looked at the Emperor, then carefully replied, "The Crown Prince is seriously ill. This subject concubine also prays daily for the Crown Prince’s speedy recovery. I come here to know that the Crown Prince is well so that my heart can be at ease."

Wei Qi’s dark eyes looked at Xi Rongyan, said nothing, but released his fingers from her chin and took her hand, which was slightly cold.

He rubbed it, using the warmth of his palm to warm her fingertips, then asked, "Have you been taking your medicine these days?"

Every day at noon, someone would deliver medicine. Xi Rongyan, who feared bitterness greatly, still endured the discomfort and drank it all down because it was sent by the Emperor.

Xi Rongyan nodded. "I have."

The concubines who had come over were already standing beside them, greeting the Emperor.

Xi Rongyan tried to withdraw her hand, but the Emperor tightened his grip, showing no intention of letting go. He only nodded, signaling them to retreat, and his gaze fell back on Xi Rongyan.

Although he was not pleased with Xi Rongyan’s attempt to pull away just now, he still spoke gently to her, "Heng’er is fine. You don’t need to go to the Empress’s place and stand there. Go back."

He added, "I will come see you when I have time."

Xi Rongyan hesitated in her heart. If everyone else went and she did not, she did not know what the Empress would think.

But Wei Qi had already seen through Xi Rongyan’s thoughts. "I have already told the Empress that starting today, there is no need for visits."

Xi Rongyan then felt somewhat at ease and nodded in agreement.

Wei Qi looked deeply at Xi Rongyan again, noticing her slightly downcast brows and eyes. He tightened his grip on her fingers, exerted a little force, and pulled her into his embrace.

chapters.title: When Has He Ever Been So Considerate?
chapters.content:
It had been two or three days since he last held her, yet the body in his arms was still so soft.

He sighed, gently stroking her hair before softly saying, "Tonight, I will come to dine with you."

Xi Rongyan obediently leaned against the Emperor, giving a light hum in response.
