Wei Qi had wanted to ask if she liked the glassware and brocade he had sent her last time, but seeing the fine rain mixed with wind blowing on Xi Rongyan, he couldn’t bear for her to stay in the rain any longer and released her.

Out of habit, he adjusted the collar of her cloak, then pinched her face, examining her for a long time before letting her leave.

Before departing, Xi Rongyan looked at the Emperor: "Your Majesty, you must also take care of yourself these days. The Crown Prince will surely recover."

Wei Qi pressed his lips together, glanced at Xi Rongyan, nodded, and watched her leave.

Only after her tranquil, pale figure disappeared did he head toward the Xuanzheng Hall.

The scene of the Emperor holding Xi Rongyan outside quickly reached Song Helan’s ears inside the hall.

At this moment, she was sitting by Wei Heng’s bedside, holding a bowl of medicine. She listened indifferently to the nanny’s report, gave a lukewarm "mm," then continued feeding Wei Heng another spoonful of medicine.

Wei Heng looked at his mother, coughed twice, and suddenly asked, "Will Father let Teacher Lin come back?"

Song Helan remained silent. The Emperor had replaced Wei Heng’s teacher with a Hanlin compiler who had no background and only empty scholarship. This was undoubtedly a signal to the court that Wei Heng was no longer as important.

Or perhaps, no one was allowed to have any influence behind Wei Heng.

Her father was far away in the northern region. Even as the Governor of the North, there were still the Emperor’s confidants there monitoring him. Every month, reports were sent back to the Emperor, and even her father didn’t know what was written in them.

But she understood that the Emperor had never truly trusted her father, nor had he completely handed over the North to him.

Apart from her father in the North, her eldest brother, younger brother, and other female relatives were all kept in the capital, given minor, insignificant official positions.

The military power in the North had only been partially given to her father by the Emperor. The other half required General Yue’s approval to mobilize.

General Yue had been with the Emperor longer. The other generals in the North were all personally trained by the Emperor. Her father didn’t dare act recklessly, lest he arouse the Emperor’s suspicion.

Song Helan couldn’t fathom the Emperor’s intentions and was worried by his sudden actions.

Yet, she calmly said, "Tonight, your imperial father will come to see you. You can mention it to him then. Perhaps he will agree."

Although Wei Heng was young, he already understood the importance of Teacher Lin to his future. He nodded solemnly.

After feeding him the medicine, Song Helan had someone attend to the Crown Prince’s rest before wearily stepping out.

She stood by the window, listening to the rain hitting the glass. In the quiet room, she watched the raindrops slide down the window, her heart already weighed down by a massive stone.

Suddenly, she said to Madam Yu, "Is it that Consort Zhen can no longer stay?"

Madam Yu was taken aback. In the privacy of their room, she softly said to the Empress, "His Majesty does indeed treat Consort Zhen differently."

"Just now at the palace gate, His Majesty seemed to pity Consort Zhen being caught in the wind. He even watched her leave with his own eyes before turning away."

"A few days ago, the Imperial Household Department also said that His Majesty had bestowed many fine things upon the Han Yuan Hall, and it was High Eunuch Gong who delivered them personally."

Song Helan’s lips curled into a sarcastic smile. "When has he ever been so considerate?"

"I originally thought he would remain cold and aloof his entire life."

As she spoke, Song Helan closed her eyes. The Emperor’s recent abnormal behavior toward Xi Rongyan forced her to suspect that the Emperor was already paving the way for Consort Zhen’s child.

She had sent someone to the Imperial Pharmacy to inquire and learned that the Emperor had specially prescribed a fertility tonic for Xi Rongyan, which was delivered to Han Yuan Hall every day.

In the past, she had thought the Emperor did not value heirs, or perhaps that the Emperor favored Wei Heng. But now it seemed the Emperor did value heirs—it just depended on whose child it was.

He probably intended to abandon Wei Heng.

Whatever the Emperor decided to do, he would surely accomplish it.

Song Helan asked again, "Is Consort Zhen wearing the bracelet I gave her?"

Madam Yu shook her head. "This old servant looked carefully. It seems she is not."

Song Helan gave a cold, mocking laugh.

She stood silently for a long time until her white cat rubbed against her legs. Only then did she bend down to pick it up.

On her way back, Xi Rongyan was invited by Madam Wan to the Dowager Empress’s place.

As soon as she arrived, the Dowager Empress beckoned Xi Rongyan to sit beside her.

After Xi Rongyan sat down, the Dowager Empress looked at her plain attire and frowned. "Why are you dressed so simply?"

Xi Rongyan looked at the Dowager Empress. "With the Crown Prince gravely ill, this niece cannot dress elaborately."

The Dowager Empress smiled. "Which favored concubine doesn’t draw attention?"

"Even if the Crown Prince is ill, you don’t need to be so plain and cautious."

"As long as you don’t make mistakes, I will protect you."

Then, the Dowager Empress held Xi Rongyan’s hand. "Do you know that His Majesty has replaced Wei Heng’s teacher?"

"He replaced him with a Hanlin compiler who has no family background."

"That compiler passed the imperial examination at thirty, is wooden in personality, and is not good at socializing. He has no connections in the capital and has been in the Hanlin Academy for twenty years. His scholarship is high, but he is too rigid for anyone to like."

"One could also say he is so upright that it borders on the absurd. Even if he can’t feed himself, he insists on giving alms. He doesn’t even own a decent set of clothes."

"By making such a man Wei Heng’s teacher, the other officials in the court will have to reconsider His Majesty’s intentions."

"According to your father, some officials have already submitted memorials to His Majesty, saying this is inappropriate, but His Majesty has ignored them."

The Dowager Empress’s eyes sparkled as she looked at Xi Rongyan. "Regardless of what His Majesty intends by doing this, in my eyes, this is your opportunity. If you give birth to a prince soon, your father and I can better support and plan for you behind the scenes."

Xi Rongyan didn’t want to think about these things. If her aunt could think of them, couldn’t the Empress?

Moreover, only the Emperor knew his true intentions behind such sudden actions.

The Emperor’s eyes always saw everything. Would he be unaware of the concubines’ secret maneuvers?

Furthermore, with the Crown Prince seriously ill, it was said that the Emperor had been personally attending to him at night, proving that the Emperor deeply loved the Crown Prince.

Making reckless moves would only arouse the Emperor’s suspicion.

Seeing Xi Rongyan’s silence, the Dowager Empress sighed deeply. "Rongyan, you have always had a very good temperament since you were young—thoughtful and kind."

"Initially, I never intended for you to enter the palace. But now that you have, and His Majesty currently favors you, you cannot remain detached."

"You must make good use of His Majesty’s favor."

Xi Rongyan raised her head and softly said, "I understand everything Aunt has said."

"It’s just that children cannot be rushed. Please rest assured, Aunt."

The Dowager Empress sighed again and placed a letter in her hand. "This is from your mother. Open it and take a look."

Xi Rongyan was startled as she took it, and after reading a few lines, she felt a pang of sorrow.

Her eldest sister-in-law was pregnant again, but she could no longer go to her sister-in-law’s place to keep her company. She didn’t know when she would have the chance to see her little nephew.

The letter mentioned that her little nephew could already stammer through the Three Character Classic, and she smiled with relief.

---

chapters.title: This Subject Does Not Wish to Disappoint His Majesty’s Kindness
chapters.content:
Days of continuous rain had beaten the peach blossoms in Guanju Palace to the ground. Xi Rongyan stepped on the fallen petals, as if treading on the bloodstained peach blossom branch that the third daughter of the Gu family had once thrown at her feet.

She froze, then took a step back before walking into the hall.

Hurrying back to her bedchamber, she kicked off her wet shoes and suddenly flopped onto the soft pillow.

Closing her eyes, she willed herself not to think.

It was already nearing noon. Yuzhu saw Xi Rongyan suddenly like this and didn’t know what was wrong. She stood beside her and asked, "Has Mistress been saddened by the letter from Madame?"

Xi Rongyan, lying on the pillow, was startled by Yuzhu’s words. After a long pause, she muttered, "Yes, it’s sad."

In the letter, her mother had told her to listen more to her aunt and to interact more with her cousin.

The slow, calm narration, though plain in every word, conveyed her mother’s intention to reassure her.

Then, memories of the past came flooding back.

Baozhu saw Xi Rongyan lying on the bed and softly advised, "It’s been raining these days, and it’s a bit cold. Mistress has just returned from outside. Why not drink a cup of hot tea to warm up first?"

Xi Rongyan nodded. After taking a sip of tea, the warmth spread through her body, and she felt much more comfortable.

After going out and being caught in the cold wind, then reading her mother’s letter, her mind was in turmoil. Buried under the covers, she dozed off and unexpectedly recalled the scene of the Emperor and the Empress coming out together.

She didn’t know why she suddenly thought of that moment.

Lost in thought, she didn’t even hear Yuzhu’s voice beside the bed announcing the Emperor’s arrival.

Wei Qi entered from outside and saw Xi Rongyan buried in the pillow.

Her pale peony dress was wrinkled, gathered at her waist. Only her white silk stockings were half-exposed beneath the hem, and the pink sash around her waist made her look even more slender. Lying on the couch like this, it was rare to see her in such a lazy state, as if she had suffered some great grievance outside.

Wei Qi paused slightly, then walked over and sat beside her. Bending down a little, he caught the warm fragrance from her body. He noticed that the jade hairpin in her hair had fallen onto the pillow. Fearful that she might move and hurt herself, he picked it up between his fingers.

Looking at her fair face half-hidden by her dark hair, he asked, "What’s wrong? Are you tired already?"

Xi Rongyan, eyes closed, was startled by the Emperor’s voice.

These past few days, the Emperor hadn’t come to see her. That morning, when she had met the Emperor, he had said he would come for dinner.

But it was only noon now.

For a moment, Xi Rongyan’s mind went blank. Then, she clearly heard Yuzhu’s slightly anxious voice: "Mistress, His Majesty is here."

Only then did she turn her head and see the Emperor sitting beside her, looking down at her.

His calm eyes were like pools of dark ink, making her feel exposed.

She belatedly propped herself up, then lowered her head as if apologizing for her earlier negligence.

Wei Qi reached out to support Xi Rongyan’s back, then felt her slightly cold face. She looked pale.

He frowned slightly, pulling her into his embrace. Then, he took her cold fingers and warmed them in his palm, looking down at the person in his arms with lowered eyes. "Are you feeling unwell?"

"I’ll call the imperial physician to examine you."

Xi Rongyan then shook her head. "I just came back from outside, and I’m a little cold."

Wei Qi turned his head and ordered Gao Yi outside to have someone send some charcoal to Han Yuan Hall.

Xi Rongyan leaned against the Emperor’s chest, inhaling the scent of dragon’s saliva incense on him. Yet, her heart was restless, and she averted her eyes, staring blankly at the embroidered flowers on the screen opposite her.

Wei Qi pressed his lips together, watching Xi Rongyan’s seemingly dejected appearance. These past few days, Xie Yumian hadn’t come here, and he knew she had just returned from the Dowager Empress’s palace. There was no reason for her mood to suddenly turn bad.

He rubbed her hand, silently watching her for a long time before saying, "After the Qingming Festival, when the weather warms up, I’ll take you to the imperial summer residence for a while."

Xi Rongyan looked up in surprise at the Emperor. When she met his gaze, she couldn’t help but nod blankly.

At this moment, a voice outside announced that the meal was ready. Wei Qi took her hand and helped her up.

Actually, Xi Rongyan didn’t have much of an appetite, but since she was dining with the Emperor, even if she didn’t want to eat, the Emperor kept serving her food, so she had to force herself to eat a little more.

After finishing the meal, the Emperor took the bowl of medicine brought by the palace servant and personally fed it to Xi Rongyan.

In the past, it had always been her mother, brother, or close maids who would gently coax her into taking her medicine when she was ill. Now, the Emperor, like her brother, fed her a mouthful of medicine followed by a sweet date, patiently waiting for her to recover from the bitterness each time.

She stared blankly at the Emperor’s hand holding the porcelain bowl—his knuckles were distinct and long, yet they gave her a sense of stability and peace.

Then, she watched as the Emperor’s other hand wiped the medicine residue from the corner of her mouth before bringing another spoonful to her lips. Though he didn’t say much, his actions were genuinely patient and meticulous, like a brother caring for her.

She lowered her head and drank the medicine the Emperor offered, biting on the date pit between her teeth, blinking her eyes.

But the medicine was too bitter. She endured the nausea and discomfort, gently pushing the Emperor’s hand away, lowering her head into the Emperor’s embrace to catch her breath.

Wei Qi put down the medicine bowl and looked at Xi Rongyan’s pale face and reddened eyes. His heart ached, and he bent down to kiss her forehead, his fingers gently stroking her hair.

He recalled the times he had forced her to take medicine before, how she had never managed to drink it properly, and how he had never taken good care of her or comforted her back then. The guilt and tenderness in his heart grew even stronger.

He knew that in the past, he had left deep scars on Xi Rongyan’s heart, and no matter how hard he tried to make amends later, it would never be enough.

He slightly bent down, gathering the person in his arms, and stroked her hair with tenderness. "Rongyan, if it’s too bitter, you don’t have to drink it."

The Emperor’s broad and warm chest tightly held her. All she could see was his dark robe, and that comforting scent enveloped her, making the redness in her eyes intensify. Unable to help herself, she buried her face tightly in the Emperor’s chest and said hoarsely, "That is the medicine His Majesty specially prescribed for this subject to nourish her body."

"This subject does not wish to disappoint His Majesty’s kindness, nor am I afraid of bitterness."

Wei Qi was taken aback. He looked down at the person buried tightly in his arms, her soft hands gripping his chest firmly.

His expression softened instantly. Such a Xi Rongyan made his heart ache even more.

chapters.title: Lingering Warmth
chapters.content:
At this moment, the rain outside the window continued to drizzle.

Wei Qi bent deeply at the waist, completely enveloping the person in his arms.

He quietly savored this moment, for he could also feel Xi Rongyan gradually leaning on him.

He rejoiced in her reliance.

The charcoal fire had been lit, and the cold room slowly warmed. Xi Rongyan, nestled in Wei Qi’s warm embrace and the rising temperature of the room, had a faint blush creeping onto her face.

The medicine beside them had already cooled, still faintly emitting its herbal scent.

Wei Qi had someone take the medicine away. Seeing that Xi Rongyan in his arms had closed her eyes, seemingly a little drowsy, he smiled.

In his past life, he and Xi Rongyan had tormented each other for nearly three years. Though she resisted him, he still understood all her habits.

She could never overcome spring drowsiness. Back then, even when she quarreled fiercely with him, the moment he left, she would bury herself under the blankets and fall asleep.

Now that she could sleep so peacefully in his arms, perhaps she already had a place for him in her heart.

He gently patted her back, silently coaxing her to sleep. Xi Rongyan, however, buried herself deeper in the Emperor’s arms. Faced with such a gentle Emperor, it reminded her of the brother who had once been so kind to her.

She cherished this warmth.

The incense burned slowly, and Xi Rongyan truly felt drowsy in the Emperor’s arms.

At this moment, a soft voice came from outside: “Your Majesty, Her Majesty the Empress sent someone to say that the Eldest Prince wishes to see you.”

Wei Qi lowered his gaze. Seeing that Xi Rongyan in his arms seemed to have fallen asleep, he carefully picked her up and gently placed her on the bed.

He looked down at her sleeping face—her delicate, painted eyebrows, clear as if untouched by worldly affairs, always stirring a lingering affection in one’s heart.

His fingers brushed past the strands of hair at her temple before gently pulling away.

The moment the Emperor left, Xi Rongyan opened her eyes. She turned her head to look at the Emperor’s retreating figure behind the screen, staring at that spot in a daze.

After Wei Qi left, the dampness of the palace path made his expression turn cold. Sitting in the palanquin, his face under the canopy was calm and indifferent, devoid of the gentleness he had shown earlier in the Hanyuan Hall.

When he arrived at the Changchun Palace, the Empress was already waiting for him at the entrance, her eyes still red-rimmed.

He silently observed the Empress’s demeanor, a hint of impatience flickering in his eyes.

Wei Heng was indeed his son. Even at such a young age, he already knew how to use illness to manipulate his father.

Wei Qi knew exactly how Wei Heng had fallen ill. The eunuchs attending to Wei Heng were all people he had sent, so how could he not know?

He also knew that the Empress must be aware of how Wei Heng had fallen ill.

If it weren’t for the need to stabilize the court’s opinions, he wouldn’t even have the patience to come here these days.

Daring to make moves right under his nose, thinking they had bought everyone over.

Wei Qi let out a long sigh, glanced at the Empress, and walked toward the east room.

Wei Heng was leaning on the couch. The moment he saw his father enter, he tried to get up from the bed.

Wei Qi stepped forward and pressed down on Wei Heng’s shoulder with a heavy hand, rendering him immobile.

Wei Heng felt a slight pain in his shoulder. Pale-faced, he looked at his father until the Emperor’s hand moved away.

Wei Qi then glanced at the Empress, who had followed him in. He sat on the chair beside, leaning back slightly, looking at Wei Heng with no emotion in his eyes: “The matter of your teacher has been decided. Your pleas are useless.”

Wei Heng’s face changed as he looked at Wei Qi, fearfully asking, “Does Father Emperor no longer want this son?”

Wei Qi frowned. “Scholar Wang is erudite, well-versed in ancient and modern texts, and is a man of integrity who does not seek personal gain. He is the right match for you.”

As he spoke, his sharp gaze fixed on Wei Heng: “I will not repeat myself.”

“What I do does not require explanation to you.”

Wei Heng’s face paled. Just as he was about to speak, Song Helan quickly stepped forward and said to Wei Heng, “Heng’er, listen to your father.”

“Your father always has your best interests at heart.”

Wei Heng hesitated. Wei Qi, however, stood up and walked out.

Song Helan had not expected Wei Qi to leave so quickly. She hurriedly followed behind the Emperor, softly pleading, “Heng’er thought that Your Majesty no longer valued him. Please do not blame Heng’er, Your Majesty.”

Wei Qi paused, turning his head to look at the Empress with a cold gaze: “I change his teacher, and he deliberately falls ill. In the future, if I make other decisions, what else will he do?”

With a cold laugh, he added, “This is the fine son you have raised for me.”

Song Helan’s face paled. So the Emperor had known all along that Heng’er had feigned illness.

She recalled the night before last when the Emperor had personally questioned Heng’er’s eunuch, Qin. She had thought she had arranged everything perfectly, and since the Emperor had shown no other expression at the time, she assumed she had deceived him. But it turned out the Emperor had been coldly observing everything all along.

As if watching a clown.

She suddenly felt that the Emperor was exceptionally cruel to her.

He had watched everything unfold without a word. After seven years of marriage, did he have no affection for her at all?

Song Helan tightly clenched her hands, not allowing her face to reveal the slightest crack.

She still stood before the Emperor as the considerate and dignified Empress, bowing her head. “Heng’er was truly heartbroken. Over the years, Your Majesty has been strict with him. When have you ever truly looked at Heng’er?”

“He is only six years old.”

“This was the only way he could get his father’s attention.”

“Your Majesty, how many times have you visited Heng’er on ordinary days?”

“From childhood until now, whenever Heng’er was ill, how many times have you stayed by his side? Wasn’t it always I who took care of him?”

A sarcastic smile tugged at Wei Qi’s lips. “At only six years old, he already has such schemes, thinking of how his future teacher can pave the way for his prospects. Who taught him this?”

“Do you want me to fear my own son?”

“Always thinking about his father’s throne?”

With that, Wei Qi flicked his sleeve and strode past Song Helan.

The cold wind from his sleeve made Song Helan’s entire body stiffen. Watching the Emperor’s retreating back, a flicker of panic appeared in her eyes.

Only now did she realize that her overly eager guidance of Heng’er had long since displeased the Emperor.

Her father had also warned her: which emperor does not harbor suspicion?

Even their own sons must be guarded against.

A slight weakness overcame her, and she collapsed onto the noble concubine’s couch, her panic giving way to a deeper, more ungraspable fear.

She had long since stopped caring about love, but she could not tolerate any threat to her status or her son.

After sitting on the noble concubine’s couch for a long time, Song Helan’s back remained straight. The nearby Nurse Yu approached and softly reminded her: “Concubine Xie has come to visit the Eldest Prince again.”

“She is currently waiting outside the hall. Shall Your Majesty see her?”

Song Helan raised an eyebrow.

She remembered that Xie Yumian had come once that morning, but because she was worried about Heng’er’s illness, she had only seen Qi Fei and Hui Fei, sending everyone else away.

She calmly adjusted her hair, then said to Nurse Yu, “It’s a pity she had to make two trips.”

Leaning back, she took a sip of hot tea and said indifferently, “Tell her to go back. Say that I am not available to see anyone.”

Nurse Yu hesitated, looking at Song Helan. “Perhaps Concubine Xie has come to pledge her loyalty?”

Song Helan coldly laughed. “She wants to pledge loyalty to plot against Xi Rongyan. It’s best not to have any dealings with her now, lest we get implicated.”

“His Majesty is not a fool. If something truly happens to Xi Rongyan, won’t His Majesty suspect me?”

With that, Song Helan glanced at Nurse Yu again. “Arrange for a few palace maids from Huayang Palace to make things difficult for her. Spread some divisive words. I’d like to see what she’s capable of.”

---

chapters.title: Desiring Her
chapters.content:
Outside the hall, Xie Yumian heard the palace maid’s reply that the Empress was not available to see her and was slightly stunned.

She had thought the Empress was the one who least wanted Xi Rongyan to gain favor.

Last time, the Empress had even asked her many questions about Xi Rongyan’s past. Now she refused to see her—did that mean she was unwilling to help?

Xie Yumian tightly clenched the handkerchief in her hand, bit her lip, turned, and left.

When she returned to Huayang Palace, Tan Pinfei, who had just come from Huang Guifei’s place, saw her and sneered, arms crossed: “Have you gone to Hanyuan Hall to share sisterly affection again?”

“Did they let you see His Majesty?”

“Even though Noble Consort Zhen is now a full concubine, you’re still just a mere concubine. How come Noble Consort Zhen is so favored, yet His Majesty hasn’t promoted your rank?”

Tan Pinfei clucked her tongue, arms still crossed. “I thought betraying Qi Fei would bring you some benefits, but in the end, His Majesty still didn’t let you go to Guanju Palace. Yet you still have the nerve to fawn over him.”

These words were like a knife stabbing into Xie Yumian’s heart.

Her entire body trembled with anger, her palm nearly bleeding from clenching, but she only coldly glanced at Tan Pinfei and sneered: “You’re so eager to please Her Majesty the Empress. Has His Majesty even noticed you?”

“Are you any better than me?”

After saying this, Xie Yumian coldly watched Tan Pinfei’s face change color for a moment before finally feeling a slight release. She then tightened her lips and entered the hall with a stern expression.

Looking at the clearly perfunctory decorations in the room compared to Hanyuan Hall, a surge of nameless resentment suddenly welled up in her heart. She picked up a vase and smashed it to the ground.

The sound of shattering made her expression momentarily fierce.

Now, everyone in the rear palace treated her like a joke. What gave them the right to look down on her?

Tan Pinfei’s father was merely a minor frontier envoy, yet her rank was still above Xie Yumian’s, and she dared to mock her.

Suddenly, the words High Eunuch Gao had said that day flashed through her mind.

Her turbulent emotions gradually calmed. She sat in the armchair, listening to the rain, deep in thought.

Over the next ten or so days, Xie Yumian spent almost every morning in Hanyuan Hall, chatting with Xi Rongyan.

Time and again, she would bring up past events. The more Yu Zhu listened, the more uneasy she felt.

If this continued, what if word got out?

That night, as she wrung out the damp strands of Xi Rongyan’s hair, she couldn’t help but softly advise: “Perhaps Mistress should have less contact with Mistress Xie from now on.”

“Mistress Xie always brings up the past. What’s the use of dwelling on those things?”

Xi Rongyan sat on the noble concubine’s couch, having just bathed and dressed in a white inner robe, with a pink thin blanket draped over her shoulders. A charcoal brazier was placed beside her, casting a soft, warm glow over her. She held a hand warmer in her hands and looked down at the birdcage in front of her.

The mist from the tea beside her curled up, brushing against Xi Rongyan’s cheeks. The warmth in the room made her entire body relax.

Her fingertips rested on the golden birdcage, watching the parrot inside hop up and down on its little swing. She propped her chin up, staring absentmindedly, as if she hadn’t heard Yu Zhu’s words.

Seeing that Xi Rongyan wasn’t responding, Yu Zhu grew more anxious. She bent down beside Xi Rongyan and softly said, “His Majesty hasn’t come much these past few days. What if His Majesty hears Mistress Xie’s words and thinks that Mistress still has someone else in her heart?”

“The past is the past. Why does Mistress Xie keep bringing it up, as if she’s afraid Mistress will forget?”

In truth, Yu Zhu had also mustered her courage to say this.

She knew that the Xie and Xi families had always been on good terms, and Mistress Xie was Madame’s own niece. She shouldn’t have said such things.

But these days, listening to it all had truly been difficult. Back then, when the Gu family had fallen, how heartbroken her mistress had been. Mistress Xie knew that too, and had even come to keep her company for two days. So why did she keep bringing it up now?

Xi Rongyan understood Yu Zhu’s meaning.

She also knew that her cousin’s relationship with her was no longer as it once was.

There were still people in the palace spreading rumors to drive a wedge between them. She had told her cousin many times that those words were deliberate provocations, but it seemed her cousin had still believed some of them.

Deep in her heart, she did not want the once-close relationship with her cousin to turn into strangers.

So whenever her cousin came these days, she would have all the palace maids withdraw, fearing that others might hear their conversation.

She softly said, “Yu Zhu, don’t worry. I know what I’m doing.”

Yu Zhu softly pressed, “A few days ago, after His Majesty went to Her Majesty the Empress, he hasn’t come much these past few days. Is it because His Majesty, for the sake of the Eldest Prince, will often go to Her Majesty’s place now?”

Xi Rongyan turned her head and saw Yu Zhu’s worried expression, which made her smile. “His Majesty can’t always come to my place.”

Yu Zhu worried, “If His Majesty doesn’t come, doesn’t Mistress feel upset?”

Xi Rongyan thought for a moment, then seriously shook her head. “Yu Zhu, I’m not upset.”

“From the day I entered the palace, I knew that there would be many people in His Majesty’s harem—there is the Empress, there are concubines, and in the future, there may be even more. I am just one of many in the harem.”

“I also understand that His Majesty treats me extremely well, but I only need to do my duty and try to hold onto what I can.”

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan used a peacock feather to tease the parrot in the cage, her voice very soft: “I also know that my current situation isn’t very good. Her Majesty the Empress probably wants to deal with me and fears that I will give birth to a prince, joining forces with the Grand Dowager Empress to compete with the Eldest Prince for the position of Crown Prince.”

“If she targets me, I won’t just sit and wait for death.”

Yu Zhu was stunned for a moment.

She looked down at her quietly seated mistress, the single jade hairpin in her dark hair thin yet radiant.

In her heart, the young lady had always been gentle and slow to anger. The eldest young master and her father had always carefully protected her since she was little, so she had never seen any of the scheming and infighting.

She had originally thought that her mistress didn’t understand the intentions of the people in the palace and had no guard against them. But now, hearing her mistress speak so seriously, she suddenly felt at ease.

At least her mistress knew to be cautious.

At this moment, a voice from outside announced that His Majesty had arrived.

Xi Rongyan heard the voice and was slightly stunned, standing up with the hand warmer in her hands.

His Majesty had not come for three or four days. The sky was already getting late, and by the usual time, Xi Rongyan would have already gone to bed.

Today, after bathing and washing her hair, her hair had taken a little longer to dry, which was why she hadn’t gone to bed yet, but it was almost dry now.

She gathered the blanket around her and walked to the outer hall, only to see His Majesty striding toward her. As soon as he was close, he reached out and pulled her into his arms, walking into the hall.

His Majesty still carried the chill of the night, and his dark clothes pressed against her skin, making her feel slightly cold.

Wei Qi noticed this too. He glanced at the charcoal brazier in the hall, then at Xi Rongyan’s slightly damp, loose hair. Holding her, he sat down by the brazier.

It was indeed cold as the Qingming Festival approached.

He placed his hand over the brazier to warm it before pressing the person in his arms closer. Then he looked down at her holding a gilded bronze peony hand warmer, her fair fingers resting on it. The tips of her nails reflected a warm golden glow, making them strikingly beautiful.

These past few days, he had been a little busy. Knowing that Xi Rongyan went to bed early, he had not come to disturb her sleep.

Tonight, he was a bit late, but even if he could only catch a glimpse of her sleeping, it would relieve his fatigue.

Wei Qi’s fingers unconsciously began to massage Xi Rongyan’s palm, his gaze fixed on her lowered lashes.

Her long lashes fluttered like fans, and her lips were the color of rouge like begonia petals. The pink embroidered blanket over her shoulders featured lifelike cranes, and the hidden patterns on her white inner robe shimmered with the light, everything about her was perfectly gentle and beautiful, like a painting.

He closed his eyes, bending down to inhale the faint fragrance at her neck, his fingers tightening involuntarily.

He desired her.

His body could not suppress the urge to pull the person in his arms into his very being.

Wei Qi could no longer restrain the desire he had suppressed for so long. He stared at those red lips for a long time, his throat rolling, before finally giving in to his waist.

chapters.title: Tired of My Nagging?
chapters.content:
The air around her was filled with the Emperor's scent.

Xi Rongyan could sense that the Emperor was approaching her.

Instinctively, she tried to retreat, but there was nowhere to hide in the Emperor's embrace. She could only lower her head and bury it in his chest.

Wei Qi watched the corner of her ear, flushed red, peeking out from his embrace, and finally restrained himself.

He gently touched her loose hair, which was almost dry, then gathered it tightly and asked, "Shall we sleep now?"

Xi Rongyan pinched the Emperor's sleeve and nodded.

Wei Qi carried her to the bed, then naturally bent down to lift her foot and remove her embroidered shoes.

Xi Rongyan sat on the edge of the bed, shyly tucking her toes inward. Watching the Emperor bow before her, her heart felt a warmth, and she softly said, "This concubine will do it herself."

Wei Qi smiled, and from the corner of his eye, he saw Xi Rongyan's slightly reddened cheeks. He still leisurely removed her embroidered shoes.

At that moment, a silent warmth seemed to fill the air. Xi Rongyan stared at the Emperor's profile, her heart beating faster.

In a daze, she was soon pulled into a warm embrace, held tightly against the Emperor's chest. Drowsy and comfortable, she felt an unusual sense of security.

Wei Qi looked at the person in his arms, half-asleep, seemingly very tired, and thought that tonight would probably not work out again.

He gently patted her back, coaxing her to sleep.

Actually, as long as she had him in her heart, even if they didn't have that kind of intimacy, Wei Qi felt he could endure it.

As long as her heart completely belonged to him, everything would fall into place. He didn't want to be as impatient as he was in his previous life, doing many things that hurt her.

Xi Rongyan quickly fell asleep in his arms, her shallow breaths brushing against his neck, exceptionally peaceful.

Wei Qi quietly watched the sleeping person in his arms, his hand resting on Xi Rongyan's soft belly. His expression was profound. Although he didn't want to force her to take medicine, he still hoped she would conceive soon.

He had heard that Xi Rongyan's first child with Gu Yunyu had taken two years to conceive.

It had taken him and Xi Rongyan nearly half a year.

It seemed her body wasn't easily prone to pregnancy. Now that he was also restraining himself, and they could only be intimate occasionally, he couldn't help but worry.

Even though she was already his, he still worried.

He wished she would use the bracelet given by the Empress Dowager, so he would have an excuse to be bold.

The next morning, as soon as Xi Rongyan opened her eyes, she saw the Emperor looking at her.

Her eyes still held some sleepiness, and in a daze, she lowered her head and nuzzled into the Emperor's chest.

Wei Qi couldn't help but smile, pinching her earlobe and kneading it. Then he said, "If you're bored during the day, go keep the Empress Dowager company."

As he spoke, he pinched her soft waist: "Tomorrow, I have to go to the imperial mausoleum and won't be in the palace. After the Qingming Festival, I'll spend more time with you."

Xi Rongyan buried her head and hummed in response. Wei Qi didn't know if she had really heard him.

He then pinched her chin to make her look up. Seeing her lazily squinting eyes, he smiled, pinching her soft and tender cheek: "I heard you haven't been eating your almond paste lately."

"Weren't you fond of it before? Why don't you like it anymore?"

Xi Rongyan widened her eyes in surprise, not expecting the Emperor to know even this.

She used to like it, but she couldn't stand the Emperor sending it every day.

She hesitated, "I just don't have much of an appetite."

Wei Qi nodded, "I'll have the imperial physician come see you later and prescribe something to stimulate your appetite."

As he spoke, Wei Qi looked down at her, "Rongyan, eat more. You're a bit too thin."

Xi Rongyan was taken aback. She didn't think she was thin; in fact, she had a slight belly when sitting.

Her mother often said she ate too many milk cakes and had gained weight, telling her to eat less.

But if the Emperor thought so, perhaps she was indeed a bit thin in his eyes. She obediently nodded.

Xi Rongyan was as docile as a cat, soft and lazy. Wei Qi couldn't help but like her more. He held her close, letting her lie in his embrace, looking at her clear, bright eyes, and affectionately caressed her face.

He didn't want to let her go for even a moment.

Wei Qi continued, "These days, the spring cold is severe. In the afternoon, go to Chonghua Palace to bathe and warm up. The palace attendants there are at your disposal. Apart from me, no one else will go there."

Her long hair fell on the Emperor's chest. Xi Rongyan played with a strand, her gaze lifting to meet the Emperor's eyes watching her.

It made her face heat up, and she softly hummed in response.

Wei Qi was somewhat dissatisfied. He cupped her face and asked, "I've said so much, why don't you say a word to me?"

Xi Rongyan was momentarily confused; she truly didn't know what to say.

After thinking for a long time, and considering that the Emperor couldn't delay his morning court, she finally said, "This concubine will help the Emperor dress."

Wei Qi raised an eyebrow, "Tired of my nagging?"

Xi Rongyan quickly shook her head, "This concubine didn't mean that."

Wei Qi smiled, lifted his head, and kissed her chin before sitting up by himself.

Wei Qi had Xi Rongyan lie down and sleep a little longer, then left alone.

Xi Rongyan hadn't actually helped the Emperor dress many times. At first, she had been nervous, but later she realized the Emperor truly didn't need her help, and she felt at ease.

The imperial physician arrived in the morning, quickly took Xi Rongyan's pulse, and prescribed medicine. It wasn't some bitter concoction but a medicinal tea for nourishing the stomach, which was acceptable.

On the second day after Qingming, after the concubines finished the court sacrifices, they had two days off.

The Empress, as usual, prepared for the suburban sacrifice and followed the Emperor to the Lushan Hunting Palace to stay for some days.

This time, the concubines who followed were all of the fifth rank and above. Xie Yumian did not qualify.

As they left, Xie Yumian suddenly spoke to Xi Rongyan, "Can you ask the Emperor to let me go with you, sister?"

"I've been in the palace for two years and have never accompanied the Emperor on a trip. Besides, if you leave, I'll be all alone and very lonely."

Xi Rongyan hesitated.

Last time, she had asked the Emperor to let her cousin come, but the Emperor had not agreed. If she asked again, what if the Emperor refused once more?

It would be another failed request.

She looked at Xie Yumian with some difficulty, "What if we go together to ask Empress Dowager?"

Xie Yumian suddenly looked at Xi Rongyan and smiled, "Everyone knows that the Empress Dowager values rules the most. No matter who asks, it won't work."

"But if the Emperor decides, it would be different."

As she spoke, she squeezed Xi Rongyan's hand, looking despondent, "But if you don't want to go to the Emperor, it's fine. It doesn't matter whether I go or not."

"It was just a passing thought. If it troubles you, forget it."

"I'm just an unfavored concubine. It doesn't matter whether I go or not."

Xi Rongyan silently watched the smile on Xie Yumian's face. Although she was smiling, it was clear that the smile was not genuine.

The words of agreement that had reached her lips ultimately remained unsaid.

She was afraid of making a promise she couldn't keep.

It would end up like last time.

The two walked back together. Xi Rongyan invited Xie Yumian to sit with her for a while, but Xie Yumian shook her head, saying she was tired and wanted to go back to rest.

Xi Rongyan watched Xie Yumian's retreating figure, wanting to say something but holding back, her hand raised in the air before finally pulling it back.

She didn't know when it had started, but she felt as if there was a barrier between her and her cousin. They were no longer as close as before.

Xi Rongyan stood still for a long time, hesitating and pacing, before finally heading towards the Xuanzheng Hall.

No matter what, she would ask for her cousin.

If it worked, perhaps they could forget the past incident. If it didn't, she hadn't promised her cousin, so it wouldn't count as a failure.

---

chapters.title: Don't You Miss Me?
chapters.content:
Wei Qi was in the hall receiving officials when Gao Yilai announced that Xi Rongyan was seeking an audience at Mingde Hall. He raised his eyebrows slightly in surprise.

He instructed Gao Yilai to have Xi Rongyan wait in the inner study and not to forget to send some of the snacks she liked.

When Wei Qi finished his business and went to the inner hall, he saw her sitting properly in a chair in the corner, her eyes not wandering, nor had she touched any of his things.

He had even let her wait inside the study, so why would he worry about her touching his things?

Wei Qi stood there, watching her. She had her head slightly lowered, her fingertips sliding absently on her round fan, as if lost in thought.

Wei Qi knew all of Xi Rongyan's behaviors like the back of his hand.

Including her worries.

She had always been kind-hearted, considering others in everything she did.

In his past life, he had seen her growing thinner and thinner. He had once threatened her: if she refused to eat properly, the palace attendants serving her wouldn't be allowed to eat either.

She would eat as much as the attendants did.

He still remembered her expression back then, the shocked look in her eyes as she stared at him.

She had stuffed food into her mouth bit by bit, only to vomit it out later, and then she had fallen seriously ill.

The imperial physician had said it was because she had eaten too quickly, overwhelming her body and causing the vomiting. She needed to take it slow.

In the end, that outcome had been caused by his own step-by-step pressure.

Wei Qi took a light step, silently approaching the daydreaming Xi Rongyan.

He bent down and lifted her chin, his thumb gently caressing her cheek. His dark eyes looked into her almond-shaped eyes as he softly asked, "What made you think of coming to see me now?"

Xi Rongyan only hesitated for a moment before looking at the Emperor's gentle eyes. She paused, then reached out and wrapped her arms around his waist, pressing her cheek against him. "This concubine just missed the Emperor."

Wei Qi raised an eyebrow, looking down at the person who had taken the initiative to hug him, silently taking a deep breath.

In his past life, getting her to hug him proactively had caused quite a commotion.

But now, even if she was willing to hug him, it was still for someone else's sake.

He gently stroked her black hair, his usually cold and detached brows now relaxed. With a gentle motion, he pulled her closer into his embrace.

No matter what, her taking the initiative like this was enough to satisfy him.

He pressed her back against his shoulder, his peripheral vision sweeping over the small table beside them. The fruits and pastries he had sent for her were untouched, as if she was deeply troubled.

Xi Rongyan used to love cherries. Nowadays, most of the cherries offered as tribute were sent to her, but it seemed she had grown tired of them.

His hand moved from Xi Rongyan's back to her waist. He spoke slowly, "If you miss me, stay here today. Tomorrow, we'll go to the hunting palace together in the same carriage."

Xi Rongyan lifted her head from the Emperor's chest and looked at his current expression. Although it was gentle, she couldn't discern any emotions of joy or anger.

In her heart, she was still somewhat uneasy, especially with the way the Emperor was looking at her. Though he said nothing, it was as if he saw right through her.

After some thought, she hardened her resolve and said, "This concubine has only been in the palace for a short time and is not familiar with the others. The only person I can talk to is my cousin."

She paused, looking at the Emperor expectantly, "Can we bring my cousin along this time?"

Wei Qi silently watched Xi Rongyan. He leaned back against the chair and rubbed her fingers, appearing to be deep in thought, looking somewhat serious.

The vivid golden dragon on his dark robe made Xi Rongyan feel, at that moment, the majesty of the Emperor who was always gentle before her.

The surroundings were quiet, with only the shadows of the attending eunuchs falling in the corner. Xi Rongyan's palms began to sweat with nervousness, wondering what she would say if the Emperor refused.

Wei Qi noticed Xi Rongyan's tension.

He let out a soft breath and looked at her, "Rongyan, I cannot make an exception for just one person."

Xi Rongyan had already anticipated this outcome, but her heart still sank slightly.

She was sensible enough not to ask again. She knew that many things were best left at that.

The Emperor was the Son of Heaven after all; she couldn't keep asking him to change his mind.

She silently looked up at the Emperor, "These past few days have been cold. This concubine has had some headaches. Can I not go?"

In truth, Xi Rongyan really didn't want to go. She had always been afraid of bumpy rides and preferred the quiet of the palace.

Wei Qi frowned and looked down, "Headaches?"

Xi Rongyan nodded, rubbing her brow with her hand, "It's an old ailment of mine. A cold wind gives me a headache. It's not a serious issue; resting will make it better."

Wei Qi subtly pursed his lips.

He had spent a lot of time getting to know her, but he had never known about this problem.

But looking at Xi Rongyan's downcast expression, she seemed genuinely unwell. He was worried and ordered a eunuch to call the imperial physician.

Xi Rongyan was startled and looked up, "It's nothing serious. There's no need to trouble the imperial physician."

Wei Qi looked at her softly, "I still want you to be checked."

"If you're unwell, we'll cancel this trip. I'll stay in the palace with you until you're better, and then we'll go to the hunting palace."

Xi Rongyan looked at the Emperor in astonishment.

She hadn't expected the Emperor to cancel his plans for her.

But the arrangements had already been made. If it were canceled because of her alone, she would feel guilty.

Her mind raced, unable to sort out her thoughts.

Soon, the imperial physician arrived to take Xi Rongyan's pulse. He said there was nothing seriously wrong with her and prescribed a couple of doses of medicine.

Xi Rongyan then voiced the thoughts in her heart, "This concubine's headache is not serious. I can stay in the palace alone and wait for the Emperor's return."

"And with my cousin here to keep me company, I won't be lonely."

Wei Qi pursed his lips and glanced at the nearby Physician Chen, "Can Consort Zhen go to the hunting palace?"

Physician Chen, hearing the Emperor's question and understanding Consort Zhen's implication that the Emperor might stay behind for her sake, quickly pondered and then bowed, "The hunting palace is only twenty li away. If she avoids the wind and takes her medicine on time, there should be no problem."

Wei Qi had the physician withdraw and then quietly watched Xi Rongyan.

He leisurely observed her, as if waiting to see what other excuses she could come up with.

Xi Rongyan was stunned, opening her mouth but rendered speechless by the Emperor's gaze.

It seemed any further reasoning on her part would be pale and powerless.

Her final struggle, "This concubine will stay in the palace. Can my cousin go in my place?"

Wei Qi remained silent, his eyes complex as he looked at her, then lowered them, not wanting to reveal his current emotions in front of her.

It was just that in her heart, she didn't really care about him.

That cousin, who wasn't truly sincere to her, was more important to her than he was.

Wei Qi was silent for a moment, then looked at Xi Rongyan and asked, "This trip to the hunting palace at Gan Mountain and Dongning Temple will last at least a month. Don't you miss me?"

chapters.title: The First Time Like This with Her
chapters.content:
The moment these words left his lips, Wei Qi instantly regretted asking.

He knew he would never get Xi Rongyan’s honest answer.

In her heart, perhaps he still couldn’t compare to that long-dead man.

Wei Qi didn’t want to hear Xi Rongyan’s reply. He bent down, resting his chin on her shoulder. In the shadowed depths of his eyes, unseen by anyone, emotions churned violently before he closed them, burying everything beneath.

He interlaced his fingers with hers, his voice low and deep: "Yan’er, if you don’t want to go, I’ll have them cancel the trip."

"In my heart, nothing is more important than you."

Though his words were gentle, a complex and resistant panic surged in Xi Rongyan’s heart at that moment.

Even though the Emperor was accommodating her to this extent—even canceling the suburban prayer ceremony for her—why did she feel as if it were another kind of irresistible command?

She disliked this from the bottom of her heart.

At this moment, the Emperor made her feel slightly uncomfortable.

But then she thought she might be overthinking. Perhaps deep down, she felt she wasn’t important enough for such treatment.

Even if she didn’t go, the Emperor wouldn’t say he would cancel the prayer ceremony.

The two conflicting emotions intertwined, and she knew she had no room to resist.

She also didn’t want to displease many people. Others had already made preparations; if she suddenly backed out, she didn’t want to endure their stares and the gossip behind her back.

She lowered her head, staring blankly at the Emperor’s fingers tightly gripping hers, then obediently agreed to go to the imperial palace.

Wei Qi felt the fingers in his grip lightly retreating—a subconscious gesture of resistance. His gaze darkened, and he pulled her hand firmly, then lifted his shoulder to look at the person in his embrace.

The woman sitting sideways in his arms slightly turned her face away. Even though her body was close to his, her shoulders were subtly angled outward.

He looked at the tassel hairpin in her hair, and it reminded him of the peach blossom hairpin beneath her pillow.

He deliberately avoided thinking about it, not because he didn’t care, but because he didn’t want to make things difficult for her.

But he had given her so many pieces of jewelry, yet he had never seen her wear any of them. So whose gift was the hairpin in her hair now? Another one from Gu Ruoyu?

She kept a dead man’s hairpin under her pillow—did she intend to lock her heart away with that dead man forever?

Yes.

Hadn’t she done exactly that in her past life?

Even if he had another lifetime, he would still be a step too late.

Even if she didn’t see him for a month, she wouldn’t mind at all.

Suddenly, he scooped up the person in his arms and carried her toward the soft couch in the inner chamber.

With a clatter, the round fan in his hand fell to the floor. Xi Rongyan startled, and when she came back to her senses, she was met with the Emperor’s calm, expressionless face, yet it seemed to carry a silent, hidden darkness.

Her vision blurred past the dragon-carved golden pillars, the sheer curtains, and finally settled on a room filled with books.

Then, the Emperor set her down on a soft couch.

Before she could push herself up, the Emperor’s broad chest pressed down on her.

The dark chest cast a heavy shadow over her, while the bright light fell on her eyes, filling her with a secret, suppressed shame.

One of her hands was still half-propped up, while the other pressed against the Emperor’s chest. She looked into his dark, ink-like eyes, which had erased all traces of his former gentleness. For the first time, she understood why others found the Emperor’s presence overwhelming.

At this moment, the Emperor was noble and imposing. Though his face showed no emotion, it still made people feel an involuntary shiver.

She looked into the Emperor’s impassive eyes and instinctively trembled, whispering, "Your Majesty..."

But the rest of her words were swallowed before they could leave her throat. The shadow above her descended, her lips were quickly parted, and she felt a hand roaming over her body, gripping her waist tightly.

Her mind went blank.

This was the first time the Emperor had ever been like this with her.

Even though she knew what might happen, it was still broad daylight, right here on this small couch, with several eunuchs standing outside. She couldn’t help but resist slightly.

Moreover, the Emperor had always been considerate and gentle in the past, carefully asking for her consent. Though they had shared a bed many nights, they had only been truly intimate a few times.

She was still inexperienced, and this side of the Emperor made her a little afraid.

At this moment, Wei Qi no longer wanted to suppress his desire for her. Even though he had been patient, taking things step by step, he had never left a mark on her heart.

This precious body—ever since she entered the palace, he had cherished and protected it. Even in their most intimate moments, he couldn’t bear to leave too many marks on her.

He paid attention to every expression, every emotion of hers, refusing to make things difficult for her as he had in his past life.

Even when they were intimate, he would rather endure his own discomfort than use any force.

Even when he saw the hairpin under her pillow, he couldn’t bring himself to blame her.

Night after night, he held the body he had longed for day and night, yet he couldn’t bear to touch her, fearing he might see a flicker of evasion or a frown on her face.

Wei Qi didn’t want to look at Xi Rongyan’s expression now. He only glanced at her from the corner of his eye, seeing her turning her face away in discomfort, biting her lip, her silver earrings swaying gracefully, her long lashes trembling slightly.

He pressed his lips together. Even though his body was already clamoring out of control, he still restrained all his emotions, gently kissing down from her neck.

This time, he didn’t ask for her consent. He quickly pressed his body down, kissing her lips and tongue, untying her belt.

This was no longer the past life. She was his rightful woman now.

He no longer had to worry that she would hate him afterward, as she had in the past life.

The light grew brighter as the noon sun rose higher. Xi Rongyan’s voice had become hoarse.

She tightly clutched the open front of her robe, her misty, tear-filled eyes silently pleading.

Wei Qi took her hand, pressing it above her head as he interlaced his fingers with hers. Then he bent down, sealing her soft pleas with his lips.

Outside, Gao Yi paced in frustration.

This was the first time the Emperor had bestowed favor on a concubine in the morning, and in the Xuan Zheng Hall, no less.

The officials waiting outside could be dismissed, but the time for lunch had long passed. Should he call for it or not?

He listened carefully to the sounds inside. There had been quite a commotion earlier, but now it was silent. Just as he was about to go in and ask, he heard the Emperor’s low groan from within and quickly retreated.

It wasn’t over yet.

It was rare for the Emperor to be in such high spirits.

Previously, some had said the Emperor had no interest in such matters and urged him to show more favor to the harem to increase the imperial lineage. Well, this certainly looked like it.

chapters.title: Yan'er, It's All My Fault
chapters.content:
When Xi Rongyan finally woke up, she had no idea how the Emperor had taken her to the Mingde Hall. She opened her eyes to find herself lying on the Emperor’s bed, wearing a fresh set of undergarments.

The Emperor was sitting beside her, seemingly reviewing memorials.

Upon seeing her awake, the Emperor set down what he was doing, stood up, and sat by her side.

In the dim light, the Emperor’s face was lowered, his gaze upon her filled with tenderness.

Wei Qi reached out and took her hand, which rested outside the blanket, and said softly, "You fell asleep in my arms, so I carried you here."

As he spoke, he gave an order to the outside, then helped Xi Rongyan sit up.

At this moment, the sky had not yet fully darkened; the faintly setting sun gave the scene a muted glow. Xi Rongyan recalled the morning’s events, then looked at the Emperor, now properly dressed and gazing at her with warmth.

He seemed like a different person from the gloomy Emperor who had pressed down on her that morning.

Her body still ached slightly.

The Emperor had never treated her like this before.

She stared at his noble and magnificent face, lost in thought, then remembered the rumors that the Emperor was mercurial in his moods.

Seeing Xi Rongyan’s distraction, Wei Qi took a small bowl from beside him and fed her a spoonful of fish soup at her lips: "You fell asleep during lunch, and I couldn’t bear to wake you. Are you hungry now?"

In truth, waking up in the late afternoon, she didn’t feel particularly hungry. Instead, the soreness in her body made her uncomfortable.

A slight movement of her legs sent a wave of aching tension through her.

But the spoon was already at her lips, so she opened her mouth.

Then she looked at the Emperor: "This concubine can feed herself."

Wei Qi lowered his head, blew on the fish soup, and brought it back to her lips: "You were tired just now. Let me feed you."

Xi Rongyan silently stared at the spoon in front of her, then lowered her head.

For some reason, she didn’t want to look at the Emperor.

The only sound in the room was the clinking of the spoon against the porcelain bowl. The silence stretched on for a long time.

When Wei Qi had fed her enough, he used a warm towel to wipe her lips.

With his gaze lowered, his movements were meticulous, and Xi Rongyan felt a flicker of confusion at the Emperor’s care for her.

The Emperor truly treated her extremely well. Normally, he cared for her like an elder brother, always speaking in a gentle and soft voice, giving her the impression that the Emperor had an excellent temper.

But sometimes, the Emperor’s expression was profound and inscrutable, as if his temper wasn’t so good after all.

She couldn’t understand the Emperor, nor did she know what he truly felt for her.

It seemed the Emperor considered her in everything, yet he had never granted her requests.

Wei Qi glanced at Xi Rongyan, who was lost in thought again, and said softly, "Stay in the Mingde Hall tonight. Tomorrow, go with me."

"You still have a headache. There will be an imperial physician in the carriage behind us to take care of you."

Xi Rongyan knew she had to follow tomorrow. She paused for a moment, then nodded.

Wei Qi’s gaze fell on the mottled red marks on Xi Rongyan’s fair neck, which stood out starkly against her smooth, white skin.

He had failed to control his strength after all.

Now, seeing them, he felt a pang of guilt.

He looked at her and asked, "Does it hurt?"

Xi Rongyan, hearing the Emperor’s question, felt a genuine sense of grievance: "It hurts."

Wei Qi’s heart ached, and he pulled her into his embrace, gently stroking her loose hair, his voice filled with remorse: "It’s my fault. I won’t be like this next time."

Xi Rongyan, buried in the Emperor’s arms, muffled, "This concubine does not blame Your Majesty."

"It’s just... can Your Majesty not do this without warning next time?"

"This concubine was scared..."

Wei Qi was taken aback. Looking down, he saw her aggrieved expression. She was someone with a celestial beauty, and her distress made his heart soften.

In his past life, Xi Rongyan had shown weakness before him, humility, and brief submission, but she had never shown him grievance.

Only then did he realize that someone who appeared so gentle and obedient could also be so stubborn.

He suppressed his waist, and at that moment, his heart was filled with nothing but tender pity. The trace of resentment in his heart dissipated. He had no reason to blame her.

It was he who had forced himself upon her.

He lowered his forehead to hers, setting aside his imperial demeanor, and coaxed her softly: "It’s all my fault."

"It’s all my doing..."

"I won’t scare Yan’er again."

As he spoke, Wei Qi took Xi Rongyan’s fingers and placed them on his chest. His eyes met her misty, smoky gaze. Seeing the grievance in her eyes, he abandoned all pretense, hoping only that the person in his arms would feel better. He said tenderly, "If Yan’er blames me, you can even hit me to vent your anger."

Xi Rongyan’s hand, enveloped by his long fingers, was placed on the Emperor’s chest. She could feel the strong heartbeat beneath her fingertips. She was stunned, then looked up into the Emperor’s eyes, where she clearly saw his affection and guilt.

The Emperor, the Son of Heaven, actually felt such remorse toward her and was softly admitting his wrongdoing.

Her heart warmed slightly, and she tightened her grip.

Of course, she couldn’t actually hit him. She had only said that to make the Emperor stop scaring her like that.

She shook her head: "This concubine does not blame Your Majesty. Your Majesty has been extremely good to this concubine."

Wei Qi held her against his chest and took a deep breath: "I have not been good enough to you."

"I’m sorry, Yan’er."

"It will never happen again."

The soft, tender words echoed in the bedchamber, a tone Wei Qi had never used before.

He then called for someone to bring medicine, coaxing her to apply it.

Not only Gao Yi, but even the palace attendants waiting outside the curtains knew that the esteemed Consort Zhen was not just a temporary favorite.

Who knew what position she would hold in the future.

The next day, the accompanying consorts watched as the Emperor appeared, hand in hand with Xi Rongyan. Their eyes were filled with complex, inscrutable expressions.

To be able to stay in the Emperor’s bedchamber repeatedly and then be led by the Emperor himself—none of them had expected this.

Their gazes involuntarily shifted to the Empress.

Song Helan, however, maintained a dignified and proper smile, showing no trace of jealousy.

She approached the Emperor, her eyes only briefly flickering over the carefully concealed red marks on Xi Rongyan’s neck before discussing the arrangements for the harem consorts with the Emperor.

Xi Rongyan also knew she was no longer suitable to stay by the Emperor’s side. She tried to pull her hand free from the Emperor’s, intending to take her leave.

Wei Qi glanced at Xi Rongyan, hesitated briefly, then released her hand, allowing her to stand among the other consorts.

The grand procession set off toward the Xizhi Gate. Each consort shared a carriage, each with their designated place.

But Xi Rongyan alone had a carriage, positioned directly behind the Empress’s. It was also larger and more luxurious.

The Empress had arranged it this way, clearly acknowledging Consort Zhen’s current favor.

Others could only feel envious but dared not speak a word about it outside. Only after boarding their carriages did they whisper among themselves.

Xi Rongyan herself felt this arrangement was inappropriate. She didn’t want any special treatment, so she went to the Empress to request a different carriage.

Xi Rongyan knew she had no special status, and such an arrangement broke the rules.

Moreover, this trip included officials. With the Empress acting this way, what would others think? She didn’t want to invite criticism.

The Empress, however, glanced at her and smiled: "Consort Zhen worked hard attending to His Majesty last night. I arranged it this way in accordance with His Majesty’s wishes. Since His Majesty has not objected, it means he approves. You need not worry."

After saying this, the Empress boarded her carriage, seemingly unwilling to discuss it further.

She turned back to look at Xi Rongyan, still standing outside: "You should get in your carriage as well. Don’t delay the journey."

Xi Rongyan watched the Empress’s retreating figure, then looked at the line of carriages waiting, and had no choice but to board the carriage behind the Empress’s.

Qi Fei watched from inside her carriage as Xi Rongyan spoke with the Empress. She lowered the curtain and sneered at Li Fei beside her: "Look at how smug she is now. Who knows what she’ll be like when His Majesty grows tired of her."

Li Fei held her daughter in her arms. After hearing Qi Fei’s words, she simply said, "It has nothing to do with us."

Qi Fei frowned: "How can you say it has nothing to do with us?"

"Have you forgotten what happened to Song Ningyu?"

"The Empress is right. As long as Xi Rongyan is in the harem, our positions will never be secure. In the future, we’ll have to grovel before her. Are you willing to live like that?"

Li Fei understood the implication in Qi Fei’s words.

The child in her arms shook a rattle, making a light clinking sound. She said, "His Majesty currently favors her. What can we do about it?"

"She has the Dowager Empress protecting her. We can’t touch her."

Qi Fei let out another cold laugh, glancing at Li Fei with disdain: "You’re still so cowardly."

"No wonder the Empress says you’re useless. With such beauty, and even giving birth to a princess, you still haven’t captured His Majesty’s heart."

"How many times has His Majesty visited the Second Princess in the past two years? I fear he hasn’t even given her a proper look until now."

Li Fei was taken aback.

These words stung her heart slightly.

She was nothing more than a former handmaiden who had served the Empress, then been sent to the Emperor’s bed by the Empress while she was in her confinement.

Over the years, the Empress had found her useless for failing to secure the Emperor’s favor.

And the Emperor had never given her a second glance.

She still remembered that night clearly. The Emperor had returned from outside, cold and distant. She had trembled as she carried a cup of hot wine to serve him his dinner.

The wine had been laced with an aphrodisiac—not by her own will, but by the Empress’s order.

She had served the Empress closely and could see how cold and unapproachable the Emperor was. Getting close to him might have cost her life.

But she hadn’t dared to disobey the Empress’s command, so she had steeling herself to serve the Emperor.

That night, the Emperor had drunk the wine and quickly fallen under its influence.

The aphrodisiac was potent. She had taken off her clothes and approached him, already convinced that if the Emperor woke the next morning, she would be dead.

As expected, she had spent that night with the Emperor. When she woke the next morning, the Emperor was already gone.

She had been relieved to have survived. Later, she continued serving the Empress, and the Emperor was often at the military camp. Even when he returned, he never glanced at her.

She had never expected that a single night would result in a pregnancy.

Later, when the Emperor ascended the throne, the harem had been small. Now, her position as a consort was due to having borne a princess.

She had never harbored any intention of competing for favor. She understood all too well that, aside from having no backing, the Emperor’s visit to her that night had nothing to do with any affection for her.

The Emperor had never once looked at her daughter. She didn’t blame him; the Emperor simply didn’t favor the child. He had never taken a liking to her.

Now, she only wanted to guard her daughter and live quietly in a corner of the deep palace, with no desire to involve herself in those struggles. They had nothing to do with her.

Li Fei lowered her head and gently stroked her daughter’s soft cheek, then whispered, "I am indeed useless. The Emperor doesn’t visit Yuwan because Yuwan, like me, lacks the fortune to earn her father’s favor."

Qi Fei looked at Li Fei with cold disdain, her beautiful face marred by timidity. "You refuse to fight for yourself or your future, but what about your daughter?"

"Do you want others to look down on the Second Princess in the future?"

"Wait until the one in Hanyuan Hall has a child. The Emperor will have even less regard for the Second Princess. An unfavored princess with a useless, unfavored mother—who would want to marry her when she grows up?"

"You don’t even plan for yourself, but what about your child?"

Li Fei glanced at Qi Fei, then silently lowered her head without speaking.

She understood that the waters of the palace were murky.

She had chosen to live quietly in a corner for her child’s sake. What confidence did she have to compete with Consort Zhen for the Emperor’s favor?

Her family background was inferior, and moreover, Consort Zhen had the Dowager Empress behind her.

Besides, the Emperor had never wanted to look at her before, and it was the same now.

She was truly a person without talent. Her only skill was endurance and following orders, so her child wouldn’t be implicated.

She had seen clearly what happened with Qi Fei. The Emperor didn’t interfere in harem affairs, yet he had demoted Qi Fei and sent her to Yanqiu Palace on the very first day Consort Zhen entered the palace, bypassing the Empress. She was certain the Emperor truly cared for Consort Zhen.

She could never act against Consort Zhen.

But on the surface, she still feigned a weak and helpless demeanor: "Even if I’m unwilling, there’s nothing I can do. His Majesty doesn’t come to my place."

Qi Fei reached out to tease the child in Li Fei’s arms and sneered: "Surely that woman can’t remain in favor forever? You still have a child. For the child’s sake, His Majesty will have to pay you some attention."

"Doesn’t the Empress help you?"

"With your beauty, you’re not the least bit inferior to Consort Zhen. This trip to the mountain villa is also your chance. Take the Second Princess to see His Majesty more often. Maybe he’ll recall old feelings."

Li Fei held her child tightly and glanced at Qi Fei: "I’ll try."

The Lùshān Mountain Villa was only twenty li from the capital. They could arrive by dusk if they set off after a brief noon rest.

Xi Rongyan’s carriage was spacious and soft, with a small bed inside.

Her body still ached. It was her first time experiencing such intimacy, and although the Emperor’s movements yesterday had been gentle, the prolonged exertion had been too much for her. Now, her lower abdomen still felt uncomfortable. She lay on the small bed, letting Baozhu massage her waist while the carriage’s rocking motion lulled her into drowsiness.

Last night, she had dreamed of that man again. She hadn’t dreamed of him in a long time, but last night, she had.

In her dream, she was forced to sit in that man’s lap as he fed her bite by bite.

He kept asking her why she refused to eat, his deep voice hoarse and cold, like a ghostly whisper, exuding a sinister chill.

She still couldn’t see his face clearly, only catching glimpses of his dark, cold eyes in the dimness, bloodshot and twisted, terrifying.

chapters.title: The Pit in My Hand
chapters.content:
Xi Rongyan was jolted awake in the middle of the night by a nightmare. She stared at the dim bed curtains, unable to tell where she was for a moment.

She still felt as if those chilling eyes were watching her.

She dared not close her eyes—every time she did, she would relive that scene.

In her dream, her body curled in pain, vomiting up what she had eaten, yet the man’s actions could not be stopped.

She didn’t understand why she kept having such terrifying nightmares, as if she were truly there.

Even with the Emperor’s broad chest behind her and his arms tightly wrapped around her, she was still afraid.

After lying awake for half the night, she now felt drowsy again and began to yawn.

Yuzhu was still whispering beside her: "Today, Her Majesty the Empress arranged things this way. Though it seems magnanimous, it inevitably pushes you into the spotlight."

She sighed again: "My lady must be extra careful around Her Majesty. She is not as gentle as she appears."

Xi Rongyan closed her eyes and murmured, "I know that without you telling me."

Just then, the carriage suddenly stopped. Soon, Eunuch Gao’s voice came through the curtain: "Noble Consort Zhen, His Majesty has sent me to invite you over."

Xi Rongyan had been lazily lying down, wanting to sleep properly, and didn’t want to move at all.

But since Eunuch Gao had come to summon her, she had no choice but to respond.

Yuzhu lifted the curtain and politely said to Eunuch Gao outside: "Thank you for waiting, Eunuch Gao. My lady will be ready shortly."

Gao Yi chuckled outside: "Noble Consort Zhen, take your time. There’s no rush."

Yuzhu then lowered the curtain and helped Xi Rongyan tidy herself up.

Because she had been lying on the small bed, the peach-colored skirt was slightly wrinkled, the hair ornaments were a bit loose, and even half her face bore faint creases from the fabric.

Yuzhu quickly helped Xi Rongyan sit up and straighten herself. The heavy, intricate skirt took a while to smooth out. After fixing her hair as well, she supported Xi Rongyan as she stepped out of the carriage.

As Xi Rongyan followed Eunuch Gao toward the Emperor’s carriage, she noticed that the curtains of the passing carriages were all lifted, and the people inside were watching her.

Only the Empress’s carriage curtains remained closed.

When she arrived at the Emperor’s carriage at the front, Xi Rongyan lowered her head, lifted her skirt, and, with the help of the palace attendants, boarded the carriage.

Song Helan sat upright inside the carriage, listening to the sounds outside with an unreadable expression.

Beside her, Nurse Yu glanced at Xi Rongyan and said, "I never expected His Majesty to favor her so much."

"Isn’t it improper for His Majesty to ignore Her Majesty and summon Noble Consort Zhen instead?"

Song Helan gave a faint smile.

Yes, she hadn’t expected it either.

In such a public setting, with so many concubines and officials present, the Emperor had called Xi Rongyan over.

The Emperor didn’t care about others’ gossip, so if she brought it up, she would only humiliate herself.

Moreover, though this trip was for a suburban prayer ritual, it was also for the Emperor to stay briefly at Mount Lu to relax. Who would dare to criticize the Emperor’s actions at a time like this?

A man like the Emperor, if he truly favored someone, wouldn’t care what others said.

But in truth, even if the Emperor favored Xi Rongyan, she herself didn’t feel jealous. She hadn’t for a long time.

As long as Xi Rongyan didn’t have a child, it was fine.

Anyone could have a prince—except Xi Rongyan.

Song Helan lowered her gaze, her fingers lightly tracing the teacup lid.

Today, because of the outing, Xi Rongyan’s attire was slightly more formal. She wore a gilded crown in her hair, with a pair of cloud-shaped gold filigree gemstone hairpins on either side. Below her ears hung a pair of jadeite and coral crane earrings that nearly brushed her shoulders. Though heavy, they gave her the bearing of a favored concubine and made her already striking features even more radiant.

Though her appearance was gentle and refined, when she brightened up, she became even more captivating. A nearby eunuch stole a glance and thought to himself that it was no wonder Noble Consort Zhen was so favored. Among all the concubines in the palace, she was the only one with such beauty and demeanor.

Xi Rongyan, who was naturally low-key and disliked attention, had noticed the unfriendly gazes from the corners of her eyes as she passed by. She knew they were warnings—she had to be cautious in every step within the deep palace.

She also thought that if one day she fell out of favor, everyone would want to step on her.

Lost in thought, her drowsiness faded somewhat. She took a deep breath and entered the Emperor’s spacious carriage.

As soon as she stepped inside, before she could even greet him, her arm was pulled by a large hand, and she tumbled into a warm embrace. The phoenix hairpins on her head tinkled softly.

The carriage began to move. Wei Qi lowered his head, looking at the person in his arms, his gaze falling on her slightly tired eyes.

She had been restless in his arms since waking up in the middle of the night, clearly unable to sleep.

He didn’t know what she had dreamed of.

The earrings by her ears swayed gently with the carriage’s movement. Her misty eyes lifted slightly, her fingers still tightly clutching his robe, like a startled kitten that hadn’t yet come back to its senses.

He smiled, picked up a cherry, and fed it to her lips: "My carriage is more spacious. We won’t arrive until dusk. If you’re sleepy, just rest in my arms for a while."

Xi Rongyan opened her mouth and bit the cherry. Then, looking at the Emperor’s half-lit face, she suddenly felt a flicker of jealousy.

No matter how long the Emperor favored her, others would still resent her.

How could she, alone, deal with so many people?

She still resisted such thoughts deep down. She wasn’t someone who sought to climb higher, but she had to think for herself.

The Emperor seemed to genuinely like her now.

Torn, she stretched out her arm and wrapped it around the Emperor’s waist. She wanted to say something coquettish to please him, but hesitated, feeling too ashamed to speak. Instead, she just buried her face in his chest and nodded.

She thought that as long as the Emperor favored her, she would behave well. She would go as far as she could. As long as she didn’t make mistakes, she would consider other options if she ever fell out of favor in the future.

Wei Qi noticed that the person in his arms seemed unusually obedient. The arm around his waist made his breath catch. He lowered his head and looked deeply at her.

He extended his hand to her lips: "Just spit the pit into my hand."

Xi Rongyan glanced at the fingers in front of her, then bit the cherry pit and looked up. She saw the Emperor’s indulgent expression, just like the one her cousin Yu had worn when he used to hold out his hand for her to spit cherry pits into.
