Back then, she was only twelve. She had been sitting at a stone table, watching her cousin Yu and her eldest brother play chess, while greedily eating cherries. Before long, the small dish was filled with pits. When the maid went to fetch another dish, her cousin Yu had smiled and stretched out his hand, telling her to spit the pits into his palm.

The sunlight that day had been bright, and her eldest brother had smiled as he moved his chess pieces. Now, recalling it, it felt as if it hadn’t been that long ago.

Yuzhu had said that her cousin had brought up painful memories, but in truth, she hadn’t forgotten.

Instinctively, she tried to push the Emperor’s hand away, intending to sit up and spit the pit into a dish.

But the Emperor’s hand on her shoulder pressed down, preventing her from moving.

His deep voice fell by her ear, and that long hand was placed in front of her again, as if he would not accept refusal: "Rongyan, no need to get up."

Xi Rongyan hesitated, then obediently lowered her head. She spat out the clean pit from between her teeth, a glistening thread of saliva still clinging to it, and it landed right in the Emperor’s palm.

---

chapters.title: What Did Rongyan Dream About?
chapters.content:
Wei Qi looked at the small pit in his palm, his fingers on Xi Rongyan’s waist tightened slightly before he placed it in a dish.

He picked up another cherry and fed it to her: "Did you have a nightmare last night?"

Xi Rongyan bit the cherry and nodded vaguely.

Wei Qi raised an eyebrow, watching her hazy expression. Patiently, he took the pit she spat out and asked again, "What did Rongyan dream about?"

Xi Rongyan paused, recalling the nightmare that still sent chills down her spine.

After a moment of hesitation, she spoke: "In my dream, there was a terrifying man. I always dream of him."

Wei Qi’s gaze stilled. He leaned back, pressing Xi Rongyan’s body closer into his embrace.

He continued to feed her cherries leisurely and asked, "Who was that man in your dream?"

Xi Rongyan shook her head. "I couldn’t see his face clearly."

Wei Qi’s deep gaze lowered. His fingertip rested on Xi Rongyan’s full, moist lips, which exuded a faint cherry fragrance, blending with the subtle warmth of her body. He traced her lips and asked, "What did he do to you?"

Xi Rongyan replied, "He forced me to eat. I couldn’t eat anymore, but he kept feeding me. It was horrifying."

Wei Qi’s hand stilled.

He looked at Xi Rongyan’s face with a complex expression, then sat up straight, looking down at the person in his arms. "Why would Rongyan have such a dream?"

Xi Rongyan shook her head. "I don’t know."

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan buried her face in Wei Qi’s chest. "The way that man looked at me in the dream was so terrifying. I really don’t want to dream of him again."

Wei Qi pursed his lips and gently patted her back, soothing her in a low voice: "From now on, I will stay by your side. You don’t need to be afraid."

Xi Rongyan softly hummed in response, closing her eyes. But the sight of those eyes suddenly appeared before her again, startling her into opening them once more.

Wei Qi observed her silently, noticing her slightly pale face. He realized she was truly frightened.

He recalled a vaguely familiar scene from the past.

This was Xi Rongyan’s nightmare. But when she had experienced it firsthand, had she been just as terrified?

He tightened his lips, lowered his head, and held her even closer, murmuring softly, "No one can do that to you. Never again."

He spoke so softly that it was almost as if he were talking to himself.

By dusk, the carriage arrived at Lushan’s Dongning Temple. Xi Rongyan had slept in the Emperor’s arms the entire way.

When she awoke, the Emperor’s hand was still gently patting her back, as if he had held her like that the whole time.

Yet the Emperor showed no signs of fatigue. He still moved with composure, holding her hand as they disembarked. Before getting off, he even adjusted the slightly wrinkled hem of her skirt.

Dongning Temple at Mount Lu was an imperial palace garden. The previous emperor had often stayed here, and everything had already been arranged. The welcoming officials knelt in a dense row at the entrance.

The accompanying guards stood at the entrance, and now the torches were lit, illuminating everything brightly.

From beginning to end, Wei Qi held Xi Rongyan’s hand as they entered, heading toward the Yangxin Courtyard inside.

Yangxin Courtyard was situated between the temple and the scattered pavilions and towers by the stream. At the very back was a study surrounded by a lake.

Yangxin Courtyard was where the Emperor would stay, while the concubines’ quarters were all in the South Courtyard.

The Empress had already arranged everything, assigning each person to their respective rooms. Someone led them to their accommodations.

Since Xi Rongyan had been following the Emperor, she went directly to Yangxin Courtyard.

The Empress’s room was right next door, while the others all stayed together in the South Courtyard.

The Emperor seemed busy with something. He only told Xi Rongyan to bathe and go to sleep first, not to wait for him, before leaving.

Xi Rongyan was left standing alone in the room.

She glanced around. Fortunately, Baozhu and Yuzhu had followed her here, which put her at ease.

Yangxin Courtyard was vast. In front of the bedchamber was a lake, and behind the back door was a secluded garden, complete with a small bridge, flowing water, a library pavilion, a flat bridge, and a tower.

The night was deepening, and the scenery was indistinct. Only under the faint light of the lanterns in the corridor could one catch a glimpse of the surroundings.

A fresh floral and leafy fragrance wafted through the air, lifting her spirits.

A palace maid came to invite Xi Rongyan to bathe. She followed the maid through layers of screens and curtains into a bathhouse the size of a room.

The floor was paved with white jade tiles, and the bathtub in the center was large enough to fit three or four people.

It was filled with a layer of begonia petals. Two maids knelt on either side, one holding a towel, the other holding fragrant ointment.

Xi Rongyan noticed two more attending maids standing in the corner of the bathhouse. She felt extremely uncomfortable and ordered everyone to leave, keeping only Yuzhu and Baozhu.

Once she settled into the bath, the water was so plentiful and hot that it stayed warm for a long time.

She closed her eyes, feeling drowsy from the steam, and chatted idly with Baozhu.

Yuzhu noticed the red marks on Xi Rongyan’s body. The ones on her waist were still slightly bruised. She couldn’t help but say, "How did you end up with so many marks?"

She expressed her concern to Xi Rongyan: "My lady’s body can’t take this."

She hesitated: "Should we advise His Majesty to be more restrained?"

Xi Rongyan leaned on the edge of the bathtub, silent amid the swirling mist.

She knew in her heart that she and the Emperor had not been together many times.

Before, the Emperor had always been gentle, and after the first time, he had simply held her as she slept.

Only yesterday had been different—the Emperor had seemed like a different person. Only then did she realize that such things could last so long, and by the end, it had been unbearable.

She softly said, "Don’t worry. Yesterday..."

"Yesterday..."

"His Majesty must have had a nightmare."

This was the only explanation Xi Rongyan could think of. The Emperor had once mentioned he suffered from nightmares. She had seen how he behaved during them before—he truly seemed like a different person.

She figured that yesterday must have been the same.

Today, the Emperor had held her all day, taking meticulous and gentle care of her. He didn’t resemble the Emperor from yesterday, who had pressed his lips together and remained silent.

After her bath, Xi Rongyan changed into fresh clothes and lay on the bed, letting Baozhu dry her hair.

Perhaps because she had slept so much during the day, she wasn’t very sleepy now. She turned her head and noticed many bookshelves in the room, so she asked Yuzhu to find a miscellany she might enjoy.

Yuzhu searched for a long time but couldn’t find any. She returned to Xi Rongyan and said that the bookshelves were filled with military books, geographical records, and historical texts.

As she spoke, Yuzhu placed a copy of Junzhai Dushu Zhi in front of Xi Rongyan: "This slave only found one book that my lady might like."

Xi Rongyan flipped through it but found no interest. She tossed it aside and stopped reading.

She thought that a man as reserved and serious as the Emperor probably wouldn’t read those popular miscellanies, so she gave up on the idea.

Looking around the room, though everything was exquisitely arranged, it was also rigid and formal, with nothing particularly interesting.

Moreover, with palace maids present, she couldn’t speak freely as she could in her own room.

By the time her hair was almost dry, Xi Rongyan still couldn’t sleep. She asked Yuzhu for the time and learned it was nearly the Hai hour—very late.

The Emperor still hadn’t returned.

She propped up her head, watching the swaying palace lanterns, yawned, and eventually fell asleep without realizing it.

When Wei Qi returned, Xi Rongyan was half-asleep.

He glanced at the person on the bed but didn’t wake her. Instead, he removed his outer robe and went to bathe.

By the time he returned, she was almost fully asleep.

He sat on the edge of the bed and watched her for a long while. His hair was slightly damp. He had originally wanted to ask her to help dry his hair, but he decided against it.

His gaze then fell on the red marks beneath her slightly loosened collar. He reached for a medicinal ointment from the side and carefully applied it to her skin.

chapters.title: Isolation
chapters.content:
The next day, when Xi Rongyan woke up, the Emperor was already gone from her side.

She reached out, and the faint warmth lingering beside her told her that the Emperor had indeed slept next to her last night.

She sat up groggily, and the waiting maidservants immediately approached the bed to help her wash her hands and face, then fetched clothes for her to change into.

Yu Zhu came to help Xi Rongyan dress. Xi Rongyan asked softly, "How early did His Majesty leave?"

Yu Zhu whispered, "His Majesty got up at the Mao hour (5-7 AM). He is holding court in the front palace. Today is the day for prayers, so mistress should quickly dress in plain clothes and go to Her Majesty the Empress."

Xi Rongyan hurriedly dressed and rushed to the Empress's quarters.

Fortunately, she wasn't late, but everyone's eyes were on her. Though no one whispered, the atmosphere was still uncomfortable.

The Empress gathered everyone and gave a few instructions about the prayer ceremony before leading the imperial concubines to the temple.

Palace maids held incense, eunuchs and guards formed an honor guard on both sides, monks chanted blessings, and everyone performed the ritual of kneeling and kowtowing three times with nine bows each.

The Emperor and the concubines prayed in separate places. After finishing her morning prayers, Xi Rongyan followed the other concubines back to their assigned rooms and changed clothes again.

Since they had to fast for three days after the prayers, she still wore plain clothes, her hair secured with a silver hairpin.

The noon meal was light and simple, which suited her taste.

Though the room was simple, a few pale yellow winter jasmine branches stretched in through the window, and beyond them was a lush green view. A gentle breeze carried a freshness she never felt in the imperial palace.

It reminded her of the courtyard in her Xi residence, where many winter jasmine plants were also grown. The sight was familiar and comforting.

In the afternoon, Yu Zhu asked, "Mistress, why not go out for a walk? They say the scenery here is pleasant."

Xi Rongyan had actually been listening to the sounds outside.

The concubines below the rank of consort were housed in the same courtyard, each in their own room. She could faintly hear the voices outside—groups of women laughing and inviting each other out.

Naturally, no one invited her.

Though she wasn’t someone who enjoyed lively gatherings, she had once had close friends. No matter the occasion, there had always been someone to talk to.

She hesitated, thinking that since she wasn’t sleepy, a walk might be good.

She went to the garden and saw a few concubines standing in groups on a nearby waterside pavilion. Since they couldn’t freely leave the South Garden, Xi Rongyan watched from a distance for a long time before deciding not to join them. Instead, she walked alone toward the depths of the bamboo forest.

Unexpectedly, halfway there, she encountered a chubby little girl running toward her, bumping into her.

Xi Rongyan quickly bent down to pick up the little girl and soothe her. A flustered palace maid rushed over, bowing to Xi Rongyan while calling out to the child, "Second Princess!"

So this was the Second Princess.

Xi Rongyan had heard that the Emperor had another princess, but she had never seen her before. Now that she did, she could tell the child was well cared for—plump and adorable.

Li Fei, the princess's mother, caught up and saw Xi Rongyan holding her daughter, Yu Wan. Surprisingly, Yu Wan seemed to like Xi Rongyan, as she didn’t cry or fuss in her arms.

Li Fei forced a smile. "Wan’er is mischievous. Did she bump into you?"

Xi Rongyan quickly stood up with the child in her arms, shaking her head with a smile. "The Second Princess is very cute. It’s my fault for not watching where I was going."

As she spoke, Xi Rongyan tried to return the child. "Consort Li, please don’t blame me."

Li Fei smiled. She hadn’t interacted much with Xi Rongyan, but over the past month, she had observed her quietly. She could tell that Xi Rongyan was not a spoiled or arrogant person.

Now, seeing how gently she held her daughter and how humble and polite her words were, Li Fei felt a liking for her.

She reached out to take the child back, but the little girl tightly clung to Xi Rongyan’s clothes, refusing to let go. She even reached for the white jade and gemstone necklace around Xi Rongyan’s neck.

Xi Rongyan looked down and realized the Second Princess liked her necklace.

She smiled. "If the Second Princess likes it, I’ll give it to her."

Li Fei quickly said, "We can’t take such a precious thing from you."

She urged Yu Wan to let go, but the child only clung tighter, her voice soft and aggrieved as she said, "Wan’er likes it."

Xi Rongyan thought of her little nephew, who was just as adorable, and said, "If the Second Princess likes this chain, then it has found its rightful owner."

She called for Bao Zhu to remove the necklace and give it to the Second Princess.

Li Fei was about to accept, seeing that Xi Rongyan was sincere, but then she caught sight of the Empress looking their way from the distant pavilion. A cold sweat broke out on her back.

She quickly took Yu Wan from Xi Rongyan’s arms and said, "Wan’er doesn’t deserve such a precious gift from you."

With that, she left in a hurry with the child.

Xi Rongyan stood still, watching Li Fei’s retreating figure, then touched her neck where the necklace had been, as if she could still feel the child’s warmth.

She looked toward the distant pavilion, where the Empress stood with her back turned, surrounded by several concubines. Their laughter carried faintly on the wind, but here, it was cold and silent.

She withdrew her gaze, tucked her sleeves in, and walked on silently.

She vaguely understood why Li Fei had acted that way.

After walking for a short while, she heard faint voices ahead. She was about to turn back when she heard her own name.

Then a voice said, "You’re so foolish. Don’t you understand why no one in the palace wants to get close to her?"

"She has so many empty rooms in her Guan Ju Palace, yet she won’t even spare one for her own cousin. She’s so guarded against her cousin—do you think she’d care about you?"

"And look at how much the Emperor favors her. Didn’t you see how he held her hand when they got off the carriage yesterday? They say her cousin asked her to beg the Emperor to bring her along, but she wouldn’t even do that simple thing."

"You’d better be careful around her. She’s cunning and knows how to keep the Emperor’s heart."

Xi Rongyan paused.

Another voice said, "Lower your voice! What if she hears you and reports to the Emperor? Have you forgotten what happened to Virtuous Consort?"

"She has powerful backers. Who knows? She might not even respect Her Majesty the Empress."

Yu Zhu wanted to go and tell them to stop gossiping, but Xi Rongyan held her back, saying indifferently, "Their words don’t matter."

"Most of the people in the rear palace are from the Prince’s former residence, and they are the Empress’s people. There’s no need to argue with them."

"Let’s go."

Xi Rongyan truly didn’t mind. Even without these things, they would find other reasons to talk.

She stayed in her room until nightfall. When dinner was served, the Emperor sent someone to summon her. Only then did she get up, tidy herself slightly, and leave.

On the way, she encountered the Second Princess picking flowers again. Before Xi Rongyan could approach, Li Fei had already ordered someone to carry the Second Princess away quickly via another path.

Xi Rongyan paused, watching Li Fei’s retreating figure for a moment before continuing forward.

The Empress wanted everyone to distance themselves from her.

When she arrived at Yang Xin Yuan, the Emperor was already seated at the table waiting for her.

It was an open pavilion, with sheer curtains hanging on all sides. Glass lanterns were strung in a circle, casting a warm, hazy glow in the fading dusk.

Emperor Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan’s face, then patted the space beside him, signaling her to sit next to him.

---

chapters.title: It Wasn’t Her Fault, He Was Too Impatient
chapters.content:
As soon as Xi Rongyan sat down beside the Emperor, he began placing food into her bowl.

"Eat more."

Xi Rongyan picked up her chopsticks, looked at the Emperor, then at the dish in her bowl—bamboo shoot and meat, her favorite. She softly acknowledged with a hum and served the Emperor his favorite dish in return.

Wei Qi looked at his bowl, raised an eyebrow, and quietly studied Xi Rongyan for a moment. He noticed her calm, downcast expression. He knew a little about what had happened in the garden that day.

He hadn’t had time to accompany her today and knew that after returning from the garden, she had stayed in her room without going out.

He pondered.

After finishing the meal, Wei Qi took Xi Rongyan to his study. Standing in front of a bookshelf, he pulled out a book of miscellaneous notes and placed it in her hands. "Do you like it?"

The day before, he had noticed the book by her pillow and asked the eunuchs a few questions. Learning that Xi Rongyan hadn’t read much of it, he realized there weren’t many books here that interested her. So he had someone bring this one on horseback.

Xi Rongyan looked at the book in her hands, then at the Emperor. She hadn’t expected him to care about such small things. Touched, she said softly, "This subject likes it."

Wei Qi was relieved. He took Xi Rongyan’s hand and led her to a table where he handled government affairs, inviting her to sit beside him and read while he worked.

Two chairs were placed side by side, clearly not a matching set—one must have been brought over later.

Xi Rongyan sat down and flipped through the book, then couldn’t help but look up at the Emperor’s profile. His tightly pressed lips carried a hint of sternness, yet it did nothing to diminish his handsome features.

In front of her, milk cakes and almond tea had been specially prepared.

The Emperor spoke little, but every detail showed his thoughtful consideration.

She held the almond tea, gazing at his profile in a daze, then recalled the words she had overheard that afternoon and the distant looks she had received.

After a long while, she turned back to the book, read a few pages, and realized she couldn’t remember what she had read.

Wei Qi occasionally glanced at Xi Rongyan out of the corner of his eye. Seeing her quietly reading, he would look away.

Having her by his side, her soft warmth and fragrance close, brought him a peace that even calming incense couldn’t match.

Just knowing she was there filled him with quiet joy.

He wanted to express this happiness to her, but he didn’t know how to make her understand. All he wanted was for her to stay by his side at all times.

Wei Qi didn’t work for long. Looking at the sky, he asked, "Shall we go see the fish in the pond?"

Xi Rongyan saw it was already dark and hesitated. "Now?"

Wei Qi smiled. "Of course."

He stood up and took her hand. "This is a good time to go."

Xi Rongyan let the Emperor lead her to a waterside pavilion in the back garden of Yang Xin Yuan.

Palace lanterns lit their way as the Emperor led her across a corridor bridge to the pavilion. He scattered some fish food into the water, and soon a school of carp gathered.

Xi Rongyan leaned against the railing, looking into the water. She spotted a large, round red carp and couldn’t help but ask curiously, "How did it get so fat?"

Wei Qi chuckled. "Probably because it’s too greedy."

He then had someone bring a sky lantern. The orange glow illuminated his face, and the firelight reflected in his usually calm, dark eyes, making them shine.

Xi Rongyan looked into those eyes and saw her own reflection faintly.

She heard the Emperor ask, "Rongyan, do you have a wish?"

Xi Rongyan looked at the paper for the sky lantern, then at the Emperor as he placed a brush in her hand. "Rongyan can write down her wish."

Xi Rongyan took the brush, hesitated, and glanced at the Emperor. She asked softly, "Will Your Majesty read it?"

Wei Qi paused, then smiled. He took the paper and turned away.

Xi Rongyan dipped the brush and wrote a line carefully. She folded the paper and tied it before placing it in front of the Emperor.

Wei Qi glanced at the paper, then at the woman in front of him, who was tying the string with a focused expression. The bright firelight illuminated her face, casting an orange glow on her nose and chin. Her earnest movements carried a girlish innocence. At this moment, she was at her most beautiful.

And her most pure and transparent.

Though he often felt he could see through her, he was also the most helpless before her.

Xi Rongyan finished tying the string and looked at the Emperor. "Should this subject release it?"

Wei Qi placed the sky lantern in her hands.

Xi Rongyan looked at the pond and asked, "May this subject go to the edge of the pond to release it?"

Wei Qi gave a low hum of assent and watched as Xi Rongyan carefully carried the sky lantern to the pond’s edge.

The edge was slippery, and he felt a pang of concern, standing up instinctively. But then he saw the smile in her eyes under the lantern light and stopped.

He rarely saw Xi Rongyan smile. Even though he often paid attention to her moods, he seldom saw her happy.

His heart thumped, and as the sky lantern slowly rose, a calmness settled over him, as if he had captured a warm breeze in his hands.

Wei Qi walked slowly to Xi Rongyan’s side at the pond’s edge. She was still looking up at the sky lantern. He heard her soft voice: "When this subject was a child, she loved releasing sky lanterns. She wrote many wishes, and they always came true quickly."

"Later, this subject found out that it was my elder brother who secretly retrieved the sky lanterns and read my wishes."

"The sky lanterns float far away. Later, this subject stopped letting her elder brother retrieve them."

Wei Qi lowered his gaze and tucked a strand of hair, blown by the wind, behind her ear. He saw the red flush spreading at the corners of her eyes. His fingers brushed the moisture at the edge of her eyes before gently embracing her.

He figured she must be missing her family.

In his past life, after Xi Rongyan entered the palace, she often asked to see her mother. He had never allowed it, fearing she would long for the outside world even more, her heart never settling, unwilling to stay by his side peacefully.

He looked up at the sky lantern drifting farther away, silent.

His mind was still filled with the fleeting smile he had seen on Xi Rongyan’s face.

Her wish—what could it be?

The night breeze carried the gentleness of spring. Wei Qi, still worried she might be cold, draped his cloak over her shoulders, silently hoping it would warm her heart.

He tightened his grip on her fingers, sharing his warmth with her.

On the way back, Wei Qi heard Xi Rongyan’s quiet voice: "This subject has been staying in Your Majesty’s Yang Xin Yuan. Is that against the rules?"

Wei Qi looked at Xi Rongyan intently. During dinner, she had kept her head down, her thoughts evident.

His people had been watching her in secret. He knew they had shunned her.

But those women were unimportant. He couldn’t give her a promise now, but one day, the rear palace would belong to her alone.

She would stand by his side.

Their child would be the future crown prince.

And no one would ever be able to threaten the crown prince’s position.
